publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the penetration of electric vehicles (EVs), the coupling of power systems and transportation networks is a widely-studied topic in recent years. As the insight of the role of data in power systems becomes increasingly profound, the potential of electricity-related data value indices being used in analysis of transportation networks' characteristics should be realized. Based on the research on data value based on the electricity transactions, the electricity-related data value, which indicates the improvement of the electric load forecast accuracy caused by actual data, is introduced into the scenario of transportation in this paper. Considering the traffic flow data in transportation networks can imply the electricity loads of electric vehicle charging stations, electricity-related data value indices are defined based on the traffic assignment problem (TAP). Obviously, different traffic flow data will affect electric loads of different electric vehicle charging stations, thus the spatial distribution of electricity-related data value indices in transportation networks can be entirely depicted according to the results of electric load forecast through a neural network. Finally, the topological structure and actual traffic data of Jiading District, Shanghai, China obtained from Shanghai Electric Vehicle Public Data Collecting, Monitoring and Research Center are applied for practical case studies. The electricity-related data value is validated to conform to the theoretical analysis and parameter setting, and the spatial distribution of electricity-related data value indices in transportation networks may contribute to improve power system operation by using actual traffic data.

articleTitle: Optimal Reactive Power Model for Distribution Network Considering the Grid-Connected Characteristics of Photovoltaic
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the quantity of distributed generation (DG) nodes linked to the power grid rises, the influence of distributed photovoltaic generation (DPVG) on the power quality of the distribution power grid is progressively intensifying. This paper propose an optimal reactive power model for distribution network considering the grid-connected characteristics of DPVG. Firstly, the influence of the proportion, access s and location of DPVG on the voltage distribution of the distribution network are explored in the IEEE33 node distribution network. Then, a reactive power optimization model considering the uncertainty of PV output is proposed, with network loss and average voltage fluctuation as improvement objectives, and solved using the mutation particle swarm optimization (MPSO). Finally, the voltage distribution and power grid loss of each node are compared to validate the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Optimized Operation of a Two-Tier Game for Community-Based Integrated Energy Systems Considering Stepwise Carbon Trading and Integrated Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a multi-subject game co-optimization method considering the stepped carbon trading mechanism and integrated demand response strategy for the problem of conflicting interests of multiple subjects in community integrated energy system. In this paper, the particle swarm algorithm is improved while considering the stepped carbon trading mechanism on both the source and load sides and the integrated demand response on the load side. First, the community integrated energy system considering stepped carbon trading mechanism and integrated demand response is modeled. Second, a master-multiple-slave Stackelberg model is built with the integrated energy retailer(IER) as the leader and the integrated energy provider(IEP), user aggregator, and energy storage service operator(ESO) as the followers. Finally, an improved particle swarm method based on Gaussian perturbation and chaotic mapping with cplex solver is used to solve the model in this paper. The simulation results verify the effectiveness of the multi-subject collaborative optimization model proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Coordinated Dispatch of Flexible Resources and Thermal Generation Based on Variable Wind Power Consumption Region
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of renewable energy in recent years, the safety and dispatch of power systems have drawn a lot of attention. A method based on a combination of bi-level programming (BLP) and interval projection algorithm (IPA) is proposed to solve a coordinated dispatch model with an energy storage system (ESS) and pumped storage unit considering the impact of large-scale wind power uncertainty and volatility. Finally, the validity of the model is verified in modified IEEE-RTS 1979, and the influence of flexible resources on wind curtailment, load shedding, and operation cost is analyzed. Results demonstrate that flexible resources could facilitate the ability of renewable energy consumption and the model can strike a balance between the security and economy.

articleTitle: Equivalent Inertia Evaluation and Optimal Configuration of PMSG with Virtual Inertia Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This article conducts research on the equivalent inertia evaluation and optimal configuration of permanent magnet synchronous generator(PMSG) with virtual inertia control. Firstly, based on the dynamic structure of the phase-locked loop(PLL) and the transfer function of the control link of the grid-following PMSG, its equivalent inertia is derived; Secondly, based on the control principle and output characteristics of the grid-forming PMSG, expressions for its equivalent inertia and output active power are obtained, and then an capacity optimized configuration model for the grid-forming energy storage is constructed; Finally, the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed equivalent inertia evaluation and energy storage capacity optimization configuration method was verified through simulation on an improved 4-machine 2-zone system. The simulation results show that the proposed inertia estimation method can accurately quantify the equivalent inertia support effect of PMSG, and the proposed energy storage capacity configuration method can meet the needs of inertia response characteristics.

articleTitle: The Impact of Disruptive Technologies on the Evolution of New Power Systems Under the Double Carbon Targets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The goals of carbon peaking, carbon neutrality, and climate change mitigation have introduced new requirements for the development of our country's energy system. Transformation of the energy and power system is necessary, and disruptive technologies can play a significant role in facilitating a safe and low-carbon transition. This paper begins by analyzing the impact of the dual-carbon target on the development of disruptive technologies, drawing on the theory of techno-social system transformation. Subsequently, it examines the development process, characteristics, and future trends of pumped storage as a case study. Lastly, utilizing a multi-level analysis framework, it constructs a transformational development pathway for China's new power system. The analysis findings reveal that effective utilization of disruptive technologies is essential for the establishment of a new power system, while also emphasizing the need for improved coordination among the landscape, regime, and niche levels. At the landscape level, it is crucial to establish a national carbon emission budget system, set emissions budgets and decarbonization plans for the power sector, and develop industry-wide zero-carbon timelines. At the regime level, emphasis should be placed on building a new power market management mechanism and operational model that can adapt to high levels of renewable energy integration. Furthermore, at the niche level, accelerating research and development of new energy storage technologies and promoting the deep integration of energy and information technology are of utmost importance.

articleTitle: Adaptive Variable Step Size Photovoltaic MPPT Algorithm Based on Light Intensity Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To enhance the efficiency and stability of maximum power point tracking (MPPT) in photovoltaic (PV) power generation systems, and to address the issue of misjudgment in the traditional perturbation and observation method (P&O), an adaptive MPPT control approach based on light intensity prediction is proposed. Firstly, the correlation between the input and output of the system is analyzed to determine the necessary input terms. Secondly, the multi-time series LSTM algorithm is utilized to select pertinent historical PV sequence information according to the correlation analysis results, enabling short-term prediction of PV output. Finally, the Boost circuit is employed as the control object, with the light intensity prediction result serving as the input to adaptively adjust the step size of the P&O. Through the MATLAB/Simulink simulation platform, the results demonstrate that the adaptive variable step size photovoltaic MPPT algorithm based on light intensity prediction can effectively mitigate power oscillation in steady state while exhibiting good tracking speed and accuracy.

Author Keywords: multiple time series long short-term memory network

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling Model of Integrated Energy Systems Considering Wind Power Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Wind power stands as a preeminent form of new energy generation, facilitating the establishment of an integrated energy systems (IESs) characterized by cleanliness, low carbon footprint, safety, and efficiency. Nevertheless, the IESs encounter obstacles like voltage fluctuations, diminished inertia, an imbalance in supply and demand, arising from the inherent unpredictability linked to wind power. This paper proposes an optimal scheduling model of IESs considering wind power uncertainty. Firstly, the Error Back Propagation Algorithm (EBPA) is utilized to predict the data of wind power approach, and the analysis probes into the inherent error characteristics associated with wind power forecasting. Then the genetic particle swarm algorithm (GAPSO) is adopted to solve the objective function considering the wind power forecasting error with segmented and holistic perspectives in IESs, respectively. Finally, an interconnection simulation model has been devised to link wind power with the IESs, and the simulation results not only affirm the model's efficacy but also substantiate the accuracy of the investigation into the error characteristics associated with wind power.

articleTitle: Research on Evaluation System of Renewable Energy Transmission System Considering Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Large-scale integration of renewable energy sources introduces challenges such as volatility, strong randomness, and intermittency on the power supply side, posing a severe challenge to real-time system balance. Energy storage, with its advantages in mitigating the fluctuation of renewable energy generation, participating in system peak shaving and frequency regulation, and ensuring operational safety and stability, becomes essential. However, the research on the evaluation system of renewable energy delivery systems with energy storage is not sufficient, and there are few studies that comprehensively evaluate the system from multiple perspectives. Therefore, this paper reviews and summarizes the problems existing in the actual operation of large-scale renewable energy delivery projects. It selects several key indicators reflecting large-scale renewable energy delivery, establishes three categories of indicators covering safety operation, utilization, and comprehensive benefits evaluation. The paper proposes a comprehensive evaluation method for large-scale renewable energy delivery systems based on the critic method. Finally, through simulation on the improved IEEE 14-node system, it calculates various indicators for three different configurations of wind, solar, fire, and storage capacities. The weights of the indicators are also calculated to evaluate and compare the schemes, validating the rationality and objectivity of the proposed evaluation system.

articleTitle: Line Parameters Identification with Data-Mechanism-Combined Method Under Insufficient Measurement Condition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: There are situations in the distribution network, such as insufficient detection equipment and long-term operation. Especially, with the introduction of distributed power sources in recent years, there is an urgent need for a method for accurate identification of line parameters. This article proposes a distribution network parameter identification method that combines data-driven and mechanism. The algorithm only requires a small amount of voltage data. And the power data required by the algorithm can be partially pseudo measurement data Firstly, the problem of identifying distribution network parameters is summarized as a nonlinear optimization problem. And the parameter optimization range is reasonably defined based on the resistance and reactance parameters in the line ledger. Then, the measurable active power, reactive power and distribution network topology are used to calculate the node voltage value through the power flow equation. The deviation between the measurable node voltage and the calculated value is used as the objective function. The PSO (Particle Swarm Optimization) is carried out to obtain the calculated resistance and reactance values. Finally, by comparing result and values in the ledger, the ledger information is corrected. The partial topology data of a distribution network in a certain province is utilized to verify the accuracy and feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Primary and Secondary Collaborative Planning Method Based on New Power Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Large-scale new energy access poses great challenges to traditional power distribution systems. In order to realize the efficient utilization and safe access of new energy, this paper proposes a primary and secondary collaborative planning method based on the new distribution system, that is, a two-layer model framework of the primary grid structure of the distribution network and the collaborative planning of the distribution automation terminal. In the process of solving the optimal distribution network structure, the annualized investment cost and annual power outage loss cost of the distribution automation terminal under the network structure are converted into one of the components of its objective function, so as to improve the optimization results of the grid structure, and finally evaluate the effect of the collaborative planning scheme. The results show that this method can optimize the operation of the distribution network, reduce the power outage loss and planning cost of the distribution network, and improve the power supply reliability and power supply quality of the distribution network.

articleTitle: Secondary System Data Flow Planning and Design for Substations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To address the problem of data duplication and isolated data caused by the binding of substation-specific data to equipment and the independent construction of various systems, this article focuses on the interaction data flow between substation equipment. Based on the differences in real-time data, data structure, and processing performance indicators, the data transmission path is optimized. The existing multi-end duplicate data collection is divided into partitioned transmission. By using cross-zone real-time bus synchronization technology, the data of primary and secondary equipment as well as auxiliary equipment are shared comprehensively at the station control level, supporting the integration and optimization of substation secondary system functions and equipment. This achieves the integration of primary and auxiliary equipment for comprehensive monitoring.

articleTitle: Resilience Improvement of Active Distribution Network with Electric-Hydrogen Hybrid Energy Storage Microgrids under Ice Disaster
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to enhance the resilience of distribution network under the ice disaster and improve its power supply capacity, a resilience improvement strategy is proposed based on the long-and-short-term mixed timescale rolling optimization for the new distribution system structure of distribution network with multi-microgrids. When distribution line trips in ice disaster, the distributed energy resources and the hydrogen-electric hybrid energy storage resources contained in the multi-microgrids can be used to supply electric power to the off-grid nodes urgently. The method also considers the economic benefits of the microgrids and the principle of its energy autonomy priority. At first, the probabilities based on the physical model of line icing are considered, and the distributed hydrogen energy storage is actively dispatched in the long duration, to provide the hydrogen energy storage guidance for day-ahead optimization. Then, in the short-term (day-ahead) optimization, a two-stage robust optimization model is constructed, where the battery energy storage is used to cope with the short-term uncertainty of renewable energy and the change of network topology. The model is solved by an extended column and constraint generation algorithm based on second-order cone constraints. Finally, an improved IEEE standard 33-node distribution network is simulated to verify the effectiveness and economy of the resilience improvement strategy.

articleTitle: An Adaptive LVRT Control Strategy for DFIG Considering the Risk of Voltage and Frequency Drop
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In view of the problem that the large-scale access of new energy causes the decrease of the equivalent inertia of the power system, the virtual inertia control strategy arises at the historic moment, but the low voltage ride through (LVRT) control strategy applied to fault scenario has not been improved. When the grid fault occurs, due to the traditional low voltage ride through control strategy giving priority to output reactive power, the successful LVRT of large area wind turbines may lead to the transient low-frequency process of the system, and cannot give full play to the advantages of virtual inertia control. At present, there are few literatures that comprehensively analyze the voltage regulation and frequency regulation requirements during fault simultaneously. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes an adaptive low voltage ride through control scheme that considers voltage and frequency drop risk comprehensively for doubly fed induction Generator(DFIG) with virtual inertia control. Firstly, the lowest point of the system frequency is predicted quickly at the beginning of the fault, and the voltage and frequency reliability evaluation indexes are constructed. Based on this, the reference value of the rotor current is adjusted adaptively to realize the reasonable optimal allocation of wind turbine active power and reactive power during fault, so as to meet the differential demand of wind turbine active power and reactive power in the process of fault ride through and system frequency response. Finally, the simulation model of wind power-thermal power combined system is established in Matlab / Simulink to verify the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: An Integrated Day-Ahead Electricity Price Forecasting of Spot Market Based on Multi-Source Historical Information
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Reasonable electricity price prediction can help market participants get higher profits. Aiming at the problem of accuracy and reliability of day-ahead electricity price forecasting, an integrated prediction method based on multi-source historical information is proposed. Firstly, maximum information coefficient (MIC) is utilized to select the input series from the historical electricity price, load, photovoltaic, sea-wind and land-wind series, which improves the relevant information density between the input characteristics and the electricity price to be predicted. Then, the long short-term memory (LSTM) is trained in the offline stage to mine the high-dimensional complex mapping relationship between the input information and the output electricity price, and an efficient integrated framework is constructed to reduce the search time for the LSTM structure. Finally, the electricity price prediction series of the day-ahead market can be obtained by inputting the online data. The comprehensive case studies on the Guangdong province spot market show that the fusion of multi-source historical information effectively improves the accuracy of electricity price forecasting, and the performance of the proposed integrated model is not only better than shallow learning, but also shows the best prediction effect among various kinds of deep learning algorithms.

articleTitle: Hybrid Energy Storage Location and Capacity Planning Considering Frequency Safety
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The goal of the “dual carbon” has led to the rapid development of the new power system with renewable energy. A high proportion of renewable energy connected to the grid through power electronic conversion devices will have an impact on the frequency response and inertia support of the power grid, posing threats and challenges. As a flexible regulation resource, Energy storage can play an important role in frequency regulation. This paper proposes a hybrid energy storage planning method considering energy storage participation in frequency support. The dynamic frequency response process of the power system with energy storage is analyzed, and frequency safety constraints are given. The location and capacity of energy storage are planned with the goal of minimizing system operating costs and energy storage investment costs. The effectiveness of the proposed constraints and energy storage hybrid planning is verified by an improved IEEE 14-bus example, which shows that the proposed method can reasonably plan the location of energy storage, improve frequency safety during system operation, and promote the accommodation of renewable energy.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Effectiveness of Stability Indices for Various Stability Modes in New Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With increased renewable energy integration, determining system stability and dominant modes becomes crucial due to heightened uncertainty and complex dynamics. The uncertainty of system parameters, structure, and dynamic characteristics poses challenges for traditional model-based discrimination methods to effectively operate. With the emergence of numerous response-driven indices, this paper makes a horizontal comparison of the application scenarios and application effects of the existing common stability discrimination indices, and analyzes the tendencies of the dominant stability mode discrimination indicators in different scenarios. Also, linking some simulation results with theoretical analysis provides a feasible direction for further in-depth research.

articleTitle: An Electric Taxi Charging Guidance Approach for Transactive Energy Sharing with Energy Community
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the development of electric vehicles. an ever-increasing coupling of energy and mobility sectors is underway. Meanwhile, electric taxis (ETs), as the main participants in the traffic-grid coupling network, have not been effectively guided for their charging behavior. Thus, this paper introduces a novel E-taxi with charging guidance platform (ETCGP), which can guide the ET to the designated energy communities (ECs) for charging under the transactive energy framework. Firstly, with the fulfillment of the passenger traveling needs, a travel-charging order matching model of ETCGP using the matching degree matrix is proposed for charging guidance. Then, an EC-ETCGP cooperation model based on the Nash bargaining theory is constructed. To solve this problem, this model is decomposed into EC-ETCGP alliance benefit maximization sub-problem and payment bargaining sub-problem. The former one is solved with a centralized approach to obtain the optimal energy exchange between the EC and ETCGP, while the latter one applies an alternating direction method of multipliers method to determine the trading prices. Finally, the simulation results show that the benefits of both the EC and the ETCGP can be significantly increased by the proposed transactive energy sharing method.

articleTitle: Green Hydrogen Production and Consumption Method for Offshore Wind Power Based on Electric Hydrogen Coupling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the continuous promotion and implementation of China's new energy policies, new energy power generation bases have been continuously established. This article proposes an offshore wind power coupling method based on the concept of source network load storage, providing an initial framework for engineering construction of green power hydrogen production. In order to solve the problem of offshore wind power consumption, an energy storage operation mechanism has been introduced to solve the problem of wind power storage, and an energy flow path for offshore wind power consumption and production of green hydrogen has been proposed. Based on the hydrogen manufacturing process, key indices of the electric hydrogen coupling test dataset are proposed, and analytical conclusions are provided. It is pointed out that electric hydrogen coupling is an important fundamental form in the future energy transformation.Hydrogen energy storage can store both electricity and hydrogen and its derivatives (such as ammonia and methanol). Narrowly defined hydrogen energy storage is based on the power to (P2) conversion process, mainly including electrolytic cells, hydrogen storage tanks, and fuel cells.

articleTitle: Exploration of Standardized Market Trading Models for Industrial Adjustable Load Participation in Power Grid Service
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the large-scale integration of new energy sources such as wind and solar power into the grid, there is a growing demand for adjustable resources on the demand side of the system. By studying the production characteristics of industrial adjustable loads, the potential for these resources to provide grid services is explored. Taking into account the flexible load characteristics from the perspective of industrial users, a standardized market model for industrial adjustable loads participating in power grid services is constructed, providing users with opportunities for independent participation in market transactions. A simulation model was established using the AIMMS optimization simulation platform to verify the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed standardized market trading model.

articleTitle: Joint Rebalancing and Vehicle-to-Grid Coordination of EVs Through An Aggregative Game Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The cooperation of rebalancing and vehicle-to-grid services by electric vehicle (EV) drivers can help alleviate traffic congestion and provide flexible power resources. This paper introduces a game model where a fleet of EV drivers make both routing and discharging decisions to maximize their own utility. The utility of EV drivers is affected by various factors, including travel time, rebalancing utility and discharging utility. Moreover, their routing and discharging decisions are also constrained by the road capacity and charging station capacity. An aggregative game model is established to describe the non-cooperative behavior of EV drivers, where the utility of each driver is affected by the aggregate effect of others. To preserve the privacy of individual EV drivers, a semi-decentralized algorithm is employed to obtain the equilibrium point, i.e., the generalized aggregative equilibrium. Simulation experiments are conducted on the Nguyen Dupuis network and the IEEE 33-bus system. The result shows a considerable rebalancing effect, demonstrating the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Fuzzy PID-Based Temperature and Humidity Adaptive Air Conditioning Regulation System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In recent years, the proportion of electricity consumption in air conditioning systems (ACSs) has significantly increased. Unreasonable temperature settings of ACSs result in wasted energy and reduced user comfort. Therefore, it is necessary to design an intelligent temperature control system to ensure comfortable temperature and humidity while improving energy utilization efficiency. This paper proposes a fuzzy PID-based temperature and humidity adaptive ACS regulation system. Firstly, an indoor temperature and humidity collection module is designed to persist the environmental data collected by sensors into a database. Secondly, an ACS reservation module based on neural network prediction algorithm is designed to optimize the opening time and temperature of the ACS. Then, a temperature and humidity control module is designed to adjust the ACS conditions based on real-time measurement information. Finally, an ACS control module is built using the Internet of Things development board, which controls the ACS by driving the infrared transmitter. The actual case simulation proves that the proposed method has a significant regulatory effect, improving human comfort while reducing electrical energy waste.

articleTitle: Optimization Research on the Operation of Multi-Body Transaction of Step Carbon Emission Right Based on Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Responding to climate change and reducing greenhouse gas emissions have become a global consensus. The operation optimization of integrated energy system in the context of energy internet has been a hot research topic in the field. Aiming at the gap between the general effectiveness of the current integrated energy system and the goal of carbon reduction and efficiency, this study introduces the stepped carbon trading mechanism into the optimization model of the integrated energy system, takes carbon trading cost as one of the main objectives, achieves the maximum profitability and the lowest carbon emission while ensuring the effectiveness of the system, and gives priority to the environment over the reduction of the company's cost and profitability. The model is constructed based on blockchain technology, which can maximize the guarantee that the system data will not be tampered with or leaked. It can provide useful guidance for the operation and management of the integrated energy system and the optimization of the scheduling.

articleTitle: Small-Signal Modeling and Stability Mechanism Analysis of Grid-Connected Converter Based on PLL Synchronization-Dominated Loop
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Recently, the instability of renewable energy generation connected to weak AC grid has significantly impeded the large-scale integration and utilization of renewable energy. To elucidate the above stability mechanism, the component connection method (CCM) can be used to develop a multivariate complex frequency domain small-signal model of grid-connected converter. Subsequently, a small-signal control block diagram based on the synchronization-dominated loop is formulated by analyzing small-signal propagation paths. Then, a stability criterion is proposed based on the feedback control theory, delving into the stability mechanisms of different feedback loops, system operating points and grid conditions. It is demonstrated that as the output power increases or the grid strength diminishes, the local positive feedback loop comprising the q-axis current control loop and PLL through grid impedance predominates the overall control loop, which is the underlying cause of system instability. Finally, the accuracy of the stability analysis is verified by time-domain simulation.

articleTitle: Optimal Capacity of Wind Thermal Pumped-Storage Baling Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Wind and thermal power baling transmission is an important way for the consumption of renewable energy, and determining their capacity ratio has become a challenging problem. Pumped storage provides flexible regulation, which can mitigate the impact of uncertainty in renewable energy output. This paper first establishes a pumped storage power station model and proposes a two-layer capacity optimization model for the baling transmission system of wind, thermal, and storage. The upper layer aims to minimize the total system cost, while the lower layer targets the minimum cost of typical daily dispatch. The impact of uncertainty in renewable energy output on the system's reserve capacity is addressed using opportunity constraints. By employing sequence operations, the probabilistic opportunity constraints are converted into deterministic constraints, transforming the problem into a mixed-integer linear programming problem that is easier to solve. The case study results indicate that configuring energy storage can effectively reduce system costs. Simultaneously optimizing the capacity of wind, thermal, and storage power sources can reduce daily operating costs, thereby lowering total costs, validating the effectiveness of the model.

articleTitle: Transformer-Based Named Entity Recognition for Power Research with Dependency Relationship Information
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The process of research activities in the electric power field produces a large number of articles, patents, and other results, which contain a large amount of information. Named entity recognition is a common method for obtaining textual information, and this study establishes a model that can efficiently recognize named entities of electric power research results. Firstly, the keywords of electric power literature are obtained for preprocessing and organization, and then the annotated dataset of keyword named entities of electric power scientific research is constructed. After that, this paper enhances the ability of the model to obtain contextual information through the Transformer encoder and enriches the expression of textual information by obtaining textual semantic structure information through dependent syntactic analysis. Meanwhile, in order to strengthen the feature extraction ability, the BILSTM-Multi-Head-Attention-CRF model is used to obtain text context information. IDCNN model is also used to make this paper's model acquire the ability to extract text semantic structure information. Finally, ablation experiments are conducted to show that the model proposed in this paper has a better recognition effect compared with the named entity recognition methods in the generic domain.

articleTitle: Research on the Proportion of New Energy Included into Power System Balance Based on Statistical Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Incorporating new energy sources into the power system's reserve is of great significance for the safe operation of the power grid and the full utilization of new energy resources. However, practical issues such as the unpredictability and randomness of new energy sources constrain their reliability as reserve power sources. This paper analyzes and studies the theoretical and actual power output of wind, solar, and other new energy sources under historical scenarios, as well as the statistical characteristics of deviations in the predicted power output of new energy sources. This paper proposes a method for incorporating the day-ahead power forecasting of new energy sources into the power system's reserve planning. Additionally, this paper analyzes the deviations in new energy source predictions during peak load periods and determines the reasonable reserve capacity for new energy sources on a day- ahead basis, as well as the appropriate proportion for their integration into the power system on the daily basis. The research in this paper provides a reference for the power grid's capacity to accommodate new energy sources, overall power balance, and resource allocation.

articleTitle: Impact of Energy Storage on Effective Load Carrying Capability of Renewable Energy Based on Reliability Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Energy storage (ES) resources can play a role in peak-cutting and valley-filling., promoting the consumption of renewable energy and capacity support in the power system. The strategic integration of ES resources into the electricity market holds significant importance in maximizing the capacity value of these resources and ensuring the long-term reliable operation of the power system. Taking into account the physical characteristics of the multi-period coupling relationship of ES resources., this paper proposes a multi-period hybrid power system time-series production model with the participation of renewable energy sources (RESs) and ES. According to the stochastic optimization method based on scenario analysis., Latin hypercube sampling and K-means clustering are used to generate and reduce the predicted power output scenarios of RESs by known probability distribution functions., describing the probabilistic output characteristics of RESs through different scenarios. Based on the time-series production model., an effective capacity assessment model is proposed., applying the reliability-based Effective Load Carrying Capability (ELCC) method., which employs loss of load probability (LOLP) and expected energy not supplied (EENS) as reliability indices. Finally., the CPLEX solver is used in the YALMIP toolbox to solve the mixed integer linear programming (MILP) model in MATLAB., verifying the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Voltage Control Strategy of New Flexible Distribution Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The large-scale and heterogeneous loads with large capacity are continuously connected to the distribution network, and the traditional distribution transformers are no longer capable to satisfy the rapid and stepless requirements of voltage regulation of the existing distribution network. It shows that researching new distribution transformers and voltage control technologies has become an urgent need. Therefore, this paper proposes a new topology for distribution transformers and derives the equivalent circuit diagram of the topology. Based on the equivalent circuit, the working principle of voltage regulation of the transformer is analyzed in detail, and the accurate mathematical models for the internal converter as well as transformer are established. According to the mathematical models, the strategies for internal loop control, fixed DC voltage control and active voltage regulation control of converters are proposed. The simulation analyses are conducted by utilizing PSCAD/EMTDC software. The simulation results show that the proposed strategy can achieve the target of voltage regulation within 100 ms and the steady-state control deviation is about zero. The proposed strategy could be applied to practical distribution network engineering to solve voltage stability control problems during load disturbances and meet the fast and stepless requirements of voltage regulation.

articleTitle: Construction Necessity and Benefit Assessment of Virtual Power Plant: The Hubei Province Case
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The lack of research on provincial construction necessary of virtual power plants (VPPs) and corresponding benefit assessment has made it difficult for governmental departments to accurately predict and assess the benefits of VPPs in the whole electricity market. Policy diversity of VPPs exists in different provinces in China. The critical thinking of VPPs in different provinces shows that most VPPs are allowed to participate in the auxiliary service market. Hence the benefit of VPPs participation in peak-shaving market is analyzed based on the field data in Hubei province, as well as the benefit of VPPs participation in valley filling market. The results show that the total benefit of VPPs participation in the peak regulation market will be about 35 million yuan in Hubei province in 2023 year, and the total benefit reaches 105 million yuan in 2025 year. The significant economic efficiency proves the construction necessity of VPPs in Hubei province, and then the key measurements taken in Hubei province is also introduced in this paper to provide reference for VPPs construction in other provinces in the next few years.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Inertia Distribution in Power Systems Based on Regional Inertial Centers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Plenty of frequency measurement points are needed in traditional inertia evaluation methods to evaluate the inertia distribution in large systems. In this paper, an inertia evaluation method based on regional inertial center is proposed, which is able to obtain the inertia distribution and total inertia of the system by using the frequency measurement of each regional inertial center. Firstly, the cluster partitioning algorithm is used to divide the generator into different regions, and based on the linear relationship between node frequency and generator frequency, the nodes are divided to the most closely related generators. Secondly, the inertial center of each region is identified according to the electrical distance. Then, disturbances are applied to different regions, and the inertia of each region is estimated by measuring the frequency change of the inertial center of the region, based on which the total inertia of the system is obtained. Finally, it was verified in the two-area four-generator system that the proposed inertia evaluation method can achieve accurate estimation of inertia distribution with limited frequency sampling point.

articleTitle: A Review of Different Shared Energy Storage Models
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the context of the New Type Power System, energy storage (ES) has wide applications in generation, transmission, distribution, and utilization. However, its development still faces challenges such as high initial investment costs and low equipment utilization. Shared energy storage (SES), as a new paradigm to improve resource utilization efficiency and promote intensive development, provides a new solution to these problems. This paper analyzes the necessity of research and development in SES in the context of the New Type Power System. It categorizes and analyzes the application models and scenarios of SES. Furthermore, it provides an overview of the current research status of SES domestically and internationally, summarizes the research status in terms of business models, optimal configuration, and optimal scheduling, and analyzes the advantages and limitations of different SES transaction models. It also discusses engineering practices.

articleTitle: Mechanism-Aware Distribution Network Reconfiguration with Transient Voltage Stability Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To facilitate the construction of a clean, low-carbon, safe, and efficient power system, the penetration rate of dynamic load and renewable has been increasing, which has also severely reduced the inertia of the entire power system and highlighted the issue of transient voltage stability. However, because of the nonlinear and high-order characteristics of the load model, transient voltage stability is usually evaluated by a “black-box” model, i.e., through time-domain simulation, direct methods, or machine learning. Therefore, the transient voltage stability mechanism remains unclear due to the lack of mathematical analytics. This paper first investigates the impact of network topology on transient voltage stability, which is later applied as a guideline to topology optimization. Based on the genetic algorithm and the relationship between transient voltage stability and critical nodes, a transient voltage stability constrained model is established and solved. The effectiveness is validated through simulation on the modified IEEE benchmark.

articleTitle: Optimization of Time-of-Use Electricity Price of Electric Vehicles Charging Load Based on Spatial-temporal Distribution
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: According to the mobility of electric vehicles (EVs) charging load, it is important to have a reasonable pricing mechanism that can help EVs users adjust their charging plans. Additionally, charging EVs in different periods and regions can optimize the spatial and temporal distribution of EVs charging load. This study proposes an optimization strategy for EVs charging load based on spatial-temporal distribution and time-of-use pricing. To begin, we combine the travel chain and urban functional areas to simulate the mobility characteristics of EVs. By employing the Monte Carlo approach, we develop a probability distribution model of the charging behavior of EVs to determine the charging load curves in various functional areas. Next, we establish a charging demand elasticity model for EVs, taking into consideration the state of charge (SOC), to measure the relationship between EV charging demand and charging price. Furthermore, we study the relationship between the price elasticity of time-of-use pricing and EVs charging load, with the aim of coordinating the interests of the power grid and EVs users. We establish a time-of-use pricing guidance model for EVs charging and solve it using the particle swarm optimization algorithm. Finally, the results of our example demonstrate that the implementation of time-of-use electricity pricing can effectively guide EVs users in adjusting their charging plans, optimizing the spatial and temporal distribution of EVs charging load, and reducing the fluctuation of charging load and charging cost. These findings provide strong evidence for the effectiveness and guidance of our proposed model.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Community Battery Scheduling Under Uncertainties of Load, PV Generation, and Energy Prices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In response to the growing uptake of distributed energy resources (DERs), community batteries have emerged as a promising solution to support renewable energy integration, reduce peak load, and enhance grid reliability. This paper presents a deep reinforcement learning (RL) strategy, centered around the soft actor-critic (SAC) algorithm, to schedule a community battery system in the presence of uncertainties, such as solar photovoltaic (PV) generation, local demand, and real-time energy prices. We position the community battery to play a versatile role, in integrating local PV energy, reducing peak load, and exploiting energy price fluctuations for arbitrage, thereby minimizing the system cost. To improve exploration and convergence during RL training, we utilize the noisy network technique. This paper conducts a comparative study of different RL algorithms, including proximal policy optimization (PPO) and deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithms, to evaluate their effectiveness in the community battery scheduling problem. The results demonstrate the potential of RL in addressing community battery scheduling challenges and show that the SAC algorithm achieves the best performance compared to RL and optimization benchmarks.

articleTitle: Research on Coordinated Optimization of Transmission and Distribution Networks Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Coordination and optimization of the restoration process of the transmission and distribution grids during the frequent occurrence of extreme events leading to major power outages is essential to increase the speed and reduce the cost of restoration. However, transmission and distribution grids belong to different operators with limited interactive information. To achieve coordinated operation between the two during the load recovery stage, this paper proposes a coordinated recovery optimization method for transmission and distribution networks. The transmission and distribution network restoration operation model are constructed with the minimum restoration cost as the objective function, and the global transmission and distribution network restoration problem is decomposed into two types of sub-problems, namely, transmission network restoration and distribution network restoration, for coordinated optimization by using the analytical method of cascade of objectives (ATC) and reinforcement learning method (DDPG). The effectiveness, convergence, and computational efficiency of the proposed method are verified by taking the transmission and distribution system composed of IEEE30-node transmission grid and IEEE33-node distribution grid as an example.

articleTitle: Impact of Climate Change on China's Future Electricity Demand and Supply
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To study the impact of climate change on China's power supply and demand is of great significance for China to incorporate climate change factors into long-term power planning. In this paper, empirical formulas and theoretical calculations are used to quantify the impact of climate change on power supply and demand. Key factors such as the power generation efficiency of coal, nuclear, gas, geothermal and solar-thermal power generation, the availability of hydropower, onshore wind and photovoltaic power generation, and the intensity of heating and cooling are studied and analyzed. Subsequently, based on different global climate models in CMIP5 (CanESM2, HadGEM2 and MIROC) and RCPs emission scenarios, this paper calculated a multi-model ensemble. Then, this paper analyzed the change of China's power supply and demand under different climate change scenarios, and used the bottom-up energy system optimization model China-MORE to analyze the impact of climate change on electricity consumption, installed capacity, power generation structure and total cost. The study shows that precipitation, wind speed and downward shortwave surface radiation are the main climatic factors affecting the availability of hydropower, wind power and photovoltaic power generation. By the middle of this century, due to the impact of climate change, the increase in cooling demand in the residential sector will account for 40~60% of the total increase, the decrease in heating demand will account for 31~67% of the total decrease, and the increase in electricity consumption will account for 6~12% of the total increase; Compared with 2020, the power generation efficiency of nuclear power, coal power, solar thermal power, gas power and geothermal power in China decreased by 0.1~1.2%, hydropower availability rate decreased by 0.3~0.4%, wind power availability rate decreased by 0.3~0.5%, and the availability of photovoltaic power generation increased by 0.5~0.8%; Additional installed capacity to account for 2.8~4.9% of the total installed capacity, and additional power generation accounted for 2.2~4.8% of the total power generation. The cost increase caused by climate change alone will account for 1.8~4.9% of the total cost of the year. Climate change factors should be considered in future power sector planning and investment construction.

articleTitle: Risk Management of Integrated Energy System Decarbonization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The integrated energy system (IES) enables the fulfillment of load demand through multi-energy flow coupling and enhances energy utilization efficiency. Given the uncertainties posed by the “dual carbon” context, studying the low-carbon economic operation of the IES has become increasingly crucial. To enhance energy efficiency and reduce carbon emissions, this paper proposes and constructs an IES that incorporates electric, gas, thermal, and hydrogen coupling. To account for the environmental variability and risks affecting renewable energy sources, which can impact the IES, the multiple-scene generation and reduction method is introduced to optimize the deterministic IES model. Additionally, carbon capture equipment is integrated into the model, and the validity of the proposed model is verified under various operating conditions. Subsequently, both the economic and environmental benefits of the system are notably improved.

articleTitle: Research on Fine New Energy Consumption Analysis Technology Based on Multi-stage Cross Section Nesting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With in-depth implementation of “dual carbon” strategy, the construction of new power system focusing on new energy is accelerating. A scientific and comprehensive evaluation of new energy accommodation and utilization level has important guiding significance for power planning and layout, grid construction and overall arrangement of grid operation mode. A fine new energy consumption analysis technology based on multi-stage cross section nesting is presented in this paper. Firstly, the reasons for limited consumption of new energy and evaluating indicators for consumption level are analyzed. Then, a multi-level nested cross-section fine new energy consumption analysis method is proposed, which accurately analyzes the particle size to a single station. Finally, multi-level, multi-dimensional, multiple data sources, minute level and customized online consumption analysis function is achieved relying on the new generation scheduling technology support system. It has been applied to a provincial-level power regulation center in China on January 1, 2023. Taking the application results as an example, the effectiveness and practical value of the proposed analysis method were verified.

articleTitle: During-Event Mobile Energy Storage Real-Time Dispatching Method of Resilient Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To address the risks posed to the electric power system's safety and stability with extreme weather conditions and the high proportion of uncertain new energy sources, an optimization model for real-time scheduling of mobile energy storage to restore critical loads was proposed, based on an analysis of the resilience of the distribution system and the advantages of energy storage with minimal temporal and spatial constraints. The article presents a definition of resilience and a system resilience curve and establishes a multidimensional set of indicators for evaluating system resilience. While adhering to the operational constraints of the electrical grid, it optimizes the scheduling of mobile energy storage units and controls the switching states between grid lines. It uses mixed-integer linear programming to find the optimal energy storage unit scheduling plan with the goal of maximizing the recovery of critical loads in the system. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method in enhancing the resilience of the power system was validated through a case study of a node distribution system.

articleTitle: A Dispatch Model for Integrated Rural Energy Systems Considering Load Flexibility
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Combined heat and power (CHP) units can realize combined heat and power with high energy utilization and good economic performance. However, the non-synchronization of electricity and heat loads in integrated rural energy systems (IRES) has prevented the good economic performance of CHP units from being fully utilized, in order to fully exploit the demand-side flexibility, a dispatch model for an IRES considering load flexibility is proposed to further improve the economy of IRES operation. The model of the greenhouse heat load flexibility is based on the cumulative temperature theory of crops and the model of livestock farm heat load flexibility is based on the flexible requirements of animal welfare for livestock farm ventilation. Then, the worst-case conditional value at risk (WCVaR) is utilized to evaluate real-time dispatch costs and to construct a dispatch model with the sum of energy production costs, demand response incentive costs, and WCVaR-based real-time dispatch costs as the objective function, taking into account the rural load flexibility constraints, the WCVaR-related constraints, and other component operating constraints. Finally, the validity of the model proposed in this chapter is verified by an arithmetic example analysis.

articleTitle: Robust Optimization of a CCS-P2G Virtual Power Plant Accounting for Penalized Carbon Price
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The virtual power plant (VPP) consisting of power to gas (P2G) and carbon capture system (CCS) can reduce the system carbon emissions and effectively respond to the low-carbon electricity market. However, the fluctuation of carbon price in the carbon trading market affects the carbon capture rate and carbon trading cost of the VPP system, and the uncertainty of renewable energy output in the VPP also affects the optimal scheduling. Therefore, this paper constructs a robust optimal scheduling model of CCS-P2G virtual power plant taking into account the punitive carbon price. In the model, the penalty carbon price increases the price of excessive carbon emission; the volatility of renewable energy output is included in the robust optimization. The simulation results show that compared with the traditional carbon price, the penalty carbon price has a better carbon reduction effect on VPP; the smaller the robustness index in the robust optimization, the more conservative the system is, and the larger the VPP gain is, and vice versa. The model proposed in this paper can efficiently participate in the competition of power market and carbon trading market, and the formulation of reasonable penalty carbon price and robustness index can realize the synergy of economy and low carbon of VPP system.

articleTitle: Cluster-Based Hierarchical Coordination Planning and Control Strategy for Distribution Network Generation-Load-Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The increasingly prominent high intermittency characteristics of a high proportion of distributed energy sources pose new challenges for the rational planning of generation-storage and the coordination control between devices in distribution networks. In light of this, this paper proposes a multi-level coordination planning and control strategy for distribution networks based on cluster partitioning method. Firstly, it introduces a comprehensive index cluster partitioning method for distribution networks that takes into account electrical distance under load forecasting. secondly, building upon the cluster framework, a two-level joint planning model is proposed. In the upper level, an addressing and sizing model for sources and storage is developed specifically for clusters. In the lower level, the objective function is set to minimize node voltage deviations, and a voltage control model is established. Then. the upper and lower-level models are solved using a particle swarm algorithm with a simulated annealing strategy and a deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm. Finally, the effectiveness of the two-tier optimization model for generation-load-storage was validated in a specific 35 kV/10 kV distribution network.

articleTitle: High Wind Power Penetration System Power Flow Off-Limit Early Warning Based on GCN and Rule Guidance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the large-scale grid connection of new energy sources, the possibility of local power flow off-limit evolving into a global security risk has significantly increased, and the risk of power flow off-limit faults in the new transmission network is also increasing. However, traditional physical models for calculating power flow off-limit face issues such as slow calculation speed, high complexity, and redundant constraints. Therefore, this paper proposes a risk warning method for power flow off-limit in power systems based on the GCN algorithm and the physical rule guidance. Firstly, the influence of new energy sources, mainly wind power, on the risk of power flow off-limit in power systems under different operating conditions is fully considered, and the wind power scenarios data is generated. Secondly, a large number of power flow off-limit fault chains are generated using an improved OPA model based on DC current flow. Then, a risk warning model for power flow off-limit based on the GCN algorithm and the physical rule guidance is constructed, realizing the advanced warning of fault chains. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted on the IEEE 39 system, and the results show that the proposed method has fast calculation speed, high accuracy, and reasonable results. It helps improve the safety and reliability of power system operations.

articleTitle: A Consensus Index-Based Distributed Control for Islanded AC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This article introduces a consensus index (CI)-based distributed secondary control approach to enhance the operation of an islanded AC microgrid. In the proposed microgrid, inverter-based distributed generators (DGs) are interconnected via a balanced communication topology featuring bidirectional edge weights of equal magnitude. The primary objective of this proposed distributed control strategy, based on the consensus index, is to ensure the convergence of both frequency and estimated average voltage to predefined reference values. Additionally, it aims to achieve precise and proportionate active/reactive power allocation in between all the participating DGs within the islanded AC microgrid. To validate the efficacy of the proposed control methodology, a series of comprehensive simulation tests have been conducted.

articleTitle: Efficient Simulation Method for Modular Multilevel Converter with Embedded Super Capacitor Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The numerous switching devices and extensive simulation scale of modular multilevel converter with embedded super capacitor energy storage system (MMC-SCES) pose a great challenge to the efficiency of electromagnetic transient simulation. To address this issue, an efficient MMC-SCES electro-magnetic transient simulation method based on the Thevenin equivalent circuit is proposed in this paper. The method employs a nested fast and simultaneous solutions approach to model MMC-SCES, which not only significantly reduces simulation time and maintains simulation accuracy, but also preserves all dynamic variables of the converter. A double-ended MMC-SCES simulation system is built to validate the proposed efficient simulation method. The results show that compared with the simulation method based on the average value model (AVM), the proposed efficient simulation method has higher accuracy and efficiency, which can fit the dynamic variables inside submodules.

articleTitle: Digital Isolator Based on On-Chip Transformer for High-Voltage SiC MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In high-voltage applications utilizing Silicon Carbide (SiC) MOSFETs, digital isolators play a crucial role. These isolators separate the low-voltage control side from the high-voltage power side, ensuring the safety of both the low-voltage control circuit and operators. This paper presents a digital isolator design utilizing on-chip transformer technology, specifically designed for SiC MOSFET drivers operating at a maximum switching frequency of 100kHz. The transformer consists of two adjacent square copper windings insulated with polyimide, achieving an isolation voltage of 5kV. The proposed design incorporates pulse count techniques with a refresh module, which not only effectively reduces power consumption but also prevents error generation. Simulation results confirm the digital isolator's capability to achieve a maximum data rate of 40Mbps, a transmission delay of 21ns, and a static current of 150uA.

articleTitle: A Stackelberg game Based optimization strategy for Joint bidding of multi-agent wind power producers and multi-agent demand response aggregators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Aiming at the economy and accuracy of resource interaction matching between multi-agent wind power produc-ers(WPPs) and multi-agent demand response aggregators(DRAs) under the DR marketization scenario, a joint bidding optimization strategy between DRAs and WPPs based on the Stackelberg multi-leader multi-follower(MLMF) game is investigated. Firstly, a two-layer MLMF game framework with multi-agent DRAs as the leader and multi-agent WPPs as the follower is established. Secondly, a price mechanism based on non-cooperative game theory is established at the leader level; a resource matching mechanism based on bidding power difference and game price is established at the follower level. The optimization algorithm with particle swarm and commercial solver nested with each other is designed to simulate the model for distributed solving, which verifies the effectiveness and reasonableness of the proposed strategy in terms of the accuracy of resource matching between multi-agent DRAs and multi-agent WPPs and the stability of the bidding of WPPs, and gives the theoretical proof of the equilibrium solution of the MLMF game.

articleTitle: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning Based Short-Term Carbon Emission Price Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Considering that the available training data are insufficient in building a conventional machine-learning based carbon price forecasting model for the national carbon emission market in China, an alternative machine-learning scheme, i.e. the model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML), is employed for short-term carbon price forecasting in this work. Specifically, a pre- trained global meta-model in MAML is generated with training data from all carbon emission trading centers, and then customized to personalized forecasting models for each carbon emission trading center, and then the carbon price forecasting accuracy of the carbon emission trading center with insufficient training data could be enhanced. Numerical results show that the proposed method could attain accurate carbon emission price forecasting results.

articleTitle: Environmentally Friendly Generator Circuit Breaker Based on Vacuum Switch and Air Circuit Breaker
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Different from the fault current fed by system, the fault current fed by large synchronous generator presents severe delayed current zero phenomenon, requiring generator circuit breaker (GCB) to damp the fault current to cross zero and withstanding high transient recovery voltage (TRV). At present, SF6 interrupters are commonly used in GCB with large capacity, using SF6 arc resistance to damp the current and withstand TRV. However, SF6 gas can severely exacerbate the greenhouse effect, and SF6 type GCB has long been monopolized by companies such as ABB and Alstom. To avoid the use of SF6 gas in GCB, considering the high arc voltage of air circuit breaker (ACB) and fast dielectric recovery speed of vacuum switch (VS), topology and working strategy of an environmentally friendly GCB with ACB and VS connected in series are proposed. The use of ACB is expected to damp the fault current to cross zero swiftly, and VS to withstand the high TRV. Simulation verifications have been carried out in PSCAD/EMTDC. Research shows that the use of 24kV VS and 1.5kV ACB in series can enable the GCB to be a feasible alternative to SF6 type GCB.

Author Keywords: fault current fed by large synchronous generator

articleTitle: Frequency-Constrained Unit Commitment Considering Pumped Hydro Storage's Participation in Primary Frequency Regulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To investigate the crucial role of pumped hydro storage (PHS) in primary frequency regulation (PFR) within the context of unit commitment (UC) problems, this paper proposes a frequency-constrained unit commitment considering PHS's participation in PFR (PHS-FCUC). Firstly, a detailed modeling of PHS within the framework of the average system frequency (ASF) model is provided to obtain the frequency dynamic response equation for a multi-machine system including the PHS and thermal units. Then, by constructing the frequency deviation curve, a concise and practical expression for the frequency nadir constraint is obtained. Following this, the dynamic frequency constraints are integrated into the UC model, resulting in the creation of the PHS-FCUC model. Finally, based on real data from a provincial-level power grid in south China, multiple scenario cases with varying levels of renewable energy source (RES) penetration and PHS ratios are designed. The proposed model is solved using particle swarm optimization algorithms, and the results are compared with the traditional unit commitment (TUC) model and traditional frequency-constrained unit commitment (FCUC) model. The results confirmed the effectiveness of the model.

articleTitle: Ultra-short-term PV Forecasting Based on Time Series Representation Learning and NWP Data Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Currently, the mainstream photovoltaic(PV) power forecasting methods generally adopt a data-driven approach for modeling. The construction of input features, a key component of these methods, has a significant impact on the prediction results. Existing modeling methods typically use meteorological data and power directly as feature inputs, or employ statistical methods to manually construct features, which introduce some subjectivity. This paper first addresses this issue by adopting time series representation learning methods for automatic feature learning, studying the deterministic and cyclical fluctuations in photovoltaic output to improve prediction accuracy. Furthermore, while using measured meteorological data and power data as prediction inputs, this paper enhances the model's predictive accuracy on a 4-hour ahead time scale by integrating Numerical weather prediction(NWP) data as predictive covariates. Lastly, the model uses the transformer architecture, the decoder part of which uses a one-step output, enhancing the training and inference speed. The results validated through comparative experiments demonstrate that the ultra-short-term PV power forecasting adopted in this paper, which is based on time series representation learning and the NWP data integration, is able to enhance the overall forecasting accuracy, especially the forecasting accuracy on a 4-hour ahead time scale.

articleTitle: Online Identification Solution and Key Technology for Secondary Equipment and Circuit Anomalies in Substations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The substation is the transmission and transformation hub of the power system, and timely detection of secondary equipment (especially protective devices) and circuit anomalies is crucial for preventing misoperation of protective devices and ensuring the safe and stable operation of the power system. This paper studies the method of anomaly identification for protection and circuit based on online data, proposes an online automatic identification scheme for substation secondary equipment and circuit anomalies for on-site applications, and proposes key technologies for online identification of anomaly types such as voltage transformer secondary open-circuit, current transformer secondary open-circuit, current transformer secondary circuit multiple point grounding, and current transformer neutral line open-circuit based on online homologous data.

articleTitle: Different Temperature Distributions During the Formation of Cathode Spot Crater in Vacuum Arcs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The 2D axisymmetric model of crater with flowable heat transfer is combined with the mass, momentum, and heat transfer equations. However, it is considered that the initial cold cathode surface does not have current density. Under the new simulation condition of electric field, two typical distributions of temperature are obtained for different external parameters. At higher pressure relative to the heating efficiency, a distribution of temperature on droplet head much higher than the central area is formed. When the heating efficiency is large enough, the temperature of central area increases continuously, resulting in the same temperature as the metal droplet head.

articleTitle: Ultra-short-term Irradiation Prediction Based on Ground-based Cloud Images and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power generation has been widely used due to its advantages of green and clean, easy installation. However, since its output is mainly determined by irradiation, the intermittency, randomness, and instability of irradiation make PV large-scale grid-connectedness a lousy impact on the safety and economic operation of the power grid. Therefore, irradiation prediction can suppress randomness and instability, indirectly improving the quality of PV power generation. In this paper, firstly, image segmentation processing and feature extraction are carried out on the ground-based cloud images to digitize the images in low dimensions, where a new adaptive threshold image segmentation method based on RGB-Grey-OTSU is proposed to make the cloud images three-valued, separating the sun, clouds, and sky, and comparing it with the traditional threshold segmentation method. Feature extraction is carried out on the processed cloud images. In this paper, three feature values of weather, the percentage of sun, and cloud are extracted, and the strong correlation between the extracted feature values and irradiation is verified. This paper adopts and compares the two deep-learning prediction models, LSTM and GRU, and their performance of ultrashort-term irradiation prediction on different prediction time scales from 5 minutes to 1 hour.

articleTitle: A Review of Data-Physical Fusion Methods for Lithium-Ion Battery State Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries, owing to their advantages of cleanliness, efficiency, safety, and stability, are widely used in various fields such as new energy, electrical energy storage, and microelectronics. Accurate estimation of the state of charge and health status during their operation is essential for improving the reliability and cost-effectiveness of lithium-ion batteries in the development and utilization process. Many scholars have conducted research on state estimation of lithium-ion batteries under different operating environments and conditions, with the most representative approaches being physics-based models based on equivalent circuits or electrochemical equations and data-driven ‘black-box’ models.However, due to the complex application scenarios of lithium-ion batteries, especially under extreme operating conditions such as low temperatures, single physics-based or data-driven models have their limitations. Therefore, this paper attempts to review the relevant literature on lithium-ion battery state estimation from the perspective of data-physical fusion, summarize existing research methods, and provide insights into future research directions. The aim is to offer guidance and references for researchers in the relevant field.

articleTitle: Efficient Revenue Allocation Approach to Virtual Power Plant Operation with Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This study examines the collaborative optimization strategies between the Virtual Power Plant (VPP) and the Electric Vehicle (EV) aggregator for enhancing market transaction revenues.
