Electric energy substitution can use electric energy to replace loose coal and oil in the energy consumption terminal, which can effectively promote the optimization and adjustment of China's energy structure and has a good development prospect. In view of this situation, a prediction method combining time series and BP neural network is proposed. The time series model based on three-index smoothing method is predicted by electric alternation, and the prediction result is modified by BP neural network. Energy use data from Shanghai Municipal Bureau of Statistics were used as forecast and comparative analysis data. The calculation results show that compared with the unilateral prediction method, the method combining time series and BP neural network can significantly improve the prediction accuracy of electric energy substitution, and the prediction model can also accurately predict the electric energy substitution potential of Shanghai from 2022 to 2025, which provides a certain reference for Shanghai to make energy substitution plans.

articleTitle: Typical Elastic Load Regulation Performance Evaluation and Optimal Selection Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Under the carbon neutrality strategy, fully exploring the potential of demand side elastic load resources to participate in power system regulation has become one of the important ways to ensure the high-quality development of the energy and power industry. In view of the difficulty in evaluating the regulation performance caused by the significant randomness of elastic load resources, this paper constructs an elastic load power characteristic model represented by air conditioning based on the method of equivalent thermal parameters (ETP), establishes a comprehensive evaluation index system of elastic load participation in power system regulation considering the adjustability and reliability, and proposes an improved load optimization method based on evidence theory. In order to achieve a reasonable characterization of elastic load adjustable performance. Finally, this paper conducts empirical analysis on a park in southern China, and the results show that the proposed method can effectively shield the interference of user random behavior, transient conditions, and other factors on comprehensive evaluation and optimization, and can better capture the comprehensive regulation performance of elastic loads.

articleTitle: Multi-Layer Feature Fusion for Small Target Detection Based on Yolov5
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the low visibility of small targets, small target detection (STD) is considered one of the most challenging tasks in the object detection framework. The term “small target” refers to objects that occupy a small proportion of the input image. For example, the widely used MS COCO dataset defines objects with a border size of 32×32 pixels or smaller in a typical 480×640 image as small targets. In contrast, other datasets have their definitions, such as objects that make up 10 % of an image. Small targets are often missed or detected by misplaced borders and sometimes incorrectly marked. The main reason for the inaccuracy of STD localization is the degradation of subsequent space due to the limited information provided by input images or video frames superimposed on the deep network layer. Since small targets often appear in various application fields, such as pedestrian detection, medical image analysis, face recognition, traffic sign detection, traffic light detection, and ship detection, it is worth studying how to improve the performance of modern deep-learning STD techniques. Therefore, we proposed an improved Yolov5-based small targets detection method in this paper. Firstly, based on the original anchor box, a group of smaller anchor boxes is added to detect small targets in the shallow feature map. In addition, we split the image into different small areas for detection and then converted them into standard image sizes. This method is straightforward and effective to help us focus on small targets in an image. Finally, we upsample the deep feature map and concatenate it with the shallow feature map to obtain a larger feature map for STD. as shown in Fig. 1. Experiments show that our model achieves a mAP of 45.1 % on the VisDrone dataset, which far exceeds the 35.7 % detection score of the Yolov5 model.

articleTitle: Evaluation Method for Weak Links in Power Supply of New Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the widespread application of renewable energy and the popularization of distributed power sources, traditional distribution systems are facing the challenge of weak power supply links. The existence of weak power supply links not only affects the stable supply of electricity, but also limits the absorption capacity of distributed power sources. This article takes into account the enhancement of distributed power generation capacity and interconnection capability in the new urban distribution system, establishes an evaluation index system for weak links in power supply, including voltage level, load rate, power loss, short-circuit and distributed generation accommodation, uses mathematical models and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for quantitative analysis, develops corresponding improvement measures and optimization strategies, and enhances the power supply capacity of weak links. The proposed method has been validated in a real case study of a new distribution system, demonstrating the effectiveness of the weak point assessment and handling method.

articleTitle: Implementation of GPU Scheduling Method for Kubernetes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Kubernetes is an open-source system used for automating the deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications, and is a core component of the Power Cloud platform. The default scheduling mechanism in Kubernetes primarily evaluates node scores based on CPU and memory utilization. While this approach assesses the resource consumption of nodes, it fails to incorporate multidimensional metrics for evaluating nodes and adapting to the complexity of GPU resources. Consequently, it fails to ensure appropriate GPU resource allocation for specific workloads within the Power Cloud platform. To address the complexity and high-stability requirements of the Power Cloud platform, this study proposes a GPU resource scheduling scheme based on Prometheus. This scheme utilizes Prometheus as a data collection tool to gather multidimensional metrics such as GPU usage, disk utilization, and network traffic across nodes in the cluster, using these metrics as additional scoring criteria. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed scheduler outperforms the default scheduler, achieving better resource allocation and load balancing.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation Strategy of Integrated Energy System Considering Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: During the heating period of integrated energy systems, the heat-led mode operation of the heat and power association unit limits the peak shaving capacity of the system, resulting in high wind power abandonment rate and operation cost. An optimal operation strategy of integrated energy system considering demand response(DR) is proposed for solving this problem. Firstly, the electric boiler is introduced into the heat and power association system to realize the thermal power decoupling and optimize the heat and power association unit output. Secondly, an integrated DR model including reducible load and transferable load is established. Finally, considering the penalty cost of wind abandonment, a day ahead optimal operation strategy of heat and power association system with minimum operation cost as the objective is proposed. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy can improve the consumption rate of wind power and reduce the operation cost of the system effectively.

articleTitle: Research on Improving the Measurement Accuracy of the Hall Current Sensor Based on the Extreme Learning Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: For the hall current sensor is affected by temperature requires temperature compensation, this paper adopts the method of multi-sensor technology, the method of current sensor as the main sensor, temperature sensor as auxiliary sensor, the measured data as data fusion input, different test current in hall current sensor, the temperature sensor to monitor its working temperature, according to the monitoring results using the Extreme Learning Machine set up the function relationship between the measured current, hall current sensor output voltage and its working temperature and data fusion processing to weaken the temperature interference to the current sensor. Finally, it is shown that through simulation, the measurement accuracy of current sensor is 1~2 orders of magnitude higher than before compensation, which can better meet the requirements of actual measurement.

articleTitle: Modeling of Induction Motor Bearing Fault by Using Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Industries rely heavily on induction motors (IM) as they are simple, robust, easily maintained and less costly. Due to 1M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">,</sup>s large application, they are subjected to various types of faults, bearing faults leading with 40–45 % of total failures. Increase in friction due to bearing wear and tear mostly leads to bearing faults in induction machines. Bearing faults due to increase in friction impacts various motor parameters like magnetic flux density, stator currents, torque, etc. In this paper, an approach to model the induction motor bearing fault by using Finite Element Method (FEM) is presented. The impact of such fault due to the wear and tear of bearings on various motor parameters is further investigated. For this purpose, a co-simuation model for a 3 kW induction motor has been developed using ANSYS Maxwell and Simplorer. The bearing fault is incorporated by increasing the value of damping friction coefficient to the motor shaft in the model.

articleTitle: Wind Power Forecasting: LSTM-Combined Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the high penetration of renewable energies connected to smart grids, accurate wind power forecasting becomes more and more crucial to cope with its intermittency to achieve power balance. However, traditional forecasting methods face several challenges from model complexity, prediction delay, and insufficient training data. To address the mentioned challenges, we propose a forecasting scheme that combines long short-term memory(LSTM) and reinforcement learning (RL), to achieve accurate forecasting of short-term wind power. First, we train an LSTM model based on historical data as the basic model, which can effectively improve the input information accuracy. Secondly, we utilize the wind power output predicted by LSTM to form the state space in RL. Meanwhile, a well-designed reward function is proposed to guide the RL agent's training, which does not need the pre-prepared data and model knowledge. Finally, the case studies verify the superiority of the proposed method in terms of wind power forecasting accuracy.

articleTitle: Correlation Analysis Between Electrification and Energy Efficiency of Park-Level Integrated Energy System Considering Operational Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, we propose the evaluation indices for the electrification level and energy efficiency of park-level Integrated Energy System (IES), and explore the intrinsic correlation between the two based on the operation optimization results. First, the historical annual load curves of the IES are clustered to obtain 8 typical daily cooling and heating load curves, and the capacities of various energy-supply facilities are selected based on the maximum values of the typical daily loads, including combined cooling, heating and power (CCHP), gas boiler (GB), electric boiler (EB), air conditioner (AC), electric energy storage (ESS), and power substation (SUB). Secondly, the operation of different facilities is optimized with the minimum annual operating cost as the objective function, thus both the electrification level and energy efficiency can be calculated and assessed, as well as the operation strategies. Finally, by adjusting the percentage of CCHP's heating supply, the operation mode of the IES is changed with the other facilities' adjustment, the correlation between the electrification level and the energy efficiency is obtained. Case studies are carried out based on a real industrial park in Guangdong, China, and the results show the effectiveness of the proposed evaluation indices, while the electrification level shows a positive correlation with the energy efficiency level.

articleTitle: Fault-Current Limiting Strategy for Grid-Forming Converters With Virtual Impedance From Both Inner CCL and Outer VCL
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the improvement of the control strategies of grid-forming converters (GFMCs), the quantity and dimensions of semiconductor components continue to increase, resulting in GFMCs unable to withstand large currents during grid faults like traditional synchronous generators (SGs). Therefore, the fault current limitation of GFMCs during grid faults has become a research priority. This paper proposes a current limiting strategy for GFMC based on dual-loop-feed virtual impedance (VI). The strategy introduces voltage compensation into both the outer voltage control loop (VCL) and inner current control loop (CCL), resulting in an enhancement of the inverter's output impedance and the response speed of current limiting control. In contrast to conventional current-saturation methods, the proposed strategy maintains the characteristics of a voltage source converter (VSC) while limiting the fault current. Finally, the proposed strategy is verified in a simulation model. The simulation results conclusively illustrate that the proposed VI-based current limiting strategy efficiently mitigates ac current during three-phase short-circuit faults and improves the stability of GFMC during fault transients.

articleTitle: Dynamic Triggering Strategy for VPPs Based on Physical Operating State and Electricity Market
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The problem of low motivation of virtual power plant participation in the power market is studied in this paper. A dynamic trigger model of virtual power plants based on physical operation state and power market is proposed to improve the enthusiasm of virtual power plants to participate in the power market. First, pricing strategies for different time scale power markets are proposed. Then, we build a data-driven virtual power plant response willingness prediction model. And a total of eight factors in two dimensions of physical operation state and market operation state are selected as model feature inputs. Finally, this paper utilizes Matlab to simulate the actual trading process in the two markets of peaking and frequency regulation to verify the feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Persistent Load Prediction Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The power industry has seen a surge in research on load forecasting. However, most of these studies focus solely on improving the prediction accuracy of a specific set of load data, neglecting practical engineering application issues. Existing load forecasting algorithms lack adaptability to different regions' load data and struggle to provide long-term effective predictions for a particular location. To address these two challenges, this paper proposes an Adaptive Persistent Load Prediction Framework. The framework achieves improved adaptability and persistence for various regional load data by autonomously adjusting prediction algorithm parameters and introducing feedback mechanisms. Through case studies, this paper demonstrates the superiority of the proposed load forecasting framework in terms of prediction accuracy and persistence across different regions.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Analysis of Market Price Levels in the Green Electricity Market
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing scale of the green power market, all kinds of risks in the green power market will gradually appear. This paper will start from the price mechanism of green power trading, consider the coal market, carbon market, green certificate market and other multi-market environment elements, construct the evaluation index system of the price level of green power, and determine the index weights based on AHP-CRITIC, and analyze the influence degree of each index.

articleTitle: Capacity Optimization of wind Generation Considering Complementary Operation with Pumped Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: A reasonable system capacity allocation scheme is an important basis for the development and utilization of renewable energy. Firstly, a multi-objective wind-pumped storage system capacity optimization model is established with the objectives of minimizing levelized cost of energy, minimizing the net load peak valley difference of regional power grids, and minimizing the output deviation of the hybrid system, considering the uncertainties of wind power outputs. Then, an algorithm combining improving the strength evolutionary algorithm and mixed integer linear programming is constructed to solve the model. Finally, the pareto frontier is obtained and the trend of three objectives is analyzed.

articleTitle: Consensus-based Coordination of Battery Energy Storage Systems for Frequency Regulation Service
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Battery energy storage systems (BESSs) have been widely adopted in providing ancillary services, e.g., frequency regulation, to the power system. Existing studies usually focus on the accurate tracking of regulation signal, while overlook the heterogeneous cost in actuating different BESS units, which might lead to a less cost-efficient operation. In this paper, we present a convex optimization model to describe the cost-aware power allocation problem of BESSs in tracking regulation signal. Considering privacy protection and scalability, we propose a consensus-based algorithm for BESS coordination in a fully-distributed manner. The optimal power allocation among BESSs is achieved by exchanging auxiliary variables within the local neighborhood, which protects the privacy and promotes the scalability. Several numerical experiments are presented to show the effectiveness of the proposed method. The optimal power allocations in individual time intervals are validated, and the collective tracking performance of the BESS units is illustrated. The economic benefit of the cost-aware power allocation strategy is also demonstrated in the case study.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Fan - Synchronizer Interconnected Power System Based on Shapelet Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing proportion of wind power, the transient behavior of power system has changed, and new instability phenomenon with unknown mechanism has occurred in some high proportion areas. In order to deeply understand the dynamic characteristics of double-fed fans and the mechanism of their interaction with the power grid, and then analyze the influence of large-scale double-fed wind power access on the stability of the power system, this paper adopts TRI co-simulation technology to conduct electromagnetic transient simulation of double-fed wind units in the RTDS system, and obtains detailed transient process data. shapelet algorithm based on mutual information method is used to select the key time series data in stable samples, and the interaction mechanism between fan and power grid is revealed by analyzing these data. This research method is of great significance to explore the transient characteristics of fan - synchronizer interconnected power systems.

articleTitle: A Scenario-Based and Model-Supported Analysis of Economic Benefit for Virtual Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Virtual power plant (VPP) is an effective way to integrate geographically scattered distributed energy resources (DERs), and is helpful for DERs to participate in the electricity markets and response to power system operation. It is of great significance for the investment and operation of VPP to comprehensively evaluate the benefits of virtual power plants. However, in the process of construction and operation of VPP, the influencing factors the economic benefits under the market environment and power system operation have not been fully studied. Therefore, this paper proposes a set of evaluation index and model to comprehensively evaluate the operation revenue, environmental benefits and costs of VPP. An VPP test system is applied in the benefit evaluation index framework, and the calculation process of the benefit evaluation index is described in detail. The proposed method can reasonably evaluate the value of VPP from aspects such as construction, operation, and emission reduction benefits.

articleTitle: Analysis Method of Grid-Connected Capability of Distributed PV Based on Multi-Data Source Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper investigates and analyzes the conditions that restrict the acceptance capacity of distributed PV at home and abroad, and summarizes the factors that affect the acceptance capacity of distributed PV. An index system of distributed PV grid-connected acceptance capability is established, which takes into account grid reliability, quality and security. According to the integration of multi-source heterogeneous data such as distributed PV access information, grid production management information and user load information, the distribution network model containing distributed PV is completed, so as to carry out the acceptance capacity analysis. The example analysis shows that: access to high voltage levels can improve the distributed PV absorption capacity of the distribution network in the same distribution area. In addtion, demand response can improve the distributed PV absorption capability of distribution network.

articleTitle: Bidding Strategies and Equilibrium Analysis in Electricity Market under RPS and CET
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to achieve the dual carbon target, the government has been seeking effective incentives for green electricity market. In this paper, a multi-market, multi-actor game model is developed, in which the wholesale electricity market, the tradable green certificate (TGC) market and the carbon emissions trading (CET) market are regarded as general Cournot models, and retailers participate in the retail competition by making bids. Firstly, a new market trading framework is formed and explains the variation of changes in equilibrium outcomes under renewable portfolio standard(RPS) and CET. Secondly, based on the new trading framework, a multi-market and multi-agent game model is proposed. Finally, the impacts of changes in RPS quotas and carbon allowances on the strategic behaviour of fossil-fueled generation companies (FF GenCos), renewable energy generation companies (RE GenCos) and retailers are analysed through numerical examples. The results show that the implementation of RPS and CET provides significant incentives for both RE GenCos and retailers to secure the power output of FF GenCos, reduce carbon emissions and promote the development of renewable energy.

articleTitle: Rolling Clearing Model of Electric Carbon Joint Market Based on Centralized Carbon Trading Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the context of the “30·60” carbon peak and carbon neutrality goals, China has launched carbon emission trading nationwide, which is currently only in the power generation sector. However, due to the different physical constraints of the carbon market and the electricity market on commodity trading, the trading time scale is quite different, and it is difficult to integrate effectively. Therefore, in order to better discover the price signals of carbon traded commodities by unifying the trading time scale of the carbon joint market, this paper proposes a clearing model of the electricity carbon joint market considering the unit load rate-carbon emission intensity curve according to the characteristics of the current trading modes of the electricity market and the carbon market. Through the centralized carbon trading mechanism and the rolling liquidation of the electric carbon joint market, the time-segment carbon price and the benefits of the joint market are maximized.

articleTitle: Power System Security Boundary Identification and Rules Extraction based on Tighten Weighted Oblique Decision Tree
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy has a significant impact on the secure operation in power system. The high-dimensional observations in large-scale power grids make it difficult to determine whether a given operation point is safe. Data-driven methods can identify the security boundary of the power system and provide secure dispatching rules. In this paper, a tightened weighted oblique decision tree (TWODT) is proposed for the power system security boundary identification and extraction. It aims to minimize the number of hyperplanes, and reduce the constraints effectively. Furthermore, the extracted rules are tightened to reduce the false positive rate of misjudging unsafe states as safe. These rules can recommend adjustment targets and ranges for generators. The testing results on IEEE4-bus and IEEE118-bus validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Optimization of Photovoltaic Power Plant Design Scheme Based on Power Generation Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Parameter selection during the design stage of a photovoltaic (PV) power plant is of utmost importance, as it directly impacts the plant's revenue. This paper presents the construction of an hourly power generation model for PV power plants and employs it to determine the optimal design scheme as the objective function. The PV power plant's power generation model takes into consideration various influential factors, including the solar irradiance model, PV module model, inverter efficiency, maximum power point tracking, incident effect loss, shading loss, and other relevant parameters. The total power generation is calculated by inputting hourly meteorological data and parameters of the PV power plant design scheme into the power generation model. Subsequently, the particle swarm optimization (PSO) is applied to optimize the design scheme, maximizing the annual power generation. To enhance the efficiency of the PSO, adjustments were made to the inertia weight and contraction factor. Compared with the traditional empirical parameter design, the optimized design scheme showed a substantial increase in power generation.

articleTitle: A Complex-Based High Bandwidth Current Control Design for LCL Grid-Connected Inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In modern electrical power systems, inverters play a crucial role of energy conversion and power control. Meanwhile, inverter control also plays a key role in the hierarchical structure control of power grid. In this paper, a dominant pole elimination current control technique is proposed, which is suitable for grid-following inverter. The dominant pole with slow dynamic is eliminated by the basic zero-pole cancellation principle, and the load the load disturbance-rejection performance is improved. For double-loop control structures with power control outer loop and current control inner loop, due to the elimination of the dominant pole, the corresponding rapidity of the current control inner loop achieves an approximate unit gain from the reference point to the output, greatly improving the performance of the power control outer loop. In addition, the difficulty of parameter design is simplified by using complex coefficients. The effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method are verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Short-Term Scheduling of Cascaded Hydropower Stations with Pumped Storage Considering Strong Hydraulic Coupling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Hydropower has the flexibility to regulate power outputs with prices in the electricity market to maximize profits. The addition of pumped-storage units to cascade hydro power stations to form a hybrid pumped storage power system can better play the adjustment ability of hydropower. At the same time, it can also better play the role of the electricity market in guiding and influencing power generation. So that hydropower can obtain higher generation revenue. Firstly, the electricity market mechanism for the hybrid pumped storage power system is studied. Secondly, the system is modeled by analyzing the upstream and downstream hydraulic coupling relationship of hybrid pumped storage power system. The model is converted into a MILP model by the linearization method. Taking the hybrid pumped storage power system in the Xiaojinchuan basin of Sichuan province as an example. The total revenue of the system is improved 12.87% after the pumped storage units are added to the cascade hydropower stations, and the dispatching operation of the cascade hydropower stations are optimized while the system revenue is improved.

articleTitle: Research on Source-Grid-Load-Storage Integration Technology in Jilin Province, Which is Adapted to the New Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, firstly, we obtain a certain precision image of building roofs in a county with the help of high-resolution remote sensing information technology; then, based on Sobel operator edge detection, threshold segmentation and other image processing techniques, we eliminate non-building information in the image, extract the edge contour, and obtain the roof area of the building, and then estimate the photovoltaic capacity; secondly, we aim to minimise the comprehensive cost of distribution grid, which includes the cost of line modification, transformer expansion, energy storage, and distributed PV investment; finally, we establish a two-layer planning model with the constraints of PV development potential by using quantum particle swarm algorithm. Secondly, with the goal of minimising the comprehensive cost of the distribution network including line reconstruction, transformer expansion, energy storage, distributed PV investment and operation cost, and taking into account the constraints of PV development potential, we establish a two-layer planning model of source-grid-load-storage, and use the quantum particle swarm algorithm to achieve a fast model solution; finally, taking a county distribution network as an example, we verify the practicability of the source-grid-load-storage collaborative planning technology based on the assessment of the county's rooftop PV development potential, which improves the economy and reasonableness of the planning scheme.

articleTitle: Emergency Reactive Voltage Control Strategy to Improve the Transient Stability of New Energy Access to the Receiving End Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As new energy replaces conventional units on a large scale, the grid inertia and voltage support capacity gradually decrease. The new energy low voltage ride-through (LVRT) at the receiving grid end aggravates the power transfer and worsens the transient stability of the grid, so it is worthwhile to study how to make use of the reactive power resources to improve the transient stability under the limited active resources. This paper first studies the power characteristics of new energy LVRT, and gives the transient instability scenario of the receiving end grid in the new energy accessing AC/DC networked power grid. It studies the mechanism of new energy LVRT on the transient stability of the receiving end grid. It researches the excitation control of the synchronous condenser and the control mode involved in emergency control. An emergency reactive voltage control strategy is proposed to improve the transient stability of the receiving end grid with new energy access, and the effectiveness of the strategy is verified based on the simulation of the actual grid.

articleTitle: Simulation Testing Method for Distribution Network Control Based on Embedded Energy Management System and Matlab
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The current distribution network hardware in the loop (HIL) simulation testing relies on specialized hardware, which is costly and requires a large workload of control strategy development. This paper proposes a simulation testing method for distribution network control based on embedded energy management system (EMS) and Matlab. Firstly, an embedded EMS architecture is designed, including communication layer, data layer, background service layer, and display layer. Secondly, control configuration is implemented based on the AOE network and automatic differentiation technology, which supports the simple implementation of distribution network control strategies through “building block”. Based on technologies such as the Rust programming language, HTTP container, embedded database, asynchronous non-blocking communication, and WebAssembly, the EMS that can be deployed on embedded devices has been implemented. Thirdly, achieve HIL simulation testing through communication between the embedded EMS and Matlab simulation model. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method was verified through the orderly charging control experiment on charging piles in the distribution station area.

articleTitle: Explore the Correlation of Key Influence Factors on the Performance of Offshore Floating PV Power System Using Bifacial PV Modules and their Optimization Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Along with the continuous and rapid development of onshore solar photovoltaic (PV) power plants in China, the land resources appropriate for PV development are becoming increasingly limited. In compared with onshore PV power systems, the offshore floating ones have advantages of higher performance efficiency under identical solar resource, lower construction, operation, and maintenance costs, and no land occupation, which hence become one of the effective ways to address the contradiction between PV development and land resources. This work simulates the power generation of floating platform PV power plants and floating thin film PV power plants with a nominal power of 5kWp in offshore sea conditions through using PVsyst and AQWA. Five important factors affecting the performance of floating PV power generation systems including the space between PV arrays (D), PV module tilt angle (β), shortest distance between PV module and sea surface (h), the sea surface reflectivity (r), and the swing angle of the floating body (FB) 's horizontal plane affected by waves(a) are quantitatively analyzed and their correlation on the power system performance was also explored by a linear regression model. The results of path analysis show that the horizontal swing angle of the FB affected by waves (a) is the most significant factor over power system performance (36.3%), the remaining other factors are the surface reflectivity (22.25<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), PV module tilt angle (18.45<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), space between PV arrays (14.93%), and shortest distance between PV module and sea surface (8.07<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) in order. Based on the above results, a site selection and optimization method for offshore floating platform PV power generation system is proposed, which is expected to increase the power generation by 8.8% compared with that of floating thin film PV power system in smooth sea condition.

articleTitle: Transmission and Distribution Cooperative Congestion Scheduling Strategy Based on Dynamic Integration of Flexible Resources in Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the limitation that the branch power exceeds the capacity of the transmission line, the transmission congestion problem will occur in some time periods of the transmission network. With the demand side response and a large number of distributed energy access to the distribution network, it is possible to coordinate the controllable resources in the transmission network and the distribution network to solve the transmission congestion problem. Aiming at the problem that the demand side response resources are scattered and difficult to negotiate the compensation price, a bi-level optimization congestion scheduling strategy based on dynamic integration of flexible resources in distribution network is proposed. Under this strategy, the transmission network layer takes the minimum congestion cost as the goal, and optimizes the adjustment scheme of the generator set and the node price. The active distribution network layer dynamically integrates the flexible resources of the distribution network through the load characteristics and the node price. Through the interaction and coordination between the two layers, the optimal congestion scheduling scheme is obtained, and the transmission and distribution coordination solves the congestion problem. Based on the modified IEEE-39 experimental system, the effectiveness of the proposed strategy is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: A Physical Experimental Platform of Hydropower-Dominant Hybrid Energy System: Preliminary Progress
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Dependence on flexible hydropower plants to integrate renewable energy sources (RESs) such as wind and solar power, followed by the establishment of hybrid energy systems, has emerged as a critical avenue for advancing RES development. In this paper, the preliminary progress in the development of a physical experimental platform of a hydropower-dominant hybrid energy system is introduced. The platform is designed to integrate multiple power sources, including the completion of the conventional hydropower system (CHPS), pumped storage power system (PSPS), photovoltaic (PV) generation system, and battery energy storage system (BESS), with plans for the future construction of a wind power (WP) generation system. The hydropower facilities (CHPS and PSPS) can simulate the refined characteristics for the hydraulic-mechanical-electrical coupling process, meanwhile, the AC intelligent load system and grid circuit breaker can aid in creating scenarios such as microgrid and grid-connected conditions. Preliminary work involves establishing a numerical model to simulate the joint operation of the above five power sources, providing a basic understanding of the system's behavior. The purpose of the platform is to address common technical issues associated with hybrid energy systems. Hence, future experimental plans include topics such as coordinated control, transient processes of hydropower systems, and dynamic characteristics of the hybrid energy system. The construction and proposed study plans of this experimental platform aim to provide a theoretical and technical foundation for real-world hybrid systems.

articleTitle: A Graph Reinforcement Learning Algorithm for Unit Commitment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Unit commitment (UC) is the key problem in power system, and efficiently getting a solution with high quality can bring great economic and social benefits. Nowadays, as the scale of the power system has been increasing, the traditional optimization algorithms are deficient in solving accuracy and computational complexity. Artificial intelligence algorithms with powerful data process capabilities are developing rapidly and have been applied in the power system and achieved good results. Therefore, this paper proposes an algorithm to solve the UC problem based on graph reinforcement learning (GRL). Firstly, the markov decision process (MDP) of the UC problem is described based on its characteristics associated with the objective function and constraints, and the reward function is designed to update the strategy of the agent. Secondly, graph convolutional network (GCN) is chosen to better capture the topological feature of power system. Combined with deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm, a GRL algorithm is proposed to solve the UC problem. Thirdly, case studies are carried out to demonstrate the feasibility and performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Approach for Lithium-ion Battery Lifetime Classification Based on Early Cycles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In recent years, the global demand for electric energy has been increasing year by year. In order to cope with increasingly serious problems such as grid-connected new energy generation and increasing dispatching pressure of power grid systems, the demand for energy storage systems is growing day by day. However, in the grid-side energy storage system, huge amounts of battery cells are grouped into modules, packs, and systems. This presents a problem: cells with inconsistent lifetimes are assembled into a battery system, which will seriously affect the overall lifetime of the whole battery system. Therefore, early classification for lifetime of cells is important, futher more, fast and accurateclassification about health status of cells is also challenging. In this paper, the XGBoost model and the transformed voltage curves extracted from early cycles are combined to realize the early classification of the end of life(EOL) of batteries in the early aging process. By extracting the features from transformed voltage curves of discharge cycles in the first four weeks (depth of discharge, DOD=100), the EOL of 64 groups of batteries was classified into three categories (large/middle/small, L/M/S). It is worth mentioning that the feature interval that has the greatest influence on the lifetime classification is found to be 3.2V-3.4V through PCA transformation, which indicates the range of feature extraction for future lifetime prediction and classification. Finally, experiments on the ISU-ILCC Battery Aging Dataset show that for small feature requirements, the prediction accuracy of the method reaches more than 85%.

articleTitle: Implementation Methods for Marketization of Domestic and Foreign Demand Response: Current Situation and Prospects
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the advancement of new power system construction, the rapid development of new energy will bring huge challenges to the stable operation of the power system. In the system of large-scale integration of new energy, power demand response will play a more important regulatory role. Firstly, the situation of demand response resources and project types were introduced. Then, the development of foreign demand response projects was discussed from the perspective of market-oriented implementation methods. Then, the implementation methods of demand response in typical provinces and cities in China were analyzed. Finally, based on the current situation of China's new round of electricity reform and foreign experience, corresponding prospects for the development of demand response in China were proposed.

articleTitle: An Optimization Method for Renewable Energy and Energy Storage Capacity Allocation Based on Temporal Production Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the rapid expansion of large-scale renewable energy bases in China, optimizing the allocation of renewable energy and energy storage capacity is crucial for improving system efficiency. In this paper, a joint optimal configuration method of wind-photovoltaic-energy storage capacity based on time series production simulation is proposed for renewable energy transmission base. Its aim is to minimize the total investment cost of the system under certain constraints about the proportion of renewable energy power generation, renewable energy utilization rate, conventional thermal power operation, energy storage power station operation, ultra-high voltage direct current (UHVDC) regulation and power transmission. To handle the nonlinear constraints, linearization is achieved by introducing integer variables. For the complex operation constraints of conventional thermal power and UHVDC channel, a simplified modeling method of start-stop cycle and adjustment cycle is proposed, which can effectively reduce the number of integer variables and improve the solving efficiency. The effectiveness of the proposed method is tested on the data of a renewable energy base in Northwest China.

articleTitle: Rolling Forecast Energy Storage Planning Optimization Method for “Three High” Areas Based on the ARIMA Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The integration of a high proportion of renewable energy sources and significant external load delivery in new power systems introduces substantial planning challenges, particularly in storage capacity. This is primarily due to the unpredictability stemming from these factors, often resulting in insufficient storage planning and consequently high rates of wind and solar energy curtailment. Addressing this volatility necessitates a novel approach to energy storage planning. This paper initially outlines the uncertain nature and characteristics of “Triple High” power systems, then proceeds to emphasize the effectiveness of the ARIMA-based rolling forecast model in intricate planning contexts. This model's adaptability and proficiency in capturing correlations between various parameters facilitate the development of an energy storage planning model, which employs the 5th percentile error for optimizing storage capacity planning. The paper compares the installed capacity of energy storage obtained through simulation with the results of a detailed 8760-hour production simulation. The closer the results are to the production simulation, the better the learning reliability and superiority of the method. Ultimately, it compares the energy storage planning results based on the Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network models, and rolling forecast models, concluding that the rolling forecast model yields the best planning results for spring mud management in high-altitude regions.

articleTitle: Distributed Hierarchical Resilient Event-Triggering Control for DC Microgrids Under Mixed Cyber Attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Distributed control techniques are commonly employed to regulate the functionality of DC microgrids. However, the communication process in distributed control is highly susceptible to cyber attacks, with the most prevalent being denial of service (DoS) and false data injection (FDI) attacks. DoS attacks interrupt communication, while FDI attacks compromise data authenticity. The incidence of these two types of attacks in the microgrids system will make the distributed controllers unable to operate normally, resulting in the system being unable to operate safely and stably. To maintain the stable operation of the DC microgrids system against mixed DoS and FDI attacks, a distributed hierarchical resilient event-triggering controller is developed. The controller is comprised of two subcontrollers and an event-driven supervisor. The two subcontrollers are designed to operate based on feedback from either the bus voltage error or the branch current error. The supervisor selects the appropriate subcontroller based on the current state of the system. The Matlab/Simulink environment is utilized to construct a test system for DC microgrids, showcasing the effectiveness of the distributed hierarchical resilient event-triggered controller.

articleTitle: Constructing Knowledge Graph for Electricity Keywords Based on Large Language Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the information age, the electric power industry, as a crucial pillar of modern society, has accumulated a wealth of valuable research literature. Knowledge graph technology offers the potential to tap into this knowledge repository, providing a better understanding of research outcomes in the electric power domain. However, due to the diversity and complexity of knowledge in the power industry, it is difficult to build a comprehensive and complete knowledge graph of power keywords. In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have made significant advancements. This paper harnesses LLM technology along with text similarity analysis and co-occurrence frequency analysis to establish a comprehensive framework for processing keyword knowledge in the field of electric power. Within this framework, various forms of information found in electric power research can be processed. This includes creating a thesaurus of electric power domain keywords; obtaining the individual attributes implied by the information keywords in this thesaurus and their interconnections; and generating a knowledge graph of electric power domain keywords. This knowledge graph includes attributes, interpretations, relationships, and associated literature for keywords. It serves as a valuable reference for the effective utilization of research outcomes in the electric power domain.

articleTitle: Strategic Bidding and Trading in Joint Electricity-Carbon Market with Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Generation companies (GenCos) participate in both the electricity and carbon markets. Against this backdrop, coordinated strategic actions provide flexibility when maximizing GenCo's profit in joint electricity-carbon markets. However, dynamic coupling relationship in joint markets and uncertainties of renewable energy sources poses challenges. In this paper, a reinforcement learning (RL)-based multi-market joint coordination method is proposed. We first formulate the joint electricity-carbon market coordination problem and then design a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) on the problem. Then, a multi-market proximal policy optimization (MM-PPO) is adopted to solve the problem. Experiments show that by coordinating their bidding and trading strategies, GenCo can achieve higher profits than in the case where they act independently and also demonstrate its effectiveness in handling uncertainties in the joint electricity-carbon markets.

articleTitle: Collaborative Optimal Dispatch of Multi-Agent Distributed Integrated Energy System Based on Game Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The escalating demands of energy consumption and environmental conservation necessitate urgent advancements in energy infrastructures. In this context, Deep Integration of Multi-energy Systems (DIMS), which concentrates on the seamless integration of advanced multi-energy and information technologies, is considered the most promising strategy for resilient energy utilization in future societies. In a setting where multiple entities participate across source-network-load-storage links, achieving a balanced equilibrium that maximizes collective benefits is crucial. It therefore becomes vital to create a Distributed Integrated Energy System (DIES) operation strategy that aligns with an open energy market. To address this, we first introduce an Integrated Energy Management System (IEMS) to coordinate internal energy transactions. We propose a distributed hierarchical game architecture, taking bounded rationality into account. Under this mechanism, the upper IEMS modulates the electricity price strategy, while the lower entities achieve autonomous optimization scheduling through multi-energy collaboration and Synergy. These entities then engage in multi-agent cooperative optimization as prosumers. Furthermore, we employ the game mechanism to leverage load discrepancies, flexible role switching, and demand response, thereby effectively improving the load curve. To validate the effectiveness of our method, we employ a comparative analysis through a simulation on a DIES comprising of an IEEE 33-node network and an optimized 7-node natural gas network. This demonstrates the superiority of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Virtual Power Plants Considering Load Demand Response under Ladder-Type Carbon Trading Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This article studies a virtual power plant (VPP) optimization scheduling method that considers ladder-type carbon trading (LTCT) and electric-heat load demand response (DR). Firstly, the structural feature and the operating principle of VPP with heat load are introduced. The principle of the LTCT and the DR characteristics of electric and heat loads are analyzed. Then, a VPP optimization scheduling model is constructed. Except for significant constraints on VPP, the proposed model includes the LTCT and electric-heat load DR models. Finally, case studies on an industrial park in north China verify that under the LTCT mechanism, VPP considering load DR is beneficial for promoting low-carbon economic and social development.

articleTitle: Cause Identification Method of Power Quality Problems in Rural Low-Voltage Distribution Network Driven by Mechanism-Data Combination
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the access of high-proportion distributed photovoltaic, the power quality problems of rural low-voltage distribution network, especially the problems of high and low voltage and three-phase imbalance, are becoming more and more obvious, and the influencing factors of power quality problems are increasing and the cause analysis of power quality problems is more complicated. In view of the above problems, this paper proposes a method to identify the causes of power quality problems in rural low-voltage distribution networks based on the joint drive of mechanism data. Firstly, based on the characteristics of irrigation load power consumption in rural distribution network, the genetic sets and judging conditions corresponding to different power quality problems are sorted out, and the genetic criteria of power quality problems are sorted out according to relevant standards; Then, the role of neural network in the cause identification of power quality problems is analyzed, and the threshold correction method of the cause identification model of power quality problems is put forward. Finally, an example of a typical rural low-voltage distribution network proves that the proposed method can effectively improve the accuracy and efficiency of identifying the causes of power quality problems in low-voltage distribution networks.

articleTitle: An Identification Method for Biological Electric Shock in Low-Voltage Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the difficulty of recognizing residual currents from biological electric shock (BES) and resistive leakage, existing residual current devices are unable to accurately remove BES from low-voltage distribution networks and ensure supply reliability at the same time. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel approach for identifying BES by utilizing measured impedance and transient DC components of residual currents. Firstly, this paper analyses the leakage current and residual current of two types of faults, BES and resistive leakage, respectively. Then two identification methods are proposed based on the residual current: the first one is to calculate the measured impedance based on the faulty phase voltage and residual current after the faulty phase is selected, to judge whether BES takes place according to its imaginary part. The second one is to extract the transient DC fraction of the residual current by Prony algorithm and compare it with the dynamic fixed value to determine whether BES is occurring or not. The logical coordination between the two methods is performed. Finally, the correctness and speed of the proposed methods are validated through Matlab/Simulink simulations. This method enhances the accuracy of the BES identification and the performance of available residual current devices in low-voltage distribution networks.

articleTitle: Frequency Regulation Strategy for User-Side BESS Based on Estimated and Corrected Droop Coefficient
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The multiplexed application of user-side battery energy storage systems (BESSs) in energy arbitrage and frequency regulation is regarded as an effective way to improve its economic profits. However, the strategy under the multiplexed mode of BESS faces the dual challenges of dynamic resources allocation and random frequency deviation signal. To pursue maximum daily profits and reliable operation of BESS, this paper proposes a frequency regulation strategy based on the estimated and corrected droop coefficient, and forms a scheduling result with the arbitrage power, the droop coefficient and the capacity compensation coefficient. The simulation results show that the strategy achieves the optimal allocation of BESS resources totally avoiding the over-capacity, so that the maximum profits and the continuously available frequency regulation capability are guaranteed.

articleTitle: Recycling Chicken Bones into Environmentally-Friendly Products is a Step Towards Achieving the Sustainable Saudi Vision 2030
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Objective: The human consumes meat daily from plants, animals, and fish. Chicken and eggs are beneficial in many diets worldwide due to their high protein content and affordability. The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is the third country in the world that consumes chicken meat. Producing food is one of the causes of global warming and causes the world to suffer from flooding and increases the temperature of the earth. Sustainable agricultural practices are increasingly vital to address the challenges of food security and environmental conservation. These emphasize the need for communities to coexist harmoniously with nature, promoting sustainability in various aspects, including food production and recycling. This study designed and built a system that can transfer the chicken bone into a material that can used in agriculture as organic fertilizer. The process involves converting discarded chicken bones into nutrient-rich additives for soil, promoting sustainable farming practices and waste reduction. Methods: The chicken bones were recycled by mixing the dry bone with food waste such as eggshells, and banana peels and used tea in the proposed smart system. The prototype explains the methods clearly. The prototype explained the methods trial data was collected the results are promising and the system is smart and reliable. Results: The chicken bones were transferred into fertilizer. The speed of transformation depends on several factors such as heat, bone size, bone weight, and the power of the mixer. The time required to achieve the results for whole chicken weighted 1000 (g) is 20 hours to transfer to soil and 10 hours with heat. These results are useful for the chicken farming industry today, especially the chicken farmers. ANOVA statistical analysis indicates a significant difference with p <.05 in the fermentation process in both methods without heat and heat. Conclusion: This study demonstrated the smart recycling of chicken bones. The ability to use chicken bone in combination with waste food could help improve eco-friendly food production. The outcomes of this study could enhance the recycling of chicken bones into fertilizer and develop the soil with essential nutrients like calcium and phosphorus, enhancing soil fertility and supporting plant growth. Also, this research project contributes to sustainable agriculture practices, which are vital for long-term food security and it is compatible with Saudi Green Initiatives and Saudi Vision 2023 confirming the importance of the resource's sustainability.

articleTitle: Power System Restoration Strategy with High Proportion of New Energy Considering Power Network Pre-Decision
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: After a large number of new energy sources are connected, how to realize the rapid networking of various power sources in the recovery process to give full play to the load recovery capability of the network island is the key problem for the power system to quickly restore power supply and reduce power outage losses. Firstly, a pre-decision method for master-slave network of power supply for power grid restoration is proposed, and the necessary conditions and ranking indexes of power supply network operation are established. Then, an optimization model of power system restoration control with the goal of maximizing the net benefit of restoration is established, which comprehensively considers the load recovery benefit of the overall restoration scheme, the cost of network power supply and the risk of network restoration caused by factors such as the uncertainty of new energy power output and the time-varying fault probability of branches. Finally, based on the IEEE 69 bus system, the effectiveness of the proposed strategy is verified, and the networking scheme with economy, reliability and rapidity is effectively selected.

articleTitle: Modeling and Strategic Design of Multi-Layered Aggregation and Control for Flexible Loads
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With continuous development of new energy generation, there is an urgent need to enhance the regulation capabilities of the power system. This paper is dedicated to transforming potential flexible load resources into practically adjustable system resources, and a three-layer aggregation and control framework presented, i.e “User - Load Aggregator - Grid Operator.” Optimal decision-making models for three types of market entities are presented, including electricity consumption strategies of users, bidding strategies of load aggregators, and regulation resource procurement strategies of the system operator. The supply-demand difference caused by generation output fluctuations of intermittent renewable energy resources is examined, and source-load regulation resources are employed in the day-ahead ancillary service markets, especially the regulation market. Case studies are carried out to demonstrate the feasibility and efficiency of the proposed multi-layer aggregation and control model together with associated strategies in achieving optimal employment of flexible loads, and the effects of load aggregators' profits and grid operators's dispatch on balancing power supply and load demand.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive AHP-Based Evaluation Method for The Schedulable Capacity of New Market Entities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to promote the active participation of new market entities in the ancillary services market, a comprehensive evaluation method for the schedulable capacities of new market entities is proposed. First the schedulable capacities of electric vehicles and temperature control loads are estimated. And then, a comprehensive AHP-based evaluation model is established to evaluate the safety, economy and environmental benefits of power systems with the participation of new market entities. Case analysis shows that the power system's overload resistance and renewable energy consumption capacity have been improved substantially after the participation of new market entities.

articleTitle: Data Driven and Combinational Empowerment Based Operational Assessment for Electric Distribution Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the new changes in the distribution network, the traditional methods cannot satisfy the increasing requirements for the assessment of the security level, service level, and power supply quality. Therefore, this paper proposes an operation evaluation method based on data mining and combinational empowerment for distribution transformers. Firstly, this paper fuses data from different systems and selects indicators in the dimensions of risk, customer sensitivity, and voltage quality. Secondly, different evaluation methods are selected according to the characteristics of indicators in different dimensions. Finally, the rationality and effectiveness of the proposed method are verified with transformers in a southern city. The simulation results show that the proposed methods can effectively refine the risk level determined by the classification rule and identify those transformers with poor customer experience or voltage quality.

articleTitle: Analysis of Key Influencing Parameters of Small Disturbance Stability for Doubly-Fed Induction Generator Connected to the Series-Compensated AC Grid Based on Fuzzy Rough Set Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing grid-connected scale of wind power, represented by doubly-fed induction generators (DFIG), some characteristics of DFIG, such as nonlinearity, switching, multiple time scales, and the interaction between the wind turbines and the series-compensated capacitance, can contribute to the sub- synchronous oscillations (SSO). Meanwhile, the difficulty in analyzing the multi-parameter coupling effect also exists when the SSO occurs. Therefore, based on fuzzy rough set theory, this paper proposes a selection algorithm to find the key influencing parameters of the small disturbance stability for the DFIG connected to the series-compensated AC grid when SSO occurs. First, the mathematical equations of the doubly-fed induction motor and the rotor side converter are modeled in the DIgSILENT simulation platform. Then, this paper gives the selection and fuzzification process of the parameters related to SSO and proposes a feature-importance-based selection algorithm for key influencing parameters according to the dependence degree. Finally, the modal analysis data from the modified 3-machine 9- bus system with DFIG and the series-compensated capacitance is employed to calculate the influence of coupling parameters on the SSO of the system and select the key influencing parameters, which demonstrates the validity and feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Estimation of Urban V2G Carbon Emission Reduction Potential
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the face of the new challenges and opportunities brought to the power industry by the “carbon peaking and carbon neutrality” initiative, as well as the rapid development of the electric vehicle industry in Shanghai, V2G technology has demonstrated significant carbon reduction potential. This paper utilizes a unit commitment approach to establish a quantitative evaluation model for the carbon reduction potential resulting from electric vehicles participating in V2G in urban areas. Based on actual data from a certain city, the annual carbon emission reduction potential of the city is evaluated, showcasing the carbon reduction prospects of developing vehicle-grid interactive technology in the context of the rapid development of electric vehicles. This study provides high-quality decision support for the development of the electric vehicle industry in cities and the promotion of V2G technology.

articleTitle: Overview of the Development of Direct Current Transmission Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Under the ‘carbon peaking and carbon neutrality’ target, the construction of clean energy bases has made it an urgent demand for long-distance, high-capacity, and low-loss electricity transmission. After more than half a century of alternating current (AC) dominating the power system, the development of power electronics technology has allowed high-voltage direct current systems (HVDC) to solve the technical challenges of integrating large-capacity new energy sources into the grid. This has allowed direct current (DC) to once again take the center stage in history and gradually become an indispensable component of new type power systems. This article reviews the historical development of global DC transmission technology, summarizes the development history and current status of second-generation and third-generation DC transmission technology in China, and provides prospects for the future development of HVDC transmission technology,

articleTitle: Considering a Refined Power-to-Gas Model: A Robust Approach to Stochastic Optimal Dispatching in Integrated Electricity-Natural Gas Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The power grid faces numerous challenges due to the volatile increase in new energy sources. Power to gas facilities offer a solution by converting electricity into gas, thereby facilitating the development of an integrated electricity natural gas system and boosting the utilization of renewable energy locally. To address uncertainties in energy sources, we develop a sophisticated electricity-to-gas model that incorporates P2G technology. Subsequently, a robust optimization model is created for the integrated energy system, incorporating the refined P2G model. Through the analysis of calculation examples of different load scenarios and different models, we can conclude that P2G technology and robust optimization models can significantly improve system wind curtailment, and fully improve system economy and energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on State Sensing Technology for Substation Equipment Based on Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper designs a substation IoT architecture based on the state awareness requirements of substation main equipment, including the perception layer, network layer, platform layer, and application layer. Subsequently, the technical requirements of the perception layer and application layer of the substation IoT platform are analyzed, with a focus on introducing the technical means of implementing substation main equipment inspection substitution based on IoT technology.

articleTitle: Integrated Identification Method for Parameters of Doubly-Fed Wind Turbine Based on Frequency Domain Universal Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the proportion of wind power in new-type power systems increases year by year, its dynamic characteristics, especially fault ride-through characteristics, have a significant impact on power systems. To accurately analyze the impact of large-scale wind power on power systems, it is necessary to construct a white-box model that can characterize the actual dynamic characteristics of wind turbine. The white-box model has numerous parameters with interactive effects, and current parameter identification methods cannot achieve identification of the entire DFIG's fault ride-through, inner and outer controller parameters, limiting parameters, and electrical parameters, especially the accurate identification of parameters insensitive to external characteristics. To solve these problems, this paper constructs a frequency domain universal model for DFIG under fault ride-through conditions, which includes the DFIG itself and all controllers. The parameters are divided into four categories for step-by-step identification, proposing a categorized and integrated step-by-step identification method. The accuracy of the frequency domain universal model is verified through comparison with a simulation model, and the correctness of the proposed categorized and integrated step-by-step parameter identification method is validated by comparing the identified values with the real values.

articleTitle: Resilience-Oriented Optimal Allocation of Multi-Port Soft Open Point in Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To better withstand extreme events, it is of growing concern to build resilient distribution networks to restore power supply in a fast and timely manner after being damaged. Soft open point (SOP) is a new type of distribution equipment with excellent performance, especially multi-port SOP, which can improve the resilience of distribution networks. In this paper, considering the functional characteristics and operational boundaries of SOP, grid-related constraints, and the intensity of natural disaster attacks, a defense-attack-defense model with four-port SOP as the main power electronic switches, i.e., a resilience-oriented optimal allocation model, is proposed. The column-and-constraint (C&CG) generation algorithm is leveraged as the solution approach. The proposed model is tested in the IEEE 33-node system with set-up disaster scenarios, and the results show that the obtained four-port SOP allocation scheme has a better effect on the resilience enhancement of the distribution network.

articleTitle: Autoencoder and Kernel Density Estimation-Based Anomaly Detection Method for Power Consumption among Distribution Network Customers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Detecting anomalies in power consumption among distribution network customers is a critical aspect of maintaining the efficiency and reliability of distribution networks. Current research in anomaly detection primarily relies on user profile clustering, which involves subjective outlier detection-based criteria sensitive to input parameters, making it difficult to obtain objective and reasonable detection results. Therefore, in this work, an anomaly detection method for power consumption among distribution network customers based on autoencoder and kernel density estimation is proposed to objectively quantify anomaly levels. First, a processing method for load increment curves based on autoencoder and seasonal decomposition is proposed to detect abnormal patterns within these curves. Second, a quantification method for anomaly levels of power consumption based on kernel density estimation is proposed on the basis of the abnormal patterns detected, which enables the objective differentiation of anomaly levels among different customers and time periods. Finally, case studies on the actual load data from distribution networks are performed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed methods. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed methods can effectively detect anomalies in power consumption and objectively quantify anomaly levels among different customers in distribution networks.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling Strategy for Integrated Electric-Thermal-Gas Energy Systems Considering Multiple Types of Energy Storage Resources
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increase of the installed proportion of renewable power generation, in the context of the Energy Internet, the electric-thermal-gas integrated energy system can be effectively utilized for its multi-energy complementarity, thus enhancing energy efficiency and contributing to carbon peak and carbon neutrality. Optimal scheduling strategies for an electric- thermal-gas integrated energy system that considers multiple types of energy storage resources are investigated, aiming to reduce the operating cost, renewable energy curtailment, and carbon emission of integrated energy system. Firstly, operational models are developed for energy conversion devices as well as physical energy storage devices to improve the operating flexibility of integrated energy system. Secondly, the dynamic characteristics of the district heating network and natural gas network are explored, and virtual energy storage models considering integrated demand response are established to further explore the flexibility of the system.
