The performance of proposed strategy is theoretically analyzed from the aspect of dominant energy source and the effect of the capacity of energy storage. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy and the accuracy of the theoretical analysis of performance are verified by realtime simulation.

articleTitle: Resilience-Oriented Load Restoration Considering the Topology Transition Process
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With global climate change, the frequency of natural disasters increases. Network reconfiguration plays a critical pole in the load restoration. However, the topology transition process has not received much attention. Considering the transition process of network reconfiguration, this paper proposed a bi-level post-disaster distribution network restoration method to minimize the load lost and the voltage volatility. The transition process is modeled in this paper and the proposed method is formulated as a bi-level mixed integer linear programming model. A relaxation-based bi-level reformulation and decomposition algorithm is employed to achieve the optimal solution. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated on the IEEE 33 node system.

articleTitle: Few-shot Residential Load Forecasting Boosted by Learning to Ensemble
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Probabilistic forecasting can characterize the uncertainties and the dynamic trends of the future residential load, while massive data are required for popular forecasting methods. In this study, we consider probabilistic load forecasting for residential users who are only willing to provide limited data samples due to privacy concerns. To address this challenge, we analyze the characteristics of residential load and employ clustering-based few-shot learning methods to augment the data. Meanwhile, we combine different models, known as model ensemble, to further improve the performance. Compared with conventional ensemble methods using the linear combination, we adopt learning to ensemble, which captures the strengths of various models by learning the optimal nonlinear combination to avoid performance loss. We demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms conventional rivals theoretically and empirically. This method also sheds light on how varying the number of provided data can accommodate different privacy concerns.

articleTitle: Day-Ahead Optimal Dispatch in Active Distribution Network Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning with Improved Feature Extraction Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The access of renewable energy will challenge the economic and stable operation of active distribution network (AND). Based on the deep reinforcement learning algorithm, this paper proposes a multi-objective intelligent day-ahead optimal dispatch method for resources in distribution network. In the day-ahead optimal dispatch, the deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method is used to deal with the uncertainty of load and renewable resources. In order to achieve the economic operation of the distribution network and reduce the peak shaving pressure of the superior power grid, the regulation scheme of energy storage system and flexible load is formulated, and an improved feature extraction network is proposed to better deal with the problem of information redundancy. The effectiveness and superiority of this method are verified by an modified IEEE-33 example.

articleTitle: Forecasting Multivariate Loads of Integrated Energy Systems Based on LSTM and Weather Variables
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Multivariate loads short-term forecasting is a crucial prerequisite for the safe and stable operation and economic optimization management of Integrated Energy Systems (IES). Existing research has shown limited consideration for the interdependencies between electricity, cold and heat loads within the system, as well as the correlations between weather factors and load profiles. This paper employs the Spearman rank correlation coefficient to quantitatively analyze the relationships among weather data and the electricity, cold and heat loads, as well as the correlations among these different load types. The analysis results reveal the presence of strong relationships among various influencing factors and load categories. Building on these findings, this study introduces a comprehensive energy multivariate loads short-term forecasting model based on LSTM networks and compares its predictive accuracy with ANN and GRU models. Case study results indicate that the proposed model provides more precise load predictions, thus offering valuable insights for multivariate loads forecasting within IES.

articleTitle: Power Consumption Data Compression via Shift-Invariant Dictionary Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Prevalent smart meters are recording a vast amount of power consumption data. The escalation of data volume renders storing and transmitting costly. Traditional data compression techniques were effective solutions. However, they often neglect the pattern-rich and time-invariant properties of the power consumption data. To address this challenge, we propose a two-module pipeline, combined with shift-invariant dictionary learning (SIDL) and k-means clustering. Experimental results prove that the proposed pipeline attains the best effect in general cases. The results also imply that the pattern-rich and time-invariant properties are the key to efficiently handle the power consumption data.

articleTitle: Multiple Agent-Based Modeling and Analysis for Coupled Electricity and Carbon Market
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In response to the imperative climate objectives delineated by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the carbon emission market has been established as a pivotal mechanism to enforce emission limitations on electricity companies. In this paper, we propose a novel simulation and analysis method for the coupled electricity and carbon market that leverages the power of multi-agent-based modeling. Rec-ognizing the intricate inter-dependencies between the trading behavior of different types of entities in the electricity market and the carbon market, our method integrates these elements to provide a comprehensive view of unified m arket dynamics, and conditional generative adversarial networks (CGAN) are used to generate the bidding strategies of generators who participate in both electricity and carbon market. The proposed framework is tested using the IEEE-39 bus system. In this simulation system, different market participants' types and behavior patterns are examined to show the impact on the market outcomes. This study found that market participants' behavior diversity significantly affects their profit in these markets.

articleTitle: Short-Term Balance Operation Model Considering Flexible Loads in Power Systems with High Penetration Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the large-scale integration of renewable energy, the power development will present the system of renewable energy as the main body, a variety of renewable energy coordinated development trend, the characteristics of the power system will profoundly affect and even determine the operation mode of the power system. The double uncertainty of the source and load cause great challenges to the system operation. Flexible load regulation is an effective measure to alleviate the power supply shortage in peak periods. Compared with traditional regulation measure, flexible load has the advantages of fast response speed, low carbon and environmental protection. In this paper, a short term operation simulation model considering the coordination of various flexible loads is established by considering the short term regulation characteristics of transferable loads and interruptible loads. The validity of the proposed model is verified by the simulation of ROTS test system, the participation of flexible electric load in optimization scheduling can effectively reduce the peak-valley load difference, achieve the purpose of peak-valley cutting, effectively alleviate the power supply shortage problem during peak load period, and reduce system operating costs. Therefore, it has a obvious application effect.

articleTitle: Research on Testing Methods for Memory Data Abnormal Bit Flipping of Relay Protection Devices Under Radiation Impact
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: During operation, relay protection devices may be subjected to radiation from high-energy particles in the ground environment, resulting in memory data abnormal bit upset. This leads to the loss of critical data, abnormal program operation, functional failure, and incorrect operation of relay protection devices. This paper first analyzes the fault excitation mechanism and fault characteristics of memory data abnormal bit flipping in relay protection devices under radiation impact. Secondly, a flexible and portable software implement faults injection testing method for memory data abnormal bit flipping was designed. This is achieved through three steps: establishing a fault injection model, building a fault injection testing system, and conducting fault injection testing experiments. Finally, the testing method proposed in the paper was validated through experiments, proving its practicality and feasibility.

articleTitle: Static Voltage Stability Assessment of Distribution Grids with Massive Inverter Interfaced DGs Considering Transmission Grid Coupling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Developing a high proportion of renewable energy is the trend of future power system development. The evaluation deviation of traditional static voltage stability assessment increases due to the fluctuation of renewable energy sources and the impact of the dynamic characteristics of inverters. This paper aims to propose a new method which can reliably evaluate the static voltage stability of distribution grids with massive inverter interfaced DGs. The simulation results show that the proposed method is more accurate than traditional methods. In addition, it shows that the control coefficient of inverters has a significant impact on the static voltage stability of the system.

articleTitle: Multi-Temporal Flexibility Requirement Evaluation Considering the Correlation of Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the context of evolving energy infrastructure, the inexorable shift towards low carbonization is apparent. A prominent characteristic of future power systems will be the substantial integration of renewable energy sources, notably wind and solar power. These resources are inherently correlated to some extent, and ignoring this correlation could result in suboptimal decisions in power system optimization, scheduling, and planning. Additionally, prior research has introduced methodologies to evaluate power system flexibility requirement by examining mismatches. However, these approaches have primarily focused on assessing flexibility requirement based on predefined wind and solar profiles. This study generates multiple output scenarios that account for the interrelationship between wind and solar resources, and it quantifies changes in mismatch coefficients across various temporal scales, thus providing an analysis of how wind-solar correlations impact flexibility requirement. With heightened correlation levels resulting in increased system flexibility requirement, particularly in the context of short-term flexibility needs. We also conducted a sensitivity analysis on the wind-solar ratio. With the increase in wind-solar capacity ratio, flexibility requirements at various time scales show a trend of initially decreasing and then increasing. Specifically, at the daily time scale, the influence of the correlation coefficient on the mismatch coefficient exhibits the highest sensitivity to changes in wind-solar ratios.

articleTitle: Assessing the Value of Energy Storage Systems for Distribution Grid Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper the potential benefits t hat energy storage systems (ESS) can bring to distribution networks are analyzed. We propose an optimization model for the strategic allocation of ESS within a distribution system with photovoltaic (PV) generation, with the main focus on maximizing value benefits. A D istFlow formulation i s used for modeling t he AC power flow. The ESS model is based on a generic formulation that captures the charging and discharging modes' complementarity. The resulting optimization model is stated as a mixed-integer quadratically constrained program (MIQCP) problem. We evaluate the model on a modified 33-bus IEEE network considering renewable uncertainties. The obtained results show that ESS can offer various important benefits such a so verall system cost reduction, energy arbitrage, voltage profile improvement, and congestion management in distribution grids. These findings highlight the significance of utilizing ESS technologies to provide aggregated value through various grid services, extending beyond energy arbitrage alone.

articleTitle: Adaptability Study of Damping Control Strategies for Low-Frequency Oscillation in Power Grid with High Penetration of Photovoltaic
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The stability of power systems is experiencing significant challenges due to the increased penetration of photovoltaic (PV) and the complexity of the power grid. Given that PV plants are responsible for suppressing low-frequency oscillations (LFOs), damping control strategies working on PV must be broadly and adaptably adaptable. This paper discusses two types of power oscillation damping control (PODC) strategies, one based on a wide-area power differentiation signal (i.e. Strategy-A) and the other based on a local grid frequency signal (i.e. Strategy-B). A four-generator two-area system with high penetration of PV is employed to test the adaptability of the two strategies based on the PRONY algorithm. From the results, it is demonstrated that the two strategies can adapt to each PV integration location; when used at more locations, the strategies may combine to produce a synergy effect greater than the sum of its parts. The adaptive regularity of the damping control strategies has extensive significance for engineering reference.

articleTitle: Low Carbon Economic Dispatch of Integrated Energy System Based on Improved Stepped Incentive-Based Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: For the purpose of optimizing the scheduling strategy of the integrated energy system by exploit the potential of demand-side resources, and to realize carbon reduction and emission reduction while achieving economically efficient operation of integrated energy systems, this study constructs a model of the integrated energy system operation with an improved stepped incentive-based demand response mechanism and the model assigns commodity properties to carbon emissions. Firstly, this study establishes the corresponding mathematical models of gas turbine, gas boiler and two-stage power-to-gas conversion. Secondly, the stepped carbon trading(SCT) mechanism is introduced to constrain the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> generated by the system. Finally, the incentive-based demand response mechanism is introduced, and the particle swarm algorithm is used to improve the parameters of the demand response mechanism with the goal of minimizing the sum of all types of costs incurred in the operation of the system. The CPLEX solver is used to solve the linearly processed model, and it is verified that the proposed scheduling strategy is able to significantly reduce the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> generated by the system and operation cost of the system by setting up a variety of different cases for comparison.

articleTitle: Coordination Design of Parameters of Additional Multi-controller in the Wind-PV-Thermal-Bundled Power Transmission System under Multiple Operation Modes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The wind-PV-thermal-bundled (WPTB) power transmission system can remedy the shortcomings of new energy generation methods, but there are still low frequency oscillation (LFO) problems caused by the random fluctuation and strong intermittency of wind power output. In this paper, unified power flow controller (UPFC), power system stabilizer (PSS) and Static synchronous compensator (STATCOM) are used to improve the stability of the transmission grid power system. The Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) is used to sample the actual wind power output. The average value of damping ratio of the key oscillation mode of the system under various wind power output is considered an objective function, and the dung beetle optimization (DBO) algorithm is used to optimize the key parameters of multiple controllers. The eigenvalue analysis and time domain simulation results on IEEE 4-machine 2-area connected to WPTB power transmission system show that the controller optimized by DBO algorithm can suppress the fluctuation of active power and power angle caused by LFO, and improve the system stability.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling Method of PV-Hydrogen Energy Storage for Distribution Network Power Supply Reliability Improvement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Electricity is critical to the operation of modern society, and as global climate change and disaster events continue to increase, microgrids are playing an increasingly important role in disaster recovery. To ensure the timely recovery and reconstruction of disaster areas, this paper discuss the optimization methods and strategies of microgrids in post-disaster dispatch. It's main objective to ensure that critical load equipment is prioritized to ensure that emergency power needs can be met. To achieve this goal, a genetic algorithm-based post-disaster dispatching strategy is used in this paper. First, priority weights are added to the scheduling strategy to ensure that the power supply priority. Additionally, hydrogen and supercapacitors are introduced to microgrids to enhance fast response in energy storage. The simulation results are used to verify that the distributed energy and energy storage systems can better meet the power demand of critical loads in the disaster area and reduce the pressure on the power system during the recovery process. Finally, two typical scenarios are used to test the proposed dispatching strategy, demonstrate that the strategy can be effectively applied to the post-disaster dispatching of the power grid and that the addition of hydrogen energy can enhance the resilience of the microgrid.

articleTitle: Joint Strategic Bidding for Iron-and-Steel Enterprises in Electricity and Carbon Markets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Iron-and-steel enterprises (ISEs) take vital roles in modern society. However, high electricity prices and strict carbon emission caps greatly influence the profitability of ISEs. To bridge this gap, this paper investigates the joint bidding strategy for ISEs in electricity and carbon markets considering detailed industrial processes. Firstly, the material-electricity-carbon flow model is proposed to capture the electricity consumption and carbon emission characteristics of the industrial processes. Then, the strategic bidding model of ISE is constituted as a bi-level model, in which the upper-level models the optimal bidding of ISE, and the clearing of the carbon and power markets are represented by two lower-level problems. Towards a computationally efficient solution method, the lower-level problem of electricity market clearing is equivalently reformulated by its KKT condition. The strong duality theorem and the big-M method are used to linearize the bi-linear terms. Finally, the bi-level model is transformed into a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) problem. And the IEEE 30-node case is used to validate the effectiveness and computational efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Standard System of Medium and Low Voltage DC Distribution System in Regional Energy Internet
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Medium and low voltage DC power distribution is the key technology to support the access and consumption of clean energy. After the exploration of research and demonstration projects in recent years, the standardization of medium and low voltage DC power distribution technology has accumulated some achievements. In order to effectively support the construction of energy Internet and serve as a useful supplement to the standard system of new distribution system, it is urgent to construct the standard system of medium and low voltage DC distribution system in regional energy Internet. Fully considering the technical development and business needs, the construction principles of systematic, coordinated, open and extensible standard system are put forward. The standard system architecture of medium and low voltage DC distribution system covering the whole life cycle is designed from three levels: basic general, equipment and facilities, and system level. According to the key development direction, the standard requirements and layout are put forward. It provides technical support for the development of regional energy Internet and the realization of green low-carbon transformation.

articleTitle: Sheath Loss Calculation and Loss Reduction Analysis of 220 kV Cable System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Reducing loss in high-voltage cable transmission lines is crucial to improve the power transmission efficiency of the power systems. This paper reports a method for calculating sheath loss in the sheath cross-bonded cable systems. Subsequently, a 220 kV, three-phase, single-core, cross-bonded cable system is used as a simulation case in PSCAD-EMTP to investigate the sheath loss under different subsection's lengths and cable arrangements. The calculations indicate that in the case of a uniform arrangement, the sheath loss is minimized and approaches zero when each subsection is of equal length. Furthermore, in the case of mixed arrangement, the sheath loss is affected by both the lengths and arrangements of cable subsections. The sheath loss can be reduced by approximately 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> to 19% compared to subsections of equal length by selecting the appropriate length ratio and arrangement depending on the cable operating conditions.

articleTitle: Multi-Dimensional Wind Power Low-Power Event Identification Based On Variational Mode Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Accurate identification of wind power low-power events is of great significance for subsequent low-power prediction work, power system power supply capability and the safe and stable operation of the power grid. In order to effectively identify wind power low-power events, this paper proposes a multidimensional wind power low-power event identification method based on variational mode decomposition. This paper focuses on low-power events of wind farm groups whose average output is less than 10% of the rated output and lasts more than 24 hours. Firstly, the original power data is subjected to variational mode decomposition to obtain the low-frequency state mode components. The possible low-power event intervals are screened out by setting thresholds for this mode and corresponding to the original power fluctuations. Based on a window size variable sliding window method, combined with multidimensional parameters such as average value, extreme value, and duration, possible low-power events are accurately identified. Case analysis shows that this method can effectively identify low-power events of wind farm groups that meet the target conditions, and effectively distinguish low-power events from other output levels.

articleTitle: Analysis of the 500kV Line Arrester Exploion Accident
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper introduces an explosion accident of a 500kV line arrester. The whole fault process is deduced according to the fault recording diagram and the correctness of the fault process is verified by simulation calculation. Finally, it is concluded that the explosion fault of lightning arrester is caused by the multiple lightning shocks in a short time, accumulation effect of long-term thermal aging and the increase of power frequency voltage caused by reclosing. It is suggested that the live detection and operation inspection of the line should be strengthened.

articleTitle: Resident Carbon Credit Incentive Decision-Making Method to Promote Valley Filling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Establishing a reasonable, feasible, and directional incentive carbon points operation model for residents is an effective means to enhance the low-carbon awareness of residents. This paper introduces dynamic carbon emission factors and power characteristics of carbon valley, and a carbon credit-oriented incentive decision-making method for residents to promote valley filling is proposed. Firstly, based on the carbon quota allocation model, considering three factors: monthly carbon quotas, basic carbon emission and incentive carbon credits, a residential carbon credits-oriented incentive model is proposed to promote carbon valley filling. Secondly, the carbon valley electricity consumption ratio is established, and the K-means algorithm is used to cluster residents. Then, considering the constraints, such as the average monthly carbon credits of residents, the proportion of below-zero credit residents and difference between the mean carbon credits of different clusters, a resident carbon credit decision-making model is constructed, and the Grey Wolf Optimization is utilized to solve it. Finally, a numerical example is given to verify the rationality and target incentive of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Simulation of Flexibility Resources Development Trends Based on System Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the rapid growth of renewable energy, the demand for flexibility in power systems is increasing, and analyzing the development trends of various flexibility resources are of great significance. This paper uses system dynamics methods to deeply study three key flexibility resources: coal power flexibility transformation, pumped storage, and electrochemical storage. By setting different development paths for the power system, we conduct simulation predictions of the future development trends of flexibility resources and comparative studies.

articleTitle: Research on the Reliable Capacity of Renewable Energy in the Distribution Network Considering Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing environmental problems caused by economic development, the energy transition is urgent. Renewable energy represented by wind energy and solar energy has become the primary choice due to its advantages of wide distribution, less pollution, and renewability. When the proportion of renewable energy in the distribution network increases, the reliability of the system can be improved. But at the same time, these renewable energy sources also have strong randomness and volatility, and their unstable output may cause safety problems. Therefore, it is necessary to evaluate their reliable capacity. To solve this problem, this paper first fits the uncertainty output of photovoltaic and wind power based on the beta distribution and Weibull distribution, then establishes the reliability evaluation model of the distribution network based on the sequential Monte Carlo method, and then proposes a reliable capacity evaluation method for renewable energy power generation by using the Secant Method. Finally, the feasibility analysis is carried out using the IEEE33 node example.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid Model for Medium-Term Wind Power Forecast Using WDlinear, LightGBM, and Kalman Filtering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As an essential renewable energy source, the fast-growing penetration of wind power over the past decades has played an essential role in both industrial and domestic spheres. Nevertheless, the stochastic nature of wind results in pronounced volatility and intermittent behavior in wind power generation, posing a significant challenge to its widespread deployment. Consequently, precise short and medium-term wind power generation predictions can significantly enhance wind power generation systems' management, allocation, and overall stability of the power system. To achieve the above goal, this paper presents a hybrid model combining WDlinear and lightGBM methodologies, then applying Kalman filtering to obtain the final prediction results. The experimental outcomes demonstrate the superior predictive performance of the proposed hybrid model compared to the baseline models when forecasting 7-day wind power generation. Furthermore, the hybrid model exhibits noteworthy traits of precision and stability across various data scenarios, affirming its efficacy and superiority.

articleTitle: Load Forecasting of 110kV Power Transformer based on Customer Maximum Capacity Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Achieving maximum capacity refers to the state that the customer operates at full capacity. Achieving maximum capacity is an important indicator in the field of industry, commercial and service industry which required a large amount of electricity supply. This paper proposes an incremental load forecasting model for rural 110kV power transformer based on customer maximum capacity model. Firstly, the historical electricity consumption data of different industries in Changsha in year 2010–2023 were collected. Then, the rules of various customers reaching maximum capacity were analyzed. The least squares method was used for simulating the load incremental model. In the case study section, maximum capacity model were established using Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm based on three typical industries.

articleTitle: A Classification Method for Electricity Users Based on the LightGBM Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Providing customized services for different users is of great significance in the development process of smart grids. In order to classify electricity users more accurately, based on GBDT algorithm, the lightgbm model was used to classify users. The preprocessed dataset was used to train the lightgbm model, and bayesian methods were used to optimize the hyperparameters of lightbgm. The experimental result shows that the final lightgbm model has a significantly higher prediction accuracy than other models, and can effectively achieve user classification tasks.

articleTitle: An Modulation Method for Improving Output Characteristics of Medium-/Low-Voltage MMCs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Modular multilevel converters (MMCs) suffer from low output level and high harmonic distortion in medium-/low-voltage applications such as DC distribution networks. In order to address the above issues, a modulation method for improving output characteristics is proposed in this paper, which the output level number is multiplied for medium-/low-voltage MMCs by introducing a step wave correction. MATLAB/Simulink simulation results are carried out to verify the effectiveness of the presented method.

articleTitle: Fine-Scale Simulation Technique for Summer High-Temperature Weather Based on Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to address the issues that the summer high-temperature season offers to power systems and energy management in order to enhance the financial and operational performance of the power system. To achieve this objective, we introduce a series of innovative fine-scale simulation methods for summer high-temperature weather. These techniques include (A) a generative adversarial network (GAN) and long short-term memory (LSTM)-based random weather simulation of summer high-temperature weather, (B) a random weather simulation of summer high-temperature weather based on gated recurrent unit (GRU) and GAN, (C) a random weather simulation of summer high-temperature weather for specific months using conditional generative adversarial network (CGAN), and (D) a simulation of typical scenarios for summer high-temperature weather based on semi-supervised learning. Method A, by combining LSTM and GAN, aims to improve time-series modeling for a more accurate representation of high-temperature weather conditions, emphasizing the modeling of temporal dependencies. Method B introduces the combination of GRU and GAN to explore performance in high-temperature weather simulation when faster training and generation speeds are required. Method C utilizes CGAN to generate weather data for specific months or seasons, enhancing the spatiotemporal consistency of simulation results. Method D, employing semi-supervised learning techniques, effectively leverages limited labeled data and unlabeled data to enhance the performance of high-temperature weather simulation. The integrated application of these methods is poised to provide the power system and energy management field with more accurate, diverse, and reliable summer high temperature weather simulation data, offering robust support for the economic and operational efficiency of the power system under high-temperature conditions.

articleTitle: A Unified State Model-Based Approach for Cooperative Voltage Regulation of Multiple DSRs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With distributed generation based on renewable energy connecting to the network, the voltage of the distribution network will exceed the limit and fluctuate. DSRs are flexible and efficient resources for demand-side response, and can be used to smooth the voltage fluctuation curve. However, how to reasonably schedule multiple DSRs is a serious challenge. To solve this problem. A unified state model of DSRs is proposed to describe the characteristics of different resources. Then power control matrix is derived, and the response order and comfort level are introduced to control ES, EV and TCL. Finally, the response level of DSRs is regulated to reduce the fluctuation of system voltage. The simulation results show that under the proposed voltage regulation strategy, the distributed resources can reduce the voltage fluctuation and stabilize the voltage fluctuation level through response. The coordinated scheduling of multiple distributed resources can improve the voltage curve more effectively than the single distributed resource scheduling.

articleTitle: Prediction of Dissolved Gases Concentration in Transformer Oil Based on VMD and ELM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Effective prediction of dissolved gases in transformer oil serves as a crucial foundation for diagnosing faults and issuing early warnings for power transformers. In this paper, we propose a dissolved gas concentration prediction model in oil based on variational modal decomposition (VMD) and extreme learning machine (ELM). Firstly, the original oil dissolved gas concentration sequence is decomposed by variational modal decomposition to obtain a number of relatively smooth sub-sequences; secondly, the extreme learning machine model is used to establish different prediction models for each sub-sequence; in conclusion, the prediction outcomes of each sub-sequence are combined to derive the prediction results for the original gas concentration sequence. The exemplar outcomes demonstrate that the model, employing variational modal decomposition and the extreme learning algorithm, yields a root mean square error of 0.327 and an average absolute percentage error of 2.71. In comparison with the prediction outcomes of other models, it is evident that the method introduced in this paper exhibits higher prediction accuracy and better capability to forecast the concentration of dissolved gas in the oil.

articleTitle: Gas Sensing Performance of Composite MOS2@CMOF to Li-ion Battery Off-Gas C2H4
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> is the early gas released in the process of thermal runaway of lithium-ion battery, and the occurrence of thermal runaway can be warned by detecting C2H4 gas. To detect C2H4 gas, we obtained a composite gas sensing material by in situ synthesis of Cu3(hhtp)2 (cmof) on the Mos2surface. X-ray diffraction (XRD), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) were used to characterize the structure, morphology and chemical composition of the samples and the gas sensitivity of the composite to C2H4 gas at room temperature was discussed. The results show that the MOS2@CMOF sensor has a high sensitivity (37.66% at 100ppm) and a very low detection limit (theoretical: 80.27ppb) to ethylene gas. Indicating that the gas sensitive material has the potential to detect ethylene gas in lithium ion batteries and can guide the development of practical early warning gas sensors.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Optimal Power Flow Method for HVAC/DC Systems Considering Wind Power Correlation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the volatility and randomness of wind power, the wind power integration has an impact on the safe and stable operation of high voltage alternative/direct current systems (HVAC/DC), it is necessary to extend the probabilistic optimal power flow method to be applicable to HVAC/DC systems. This paper proposes a probabilistic optimal power flow method for a HVAC/DC system penetrated with correlated wind power. Firstly, the DC line and VSC are modelled as special components of an AC system, to which an AC optimal power flow model can be applied. Copula function is used as the joint probability distribution to describe the correlation between multiple wind farms. Based on the fitting Copula function, scenarios are generated to typify the wind power, and K-means clustering is utilized to obtain a small number of scenarios for the sake of relieving computation burden. Finally, an HVAC/DC test system with 14 buses is employed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Evaluation Method of Static Voltage Stability of Renewable Energy Farm Based on Sufficient Conditions of Power Flow Insolvability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the current limit and other factors, the voltage support capacity of new energy is weak, the static voltage stability risk of the station is high, and the existing analysis results are lack of intuition. In this paper, a static voltage stability analysis method of renewable energy farm based on the sufficient conditions of power flow solution is proposed to judge the existence and voltage stability of the power flow solution of renewable energy farm by solving the minimum voltage amplitude of the equilibrium node of the power grid outside the renewable energy farm. Firstly, by analyzing the static voltage stability problem of single-machine infinite system, the influence of the external voltage amplitude of the voltage source converter (VSC) on the maximum transmission power is analyzed using the analytical solution of the minimum voltage of the balance node. Secondly, for the static voltage stability problem of the radial multi-machine system, the DistFlow power flow model and its convex relaxation form are used to calculate the lower limit of the external power grid balance node voltage amplitude to determine the static voltage stability margin. The proposed method can provide the minimum equivalent voltage amplitude of the external power grid to maintain the stability of the static voltage of the renewable energy farm. In actual operation, the static voltage stability of the system can be efficiently evaluated by comparing the equivalent voltage of the external power grid with the calculated minimum equivalent voltage.

articleTitle: Multi-Physical Field Simulation Study of High Voltage Converter Valve Saturated Reactor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the core equipment of the UHVDC converter valve, the saturable reactor is responsible for eliminating the harmonics caused by the converter valve and improving the system reliability and stability. The vibration sound generated during the operation of the saturated reactor contains a lot of information, which can reflect the operating state of the saturated reactor to a large extent. It is of great significance to carry out effective simulation of the saturated reactor, and has guiding significance for the state evaluation of the saturated reactor and the safe operation of the converter valve. In this paper, the generation and propagation of the acoustic signal of the saturated reactor core are studied, and a multi-physical field simulation model based on COMSOL is proposed. Then, the vibration test of saturated reactor under high frequency pulse excitation is carried out. The correctness of the simulation model is verified by comparing the experimental data with the simulation data, and the effectiveness of the technology is verified.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Cascaded UHVDC Transmission System at Sending End for High Proportion of Renewable Energy Delivery
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: A scheme of sending end VSC (self-commutation and flexible control)-LCC (low cost, high capacity and strong short-time overload capability) hybrid cascaded UHVDC for delivery of ultra-high-proportion renewable energy had been proposed in this paper. Based on this scheme, the advantages of VSC and LCC can be integrated to realize the multi-time scale dynamic reactive power response and strong virtual inertia response on the sending end as well as the high-frequency wide-range adjustment of active power. The proposed scheme is a possible solution to the issues of static voltage stability, transient over-voltage and low inertia, which are commonly regarded as the main challenges for the delivery of ultra-high-proportion renewable energy with an inevitable weak AC grid. As a result, the capacity requirements of synchronous condenser or STATCOM on sending-end could be reduced significantly with the proposed scheme. The topology and control strategies of this scheme had been explained thoroughly. The superior performance of the proposed scheme has been validated by EMT simulation under various typical operation conditions.

articleTitle: A PI Consensus-Based Second Control for P/V Droop-Controlled Converters in Low-Voltage Resistive Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Droop control is widely used to achieve desired power sharing among distributed generations (DGs). For low-voltage resistive network, P/V droop control is preferred rather than the conventional droop. However, P/V droop also suffers from inaccurate active power allocation and deviation of voltage and frequency from rated values induced by inequal line impedance and its inherent defects. A PI-consensus based secondary controller is hereby proposed for the P/V droop control to address these problems. With the effect of PI-consensus algorithm, the deviations of voltage and frequency are minimized, and the active power of DGs reach a consensus, achieving desired power allocation. Simulations are conducted to verify the effectiveness and the robustness of the proposed second control in an islanded low-voltage resistive power system. Besides, an experiment is carried out to further validate its efficacy.

articleTitle: Joint Planning of Energy Storage and Distribution System Considering Network Reconfiguration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the mass access of distributed generation (DG) and the increase of load level, the scale and network topology of distribution system need to be expanded and adjusted urgently. Energy storage (ES) system configuration and network reconfiguration can improve the source-load consumption capacity and operation flexibility of distribution systems. However, the previous researches on distribution system joint planning didn't take network reconfiguration as a planning option due to the complexity of the models and the large number of variables involved. In this paper, a mixed integer linear programming (MILP) joint planning model of ES and distribution system is proposed, which takes the minimization of present value of the annualized total investment as the optimization objective, considers topology, construction, and operation constraints. The IEEE 24-node distribution system is used to verify the effectiveness of the brought joint planning model, while cases of no ES configuration, no network reconfiguration are introduced. The case studies verify that ES access and network reconfiguration has the effect of delaying the expansion of distribution system, improving the grid's loadability, and the total cost of case reconfigurable network with ES can be significantly reduced compared with other cases.

articleTitle: An Accurate Power Balance Analysis and Improved Design Method of the High Orbit Communication Satellites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The power balance analysis of the high orbit satellites determines the configuration of the satellite power subsystem, which directly affects the weight of the power subsystem and even the load to interference ratio of the entire platform. The refined energy balance analysis method proposed in this paper, basis on the existing energy balance analysis based on the maximum load, this paper gives multi angle suggestions on the determination of the satellite in orbit load model, so as to achieve more accurate power design; On the other hand, in combination with the actual operating conditions in orbit, an improved design method of energy balance is proposed for the existing energy system design and the current actual load of the satellite. That is, the energy imput is reduced by adjusting the actual solar incidence angle, and the power margin is controlled within a reasonable range, thus reducting the impact of power over design on the power supply system and power transmission path, it provides a important reference for the energy balance analysis and design of high orbit satellites.

Author Keywords: the actual operating conditions in orbit

articleTitle: Harmonic State-Space Based Hybrid AC/DC D-Q Admittance Model of MMC
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Modular multilevel converters (MMCs) play a vital role in the formation of hybrid AC/DC power system. Despite their numerous advantages, however, impacted by the unique admittance characteristics, the wide-band oscillations occur more common recently. To address this issue and properly investigate the admittance characteristics of MMCs, this manuscript establishes the hybrid AC/DC admittance model in the dq synchronous reference frame with the harmonic state-space (HSS) method. Compared with the conventional AC and DC admittance models, the hybrid AC/DC admittance model offers salient features as follows: 1) it stays immune to the variation of the AC and DC grid admittances; 2) it simultaneously portrays the AC and DC side admittance characteristics and describes the self-admittances with its main-diagonal elements; and 3) it thoroughly captures the coupling interaction between the AC and DC sides and expresses the coupling interaction with its off-diagonal elements. Based on the aforementioned advantages, the hybrid AC/DC admittance model can analyze the stability of system more comprehensively. Finally, the consistence of the theoretical results and simulation results proves the accuracy of the proposed hybrid AC/DC admittance model.

articleTitle: Typical Scenario Generation Method for Integrated Energy Systems Considering Spatio-Temporal Properties
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Integrated energy system (IES) involves a variety of energy data with large differences in characteristics and complex spatio-temporal characteristics, in order to solve the uncertainty of new energy output in IES and the arithmetic difficulties caused by large-scale scene set, this paper proposes a typical scene generation method for IES considering spatio-temporal characteristics. First, the temporal and distributional characteristics of wind and solar power are analyzed respectively. Then, based on the Monte Carlo sampling method, combined with wind power and photovoitaic power generation models, the generation of wind-scenery scenes is realized. Further, the scene was cut down using the synchronized back generation elimination method. The effectiveness of the generated typical scenes was evaluated by establishing an evaluation index system. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method are confirmed through a case analysis, which is of great significance for the planning, decision-making and optimization of IES.

articleTitle: Design of a Low-Noise Multi-Range Broadband Front-End Amplifier for MEMS Electric Field Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The practical application of Microelectromechanical system (MEMS) electric field sensors is limited due to several issues, including low sensitivity, narrow measurement range, and limited frequency range. This article introduces a fully differential CMOS preamplifier design for MEMS micro DC electric field sensors, and proposes a new multi-range charge sensing amplifier that eases the trade-off between gain, bandwidth and noise. Using the XFAB-H035 process and a folded cascode amplifier with a gain boosting structure, a low-noise, high DC gain and wide-band operational amplifier is designed.

articleTitle: Power Coordinated Control of Multi-Port Electric Energy Router Based on VSG Adaptive Parameter Tuning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The electric energy router plays a crucial role in the field of the energy internet by facilitating the seamless integration of renewable energy sources and enabling flexible power conversion. This paper focuses on the circuit topology and operational control of the electric energy router. Firstly, we present the topology structure of the electric energy router. Building upon this foundation, we propose a control strategy that enhances the power router's frequency support capability to the main power grid through the implementation of virtual synchronous generator control on the AC-side port, along with adaptive control parameter tuning. Finally, we demonstrate the application of the electric energy router in a photovoltaic energy storage DC microgrid. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed control methods, a model is constructed using the MATLAB/Simulink simulation platform.

articleTitle: Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm Based Fault Repair Method for Distribution Network under Natural Disaster
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to minimize power losses caused by natural disaster, improve the repair efficiency of the repair crews and increase the load recovery of power system at the same time, a decision-making method for fault repair considering emergency repair resources and crews distribution under typhoons disaster is proposed. The method proposes a post-disaster fault repair model that includes disaster mechanism analysis and power system repair scheduling. First, coding the type and extent of damage to power system equipment under typhoon disaster, and summarizing the locations of failure points, resource depots and the amount of material, and the location of repair crews in the preliminary model of disaster-resource. Furthermore, the actual repair process is built as a nonlinear model with the minimum power loss as the objective function, and the artificial bee colony algorithm is used to obtain the optimal plan for the amount of materials carried by the repair crews and the routes of travel. This model can realize the minimum power loss while improving repair efficiency and reducing resource waste. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated with the modified IEEE 33-node distribution test system.

articleTitle: Implementing a Smart Irrigation System using IoT Technology to Achieve Saudi's Green Ambition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the global rise in population and the consequential surge in demand for agricultural products, efficient water management has become imperative to sustain agricultural practices. In arid regions like Saudi Arabia, where water scarcity poses a significant challenge to agriculture, adopting smart irrigation systems integrated with Internet of Things (IoT) technology emerges as a promising solution. This study explores the implementation of a Smart Irrigation System (SIS) utilizing IoT technology to align with Saudi Arabia's ambitious goals of environmental sustainability and agricultural self-sufficiency. Methods: The proposed system uses a microprocessor that leverages IoT devices such as soil moisture sensors, salinity sensors, ultrasonic sensors, water pumps, and automated actuators to create an intelligent, data-driven irrigation framework. Real-time data from these sensors were collected and analysed using algorithms to determine precise irrigation requirements based on factors like soil moisture levels, weather conditions, and crop types. By integrating IoT technology, the system facilitates remote monitoring and control through a userfriendly interface accessible via smartphones or computers. This seamless integration of digital technologies optimizes water usage, reduces wastage, and enhances overall agricultural productivity. The prototype explained the methods trial data were collected and the results are promising. Also, the statistical analysis was achieved. Results: The proposed system displays data from moisture and TDS soil sensors. The ultrasonic distance sensor detects the water level in a tank, and the pump waters the plants when the soil moisture is low. Finally, an IoT module was integrated with these sensors to send notifications wirelessly via Wi-Fi or GSM to the user or farmer. The system can control and monitoring in real time. ANOVA statistical analysis indicates a significant difference with p <.05 in the correlations between salinity, TDS, moisture, and water respectively. measurements. That means the study can have success if applied on a larger scale. Conclusion: The project represents a transformative approach toward achieving Saudi Arabia's green ambition. By harnessing the power of data-driven decision-making, this innovative solution not only addresses the pressing issue of water scarcity but also fosters sustainable agriculture, economic growth, and environmental preservation, thus paving the way for a greener and more prosperous future and in line with the Kingdom Vision 2030.

articleTitle: A Fault Branch Location Approach for Partially Observable Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: A large number of distributed generations (DGs) has been integrated into distribution network, which makes the fault features much more complicated compared with traditional distribution network. At the same time, the observation capability of distribution network is limited due to the expensive measurement deployment costs, bringing significant challenges for fault location. To tackle this issue, this paper has proposed an accurate fault branch location method for distribution networks with massive DGs by a few measurements placed in the system. Based on the traditional fault location method, an improved feature is designed as the input of the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), which uses the voltage value of the distribution network without collecting waveform data. Taking the cost function of CNN as the optimization goal, a measurement placement algorithm is proposed to improve performance. Simulation results based on IEEE 39-bus power system model show that the proposed method performs well for four common types of faults, even if few measurements are placed.

articleTitle: A Power Data Generation Method Based on CNN-LSTM-GAN for Cable Transmission Line Assessment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: At present, the quality of feature data collected through cable transmission lines needs to be improved. There are insufficient credible data samples that can support project review technology analysis and research, which limits the development and application of data-driven smart cable transmission line review technologies. Based on this, this article uses the convo-lutional neural network(CNN), long short-term memory(LSTM) and generative adversarial network(GAN) model to solve the problems of missing power data and insufficient number of samples in the cable transmission line review scenario. First, we use convolutional neural network and long short-term memory to finish the missing power data restoration. Then, based on the completed data set, generative adversarial network is used to generate power data. Finally, the effectiveness of the CNN-LSTM-GAN model was verified by taking the power data in real cable transmission line review as an example. The results show that the data generated by this method has high accuracy, which helps to accurately draw load curves and solve project review difficulties.

articleTitle: D-Vine Copula Based Spatial Correlation Characterization for Capacity Credit Assessment of Wind and PV Power
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the share of renewable energy in the power system increases, the risk of inadequate load supply also rises. Therefore, the concept of capacity credit (CC) is introduced to reflect the power supply capability of generation resources in the field of power planning. Accurate assessment of CC relies on reasonable reconstruction of wind and photovoltaic (PV) power output scenarios. In this paper, a method for modeling the spatial correlation of output from multiple wind farms and photovoltaic power stations based on D-vine copula is proposed. Moreover, an efficient interpolation method for CC assessment using D-vine copula sampling is introduced. Numerical experiments are designed based on two wind farms and two photovoltaic power stations in a real power system in China, demonstrating the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed model. Furthermore, we analyzes various factors that influence combined CC of wind and PV power.

articleTitle: Parameter Design Method for Surge Arrester Coordinating Action in 66 kV Power Grid Based on Intermittent Arc Overvoltage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In Northeast China, 66 kV power systems are widely distributed. This paper introduces an explosion accident of a lightning arrester, which is installed on the 66 kV neutral point of No.1 main transformer in a 220 kV substation, resulting in the tripping of the main transformer. According to the accident scene, fault oscillogram analysis and simulation calculation, it is found that the accident is mainly due to the improper selection of the 66 kV neutral surge arrester. When a long-lasting and high-frequency single-phase intermittent arc grounding fault occurs on 66kV overhead transmission line, the recurring transient overvoltage on the 66 kV neutral point of the main transformer induces frequent actions of the neutral surge arrester, causing the thermal collapse and explosion of the arrester. Eventually, it further leads to the tripping of the main transformer. The fault is severely enlarged. Aiming at this fault and the confusion at present in the selection of neutral arrester in 66 kV system, this paper puts forward a new parameter design method of neutral arrester in 66 kV power grid considering the protection coordination relationship with phase arrester, which can improve the operation reliability of arresters in 66 kV system on the premise of ensuring electrical equipment insulation coordination.

articleTitle: Forecasting Combined Electricity-Heat-Cooling-Gas Loads in the Integrated Energy System Based on Multi-Task Learning and Transformers Models
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The electricity-heat-cooling-gas (EHCG) loads forecasting is an important prerequisite for the safe and stable operation and economic optimization management of integrated energy system (IES). A new method combining multitask learning (MTL) and Transformers models was proposed for EHCG loads forecasting in the IES in this paper. The MTL model can study the complicated correlated information of combined EHCG loads in the IES, and the Transformers model can effectively identify the GHCG loads correlated-based rule. An industrial park IES in North China was treated as a case, and the forecasting results shows the MTL-Transformers-based hybrid method holds the best forecasting performance compared with that of ARIMA, LSTM, LSSVM, CNN-BiGRU and Transformers without multitask learning model. The proposed EHCG loads forecasting method is effective in this paper.

articleTitle: Short-Term Load Forecasting Method Based on VMD-MLP-TCN
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the traditional power load forecasting model has low prediction accuracy for short-term time series, this paper proposes a power load forecasting model based on variational mode decomposition (VMD) combined with multilayer perceptron (MLP) and time convolution network (TCN). Firstly, in order to improve the anti-noise performance, the original load sequence is decomposed by variational mode decomposition, and the number of modes is determined by Pearson coefficient method (PCC). Then, the decomposed modal components are extracted by MLP to extract the backbone features. Finally, the features of each modal component are input into the TCN model to obtain the final predicted value. Experiments are carried out on the public transport load data of a typical city in Zhejiang Province, and the prediction results are compared with other models.

articleTitle: Autoformer Based Electricity Market Price Forecasting for Risk Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In an electricity market, trading frequency is high and the spot price fluctuation range is large. Improving the forecast level of spot price is conducive to operate the electricity market smoothly, and assists market players to formulate reasonable trading strategies to maximize their benefits. Combined with the data characteristics of spot market and the feature of an Autoformer can process long-period data, this paper builds a forecast model of spot price on the basis of the Autoformer. The proposed model can simplify the spot price forecast of input processing, realize the input of raw data, and output the forecast result, which greatly facilitates the application of spot price forecast. The Autoformer model has the characteristics of deep learning and has better prediction ability of long-period time series data. Based on the actual transaction data of electricity spot in the PJM market and compared with four other neural network models, the prediction results show that the model has a better prediction effect and can be directly applied to the field of spot prices.

articleTitle: Demand Side Load Forecasting Method Based on STL-RFE and DeepAR Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to ensure the stable operation of the power grid, accurate power load forecasting must be carried out. The power load data has obvious time series characteristics and is affected by a variety of nonlinear factors, resulting in a high degree of randomness. In order to improve the prediction accuracy of power load, a demand side load forecasting method based on STL (Seasonal and Trend decomposition using Loess) - RFE (Recursive Feature Elimination) and DeepAR (Deep Autoregressive) model is proposed in this paper. This paper first normalizes the historical data, then processes the abnormal data through STL decomposition to expand the data set, and uses RFE to screen the feature data set to form the best feature combination. Finally, the DeepAR model is used to predict the load power and evaluate the results. Based on the typical demand side load sample data of a park, this paper predicts the adjustable load in this area. Compared with the single DeepAR model, the STL-RFE and DeepAR models can effectively improve the accuracy of load forecasting. Compared with other models, the RMSE of the prediction results is reduced by at least 0.0158, the MAE is reduced by at least 0.0147, and the MAPE is reduced by at least 1.4473 %.

articleTitle: A Reliability Evaluation Model for Dual Relay Protection System Considering Environmental Factors Classification and Defect Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Environmental factors such as temperature, electromagnetic fields, and cosmic rays can affect the reliability of relay protection systems. Thus, for dual-unit protections operating in the same environment, the occurrence of defects is not mutually independent; there exists a phenomenon of defect accumulation. Ignoring the influence of environmental factors and defect aggregation can lead to inaccurate reliability assessment. To improve the accuracy of the reliability assessment for the dual-unit, this paper proposes a reliability assessment model for dualized relay protection systems considering environmental factor classification (EFC) and defect aggregation phenomena (DAP). In detail, first, the problems with traditional models in the reliability assessment of dualized relay protection systems are analyzed. Secondly, considering the phenomenon of defect accumulation in dualized relay protection systems, an eight-state Markov model that considering the EFC is established, and the probability of defects occurring in the dualized relay protection system under this model is derived. Finally, the accuracy of the proposed model is verified through model comparison.

articleTitle: Decoupling-based Withdrawal Scheme to Enhance Resilience of Multi-agent Energy Storage Systems under Contingencies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Renewable energies (RENs) are growing as never before due to climate concerns. Energy storage system (ESS) is regarded as a promising solution to help the power grid integrate RENs. However, the ESS is increasingly evolving into cyber-physical deeply coupled systems that are vulnerable to cyber-physical security risks. In this paper, we consider potential contingency in the ESS, and formulate the contingency problem by combining the characteristic of cyber-physical interactions. On this basis, it is revealed that a contingency at the physical layer may cause wrong information misleadings at the cyber layer, which can in turn lead to the normal energy storage devices in the ESS being out of control. Furthermore, we develop a decoupling-based withdrawal scheme to guarantee the normal operation of the whole ESS, even under contingency. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed scheme is verified in case studies. Results show that a physical-layer contingency can cause topology decomposition, which can further result in the failure of the ESS to provide flexibility services to the power grid. While with the proposed scheme, all remaining energy storage devices in the ESS can still operate normally, despite the contingency in some devices. Therefore, the proposed scheme contributes to the enhancement of the resilience of ESS.

articleTitle: Modeling of Distributed Photovoltaic Interactive Communication Based on OPNET
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In recent years, distributed new energy represented by photovoltaic technology has been increasingly widely used, and the scale of grid connection is increasing. In response to the increasingly urgent demand for distributed photovoltaic interactive communication, this article analyzes the model of distributed photovoltaic interactive data flow, builds a distributed photovoltaic user interactive communication model based on OPNET software, and builds a small simulation network that includes photovoltaic users and aggregators, verifying the practicality of the model.

articleTitle: The Electricity Spot Market Clearing Method Considering the Participation of Electric Energy Storage Based on Capacity Compensation Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to encourage the electric energy storage to actively participate in the electricity spot market trading and realize the effective coordination of multiple electric energy storage in the electricity spot market, this paper proposed a method of electricity spot market clearing under the participation of electric energy storage considering capacity compensation. The flexible invocation price declaration mechanism and capacity compensation pricing mechanism of electric energy storage are designed. The integrated cost function of electric energy storage will be defined, taking into account its flexible call cost and capacity compensation cost. Taking the lowest comprehensive cost of electricity and storage as the optimization objective item, the electricity spot market clearing model considering the compensation of electricity storage capacity was constructed. Compared with the traditional model, this model not only requires the lowest comprehensive cost of electric storage, but also requires that the new energy consumption benefit exceeds the flexible call cost of electric storage. Finally, a numerical example based on the actual data of a provincial power grid was constructed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The example results show that the market operation organization can influence the income of electric energy storage by adjusting the capacity compensation coefficient, and realize the reasonable guidance of electric energy storage construction investment.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Passive IGBT Driver Technology Based on Multi-stage Regulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Large drive resistors are often used in conventional gate driver to suppress current overshoot and voltage overshoot of power devices, but this will increase the switching losses. In order to achieve simultaneous optimization of electrical stresses and switching losses, this paper proposes an enhanced voltage source drive technology (EVGD), which can avoid building a complex IGBT model and using too many high-speed devices. EVGD is able to control the slope of voltage and current at turn-on stage and turn-off stage. With the driver resistance as the common branch, a new circuit is constructed through the parasitic inductance of the triode and power device. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(di_{\mathrm{c}}/\mathrm{d}t$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{d}v_{\mathrm{c}\mathrm{e}}/\mathrm{d}t$</tex> of the power device are controlled by applying additional equivalent voltage sources at different switching transient stages. The proposed technique enables simultaneous optimization of switching losses and electrical stresses without the need for high cost components. The proposed method is experimentally verified on IGBT(IKW75N60T) in the double-pulse test. The current overshoot and voltage overshoot can be reduced by 12.0% and 14.5% respectively. Turn-on losses and turn-off losses can be reduced by 4.16% and 7.6% respectively.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Assessment of Wind Farm Lifecycle Performance Based on Improved CRITIC Weighting Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: T Considering various dimensions such as operational indicators, electricity generation, and wind farm availability throughout the operation of a wind farm, this paper establishes a comprehensive evaluation system for wind farm lifecycle performance based on the improved CRITIC weighting method. Taking a holistic view of the wind farm's entire lifecycle, the paper compares the results obtained using the improved CRITIC weighting method with those using the original CRITIC weighting method through a case study analysis. The advantages of the improved method in wind farm performance evaluation are demonstrated, illustrating its effectiveness in promoting the development of wind energy.

articleTitle: Research on Optimal Configuration of Multi-source Coupled Heat Supply System Based on Phase-Change Heat Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Aiming at the shortcomings of solar air source heat pump in the heating process, which is inefficient and limited by geography, this paper proposes a multi-source coupled heating system based on phase-change heat storage device. The system is configured with a solid-liquid phase change thermal storage device based on time-sharing control on the basis of the traditional PVT collector-air source heat pump, and establishes a flexible and variable energy supply system in the park through the addition of a thermal storage system, which realises that the heat in the park can be “shifted to fill in the peaks and valleys”, and further improves the reliability of the park's energy supply and environmental friendliness. At the same time, the simulation model of PVT collector-heat storage-air source heat pump system is constructed based on TRNSYS software, comparing the performance difference between ordinary heat storage tank and phase change heat storage tank. The analysis results show that the performance of the system improves significantly in terms of power generation and heat collection efficiency and energy consumption after using the phase-change water tank as the heat storage tank.

articleTitle: Flywheel Energy Storage System with Synchronous Machine for High Proportion New Energy Connected Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In line with the global dual carbon goals, high proportion of renewable energy and high proportion of power electronic equipment will become the development trend of the future power grid, and the accompanying system operation safety issues will become increasingly prominent. Energy storage has good controllability and fast regulation characteristics, which can suppress fluctuations in new energy generation. However, at the same time, it further increases the proportion of access to power electronic equipment, exacerbating issues such as low inertia and underdamping. Although virtual synchronous machine technology can be used to address this issue, it sacrifices energy storage capacity and increases control complexity. In this paper, a novel flywheel energy storage system (FESS) with synchronous machine (SM) is proposed, where the SM is directly connected to the grid, then its real inertia and damping can be used for power grid support and only a partial capacity inverter is needed. The topology and operation principle of the FESS are analyzed in detail, and a simulation has been carried out to validate the effectiveness of the proposed FESS.

articleTitle: Optimal Restoration of Distribution System under Multiple Faults Considering Outage Propagation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the development of power utilities, the operation of distribution systems (DSs) has become more and more complex. The increasing frequency of various extreme events has caused multiple faults and major outages in distribution systems, affecting people's production and life.
