This paper introduces an experience of a typical agricultural county in green energy transformation from five aspects: energy supply, energy consumption, energy technology, energy system, and the utilization of urban and rural waste for energy. It summarizes the background, measures, achievements, major challenges, and main experiences accumulated. It is expected that those can be regarded as a reference for other regions.

articleTitle: Optimizing Substation Communication: A Time-Sensitive Networking Approach for Addressing Real-time Transmission Demands
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As substations become increasingly intelligent, a growing disparity arises between the surge in network traffic and the real-time transmission demands of critical communication services. Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) offers the capability to shape, schedule, and synchronize data flows, thereby enhancing the transmission quality of time-critical services. We propose a TSN-based intelligent substation traffic scheduling scheme. The transmission delay boundary of substation messages under TSN is calculated based on network calculus theory. The Omnet++ network simulation platform is used for case analysis. Simulation results reveal that, with static configuration of gate control lists, this traffic scheduling approach ensures ultra-low latency and zero jitter for sampled value message transmissions, while concurrently ensuring real-time transmission for all other communication services.

articleTitle: Fault Recovery Strategies for Active Distribution Substation with Distributed Photovoltaic Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The study of fault recovery methods for active distribution substations is of significant importance in enhancing power supply reliability and reducing user power outage losses. Incorporating distributed photovoltaic generation into these substations not only enhances outage recovery efficiency but also introduces the risk of secondary outages due to its output uncertainty. To bolster the safety of distributed photovoltaic involvement in substation outage recovery, this paper delves into fault recovery strategies for active distribution substations considering photovoltaic integration. A load recovery model involving photovoltaic participation is formulated, while safety constraints during the grid res-toration process are compre-hensively considered. The model is tackled using the particle swarm algorithm. Simulation outcomes illustrate that, with the integration of distributed photovoltaic generation, not only can safe recovery be achieved while adhering to constraints, but a higher load can also be restored.

articleTitle: Overvoltage Research and Insulation Coordination for HVDC Transmission System Based on Medium-Frequency DRU-MMC
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Currently, the application of HVDC transmission system based on medium-frequency DRU-MMC is a research hotspot. In the design of the medium-frequency DRU-MMC system, overvoltage protection and insulation coordination are crucial issues that must be addressed. Furthermore, the influence of frequency on the overvoltage characteristics of the DRU-MMC system also holds research value. Given the limited research on overvoltage-related topics of DRU-MMC systems both domestically and internationally, this paper proposes an overvoltage protection scheme suitable for medium-frequency DRU-MMC systems. Based on the comprehensive reference to traditional DC engineering and the research achievements of the characteristics of the DRU-MMC system itself, the paper investigates the impact of frequency selection in the medium-frequency system on the overvoltage of the DRU-HVDC system using PSCAD/EMTDC. It was found that the influence of frequency on overvoltage does not follow a specific pattern. Depending on the location of the fault and the type of fault, the trend of overvoltage variation with frequency differs, making it impossible to draw definite conclusions.

articleTitle: Assessment and Prediction of Energy Usage Based on ECV and ARIMA-DBN Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the background of the current growing energy demand, traditional energy usage assessment and prediction systems, which are typically based on government-released energy consumption indicators, are difficult to achieve timely and accurate monitoring and prediction of energy usage. Therefore, an energy usage assessment and prediction method based on the entropy weighting method, criteria importance through inter-criteria correlation method with coefficient of variation method (ECV) combination methods and the auto-regressive integrated moving average with the deep belief network (ARIMA-DBN) combination methods is proposed. Firstly, an energy usage evaluation method based on the ECV combination approach is proposed, which achieves a comprehensive assessment of energy usage by constructing an indicator system. Then, an energy consumption prediction method based on the ARIMA-DBN combination approach is proposed to forecast the dynamics and development trends of energy usage. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed methods is validated using energy consumption data from energy-consuming enterprises in Zhejiang province of China. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed methods can effectively evaluate energy usage and improve the accuracy of energy consumption prediction.

articleTitle: Improved Multi-tier Exergy Hub for Micro Rural Energy System Management
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Micro rural energy systems (MRESs) can significantly enhance energy efficiency through the deep coupling and cascading utilization of various energy resources. Managing MRES using exergy analysis allows for a comprehensive understanding of energy utilization in both quantity and quality dimensions. Therefore, there is a need for a systematic and clear exergy analysis model for MRES. This study focuses on MRES with renewable energy sources and proposes an improved multi-tier energy hub (EH) model along with an associated energy management optimization model. Furthermore, based on the EH model, an exergy hub (ExH) model is developed to consider both the quantity and quality aspects of energy. The study also derives corresponding exergy efficiency evaluation indicators from two perspectives on renewable energy. The effectiveness of the proposed models is validated through case study results, demonstrating a low exergy deviation of 0.9862 MWh. Moreover, the optimization based on exergy efficiency indicates room for further exergy savings in MRES (1.34% and 6.1%). Our study highlighted the advantage of engineering exergy efficiency with minimal exergy waste <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{4.83}\times \mathbf{10}^{-\mathbf{3}}\mathbf{MWh})$</tex> but cautioned that this might have economic trade-offs.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on Common and Different Values of Pumped Storage and Thermal Power
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Pumped storage is integral in modern power systems, especially those emphasizing renewable energy. It significantly boosts renewable energy utilization and aids in achieving carbon reduction targets. Comparatively, thermal power plants have traditionally ensured grid stability and security. Therefore, comparing the shared characteristics and differences in value between pumped storage and thermal power is essential. This article begins with a qualitative analysis of the commonalities and distinctions between pumped storage and thermal power. It establishes a fundamental model for peak load regulation encompassing both. It then builds economic and comprehensive evaluation models based on shadow pricing theory to assess the benefits of peak load regulation and provide investment guidance. In conclusion, by using load data and power generation curves from a provincial-level electricity grid, this article quantitatively analyzes the roles of pumped storage and thermal power in peak load regulation. This analysis is crucial for understanding how pumped storage enhances the efficiency and sustainability of modern power systems, especially those emphasizing renewable energy, and offers valuable insights for investment decisions.

articleTitle: Feature Extraction Method for Transient Overvoltage Based on Spearman Correlation Coefficient
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The large-scale grid connection of renewable energy is accompanied by problems such as insufficient voltage support capability and weakened disturbance resilience. For multiterminal DC sending system, commutation failure faults may lead to overvoltage issues, threatening the safety and reliability of power grids. To better assess transient overvoltage levels, this paper proposes a feature extraction method based on Spearman correlation coefficient, exploring key response variables related to transient overvoltage level. Firstly, based on the dynamic characteristics of renewable energy and induction motors during fault periods, the overvoltage mechanism under commutation failure is studied. Then, according to transient characteristics after commutation failure, main influencing factors of transient overvoltage are analyzed. Combining the influencing factors, a feature extraction method based on Spearman correlation coefficient is proposed, which improves the speed and accuracy of input feature selection. Finally, case study is implemented to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A DQN-Based Coordination Method of HVAC and Energy Storage for Building Energy Management
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Buildings account for 33% of global energy consumption and generate 28%of carbon emissions, drawing increasing attention in energy sector. However, the complex building thermal dynamic process poses a great challenge for building energy management (BEM). Thus, this paper proposes a coordinated BEM method of HVAC and energy storage based on deep Q-network (DQN), aiming to reduce the building operating cost while maintaining occupant comfort. Also, a variable-length rolling-horizon procedure is applied to enhance the coupling of the future scheduling time interval. In this method, a third-order building equivalent thermal model is integrated into the DQN to accurately model the dynamic temperature changes in the building. Moreover, considering the uncertainties of photovoltaic (PV) outputs and loads, the concept of stochastic optimization is introduced to the state and reward functions of DQN by generating multiple scenarios based on prediction data. The Simulation results verify that the proposed DQN-based BEM method can effectively reduce the building operating cost and keep a high level of comfort throughout the day by coordinating HVAC and energy storage.

articleTitle: Risk Premium Allocation in Energy Hubs Based on Risk Contribution
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Energy hubs aggregate various distributed generators and participate in energy markets as a whole. The total profits would be further allocated to each equipment according to their contributions. Most of the profit allocation methods are risk neutral, but energy hubs always face various uncertainties and submit risk averse bids in electricity markets. In this paper, a risk averse profit allocation considering equipment's uncertainties and contribution to risk is proposed. Firstly, marginal shortfall is introduced to measure the single equipment's contribution to energy hubs' total risk. Then, risk premium afforded by each equipment can be determined according to the predefined index, risk adjusted return on capital. Finally, the profit allocation method is proposed considering equipment's outputs and risk premium. A real energy hub in Shanghai is adopted to illustrate the proposed method. Energy retail services and energy storage's arbitrage contribute most of the total risk. Their allocated profit may suffer a loss up to nearly 5.9% of their expected profits for risk premium.

articleTitle: The Levelized Cost of Thermal Power Based on Coal Price Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In recent years, China's electric power safety supply accidents have occurred frequently. This research attempts to extract the key influencing factors, analyze the main driving forces, and the power supply issues from the perspective of cost diversion. This research constructed a multi-factor Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) coal price prediction model to analyze the changes in coal prices. Then a Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE) model for coal-fired power generation was established, and different scenarios were set up for cost analysis. Finally, from the perspective of cost fluctuations of power generation enterprises, suggestions are put forward on the issue of safe power supply in China.

articleTitle: Modular and Optimal Combination Strategy for Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In response to the lack of unified technical principles and configuration specifications in the capacity configuration design of microgrid projects, most design schemes have strong individuality and poor universality, and there are problems such as unreasonable equipment configuration. This paper focuses on the modular design concept of intelligent microgrids, and divides the components of microgrids into different modules based on different elements within the microgrid, analyzing the characteristics of distributed power sources, energy storage, and other modules. On this basis, according to the full life cycle cost of each module, a full life cycle optimization model of modular microgrids is established, and an improved simulated annealing particle swarm optimization (SAPSO) algorithm is used to solve the model, so as to give the optimized combination configuration results of each module in a specific application scenario. Finally, simulation verification is carried out through examples, taking the actual wind and solar data of a certain place as an example to verify the effectiveness of the proposed model and algorithm. By comparing and analyzing the configuration results of two different operation modes and different operation methods, it is shown that, based on the modular configuration of microgrids, the optimal solution of the model can ensure the best economy of investment, and obtain good social and economic benefits, providing a theoretical basis for standardized modular microgrid configuration schemes.

Author Keywords: improved simulated annealing particle swarm optimization algorithm

articleTitle: Robust Primary Frequency Reserve Optimization for Renewable Energy Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: During the operation of the power system, the uncertainty of the natural resources conditions will cause the deviation of the actual frequency support capacity of renewable power generation deviates from the expected value, which will affect the post-disturbance frequency stability. This paper studies the robust setting of primary frequency modulation backup of renewable energy power systems considering the uncertainty of wind and solar power generation. Considering the influence of the uncertainty of wind and solar power generation on the frequency regulation backup, a robust tuning model of the primary frequency regulation frequency backup of the renewable energy power system is established. In the sufficiency verification stage, the sufficiency of the primary frequency modulation reserve in extreme wind and solar power generation scenarios is analyzed, and the column and constraint generation algorithm is used to solve the problem. Finally, the validity of the model is verified in the improved IEEE 39-bus system.

articleTitle: Shared Energy Storage Business and Profit Models: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As a new paradigm of energy storage industry under the sharing economy, shared energy storage (SES) can effectively improve the comprehensive regulation ability and safety of the new energy power system. However, due to its unclear business positioning and profit model, it restricts the further improvement of the SES market and the in-depth exploration of the economic benefits of energy storage. Based on this, this paper combs and classifies the concept of SES and business model. On this basis, this paper analyzes and summarizes the pricing mode, income source and trading mode of the profit model of SES from three dimensions of directional, qualitative and quantitative; and then discusses and compares the current trading mode of SES under non-cooperative game and cooperative game. Finally, the future development of the SES technology business model is prospected with the existing research, hoping to provide useful reference.

articleTitle: Modified VMD Algorithm based Fault Location Method for Overhead-Cable Hybrid Transmission Line in MTDC System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Fault location based on travelling wave (TW) of multi-terminal DC (MTDC) transmission system is playing an important role in safe and stable operation of power system. The existence of wave impedance discontinuities in overhead-cable hybrid transmission lines (OCHTLs) leads to abrupt changes in TW velocity., which the traditional TW based fault location method is not adaptable. This paper proposes a novel fault location method for OCHTLs., which could increase the fault ranging accuracy. Firstly., typical OCHTL equivalent model is established and the propagation characteristics of the fault voltage TW (VTW) of OCHTLs is studied. On this basis., Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD)-Teager energy operator (TEO) algorithm is used for extracting the arrival time of voltage TW head-wave. Aiming at the problem of modal aliasing during the parameter selection of VMD, K- L divergence is utilized to optimize the modal number and penalty factor of the VMD algorithm. Moreover., by analyzing the attenuation characteristics of zero-mode and line-mode voltage., the relationship between velocity and arrival time of line-mode voltage TW is used to construct the faulty segment criterion. Subsequently., a higher precision fault location algorithm based on two-terminal information of fault segment is proposed. Finally., a MTDC with OCTHLs is built in PSCAD to verify the robustness and correctness of proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Towards Low-Carbon Collaborative Planning for Charging Stations and Distributed Renewable Resources
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In light of contemporary societal emphasis on low-carbon development and the exponential growth of electric vehicles, the optimization of EVs within low-carbon energy networks has garnered heightened attention. In pursuit of achieving more profound emissions reductions and the substantial integration of renewable energy sources, this study delves into a collaborative planning approach encompassing public charging station and distributed renewable energy sources. Aiming at improving renewable energy consumption of electric vehicles and integration of distributed renewable energy sources on distributed networks, a mixed integer model is proposed to determine the sizing and size of charging station, PV generation, and other renewable energy sources. Meanwhile, several significant factors such as electric vehicle charging demand, the operation conditions of the power distribution network are considered. The proposed model is solved by neural networks to make sure the accuracy of solutions and solving speed. he effectiveness of this method is verified by simulation. To make sure of the feasibility and practicality of the methodology, numerical experiments are conducted. The results show that this method can well optimize the location and size of the charging stations, PV generators and utilization of renewable energy as much as possible.

articleTitle: Review of Fault Probability Prediction Models for Power System Equipment under Extreme Weather Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the expansion of power system scale, the faults of power system equipment under extreme weather may result in large area blackout. To keep the security and stability of power systems, researchers have proposed proactive fault probability prediction models to mitigate the risks of large-scale failures in advance. Power system fault probability prediction models can be divided into three different categories. The three probabilistic fault prediction models are mechanism-based probabilistic fault prediction models, data-driven probabilistic fault prediction models and hybrid probabilistic fault prediction models. Additionally, the application of various fault probability prediction models in relevant disaster domains are also summarized. The aim of this paper is to provide a reference for future development of fault prediction models in power systems.

articleTitle: Formation of Operating Reserve Component in Locational Marginal Prices Considering Controllability of Wind Power
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Reserve ancillary services are important for handling the uncertainty of renewables in power systems. In the market environment, reasonable price signals are used to guide the optimal allocation of reserve ancillary services. In general, price signals are formed by market clearing. However, the current market clearing methods do not consider the controllability of renewables (in this paper, it refers to the power cap of renewables), which is essential for accommodating large-scale renewables. As a result, the reserve price signals cannot reflect the influence of the controllability of renewables. To fill this gap, the operating reserve price component considering the controllability of wind power is formed in this paper based on the locational marginal price theory. The influence of the wind power cap on the reserve requirement and wind power curtailment is analyzed and analytically modeled. Based on this, the energy-reserve joint market clearing model considering the wind power cap is established. Moreover, the operating reserve component in locational marginal prices is derived. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve the trade-off between the reserve pressure and wind power curtailment. Besides, the reserve cost allocation can be reasonably implemented through the derived operating reserve price component.

articleTitle: Frequency-Constrained Robust Service Restoration of Distribution Networks Under Renewable Power Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Renewable distributed generation is regarded as one of the promising resources for distribution system restoration. However, their uncertain power output introduces risks to power balance and frequency security, especially in the systems undergoing restoration with limited reserves and low inertia. This paper develops a robust service restoration method. It proposes a two-stage framework: first, deciding load restoration and integrating renewable generation; second, ensuring system security with operational constraints. Uncertainties from load and renewable generation are considered. The frequency constraints for the rate of frequency change (RoCoF) and quasi-steady frequency are formulated based on the decisions of load and renewable generation integration, contributing to their optimal coordination during the service restoration process. The proposed two-stage robust problem can be solved using the C&CG algorithm. The numerical studies based on the IEEE 33 bus system are used to illustrate the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an Intelligent Customer-Transformer Relationship Topology Recognition System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the context of the rapidly expanding scale of the power grid, significant growth in electricity customer data, and the rapid development of smart grids, issues such as disorganized customer information, data loss, and unclear customer-transformer relationships have emerged during the deep transformation of urban and rural electrical networks. These challenges have hindered the efficient construction and operation of smart grids. Traditional methods for identifying customer-transformer relationships are time-consuming, especially in older substation areas, requiring manual investigations, leading to resource waste and inefficiency. This study proposes an Intelligent Customer-Transformer Relationship Topology Recognition System based on Spring Boot, MyBatisPlus, and DM8. The system aims to address the challenges faced by power companies in identifying customer-transformer relationships. It plays a proactive role in the development and construction of smart grids and the achievement of carbon neutrality goals.

articleTitle: Strategic Behavior Modeling of Energy Aggregators in Electricity and Carbon Markets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Energy aggregators (EA) play an important role in the electricity- carbon joint market. EA can aggregate traditional thermal power units and renewable energy generators, and their operation strategies will directly affect the renewable energy consumption, carbon emission allowances (CEA) and economic benefits of the system, and their decisions will play a counterproductive role in the pricing of electric energy and CEA. Firstly, based on the renewable portfolio standards, this paper proposed a clearing model of the electricity and carbon market for EA. Secondly, after fully considering the uncertainty of renewable energy, a two-stage optimization model that can maximize the benefits of EA and maximize social welfare is established by simulating the trading process of EA in the electric energy carbon emission rights market. Finally, by using the KKT theorems and dual theory, the initial nonlinear two-stage problem is transformed into a linear mathematical problem with equilibrium constraints. The above model is analyzed on the improved IEEE-30 node power grid model. The results show that the strategic behavior of EA both increases their revenue and effectively reduces the carbon emissions of the system.

articleTitle: The Lessons and Insights of Flexibility Adjustment Resource Development in Germany
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: High renewable energy penetration presents major challenges to power system flexibility, which has become a hot topic in future energy systems. Germany is leading the trend in the development of both traditional and new flexibility adjustment resources. This paper provides an overview of the development of flexibility resources in Germany, analyzes their developmental experiences, and draws valuable insights for reference.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Analysis Method Based on the Combination of Multiple Indicators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The new power systems have higher requirements for stability control accuracy and speed, and online stability control decision-making based on real-time grid information has become a future development direction. Online stability control optimizes control measures based on real-time stability margins and control objectives, and needs to reliably quantify system stability margins under both stable and unstable scenarios. Aiming at the status quo that the existing indicators are only applicable to stable or unstable scenarios, an online quantification method of stability margin based on the combination of multiple indicators is proposed, which combines the stability indicators that support the fast judgment of stability and the stability indicators that can measure the degree of instability to realize the quantification of stability margin in multiple scenarios. Firstly, the general process of online assessment of transient stability is analyzed. Then, a stability margin online quantification method based on the combination of multiple indicators is designed from the demand of online stability control optimization and decision-making, and the combination of concavity and convexity of phase trajectory and the extended equal-area criterion of homologous data is used as an example to give the application process. Finally, based on the IEEE39 node system, the proposed method is verified to quantify the stability margin when the stability scenario changes, and the analysis of examples shows that the proposed method can give the stability margin in stable and unstable scenarios on the basis of rapid judgment of stability and support the decision-making of stabilization and control.

Author Keywords: concavity and convexity of phase trajectory

articleTitle: Wide-band Oscillation Disturbance Source Location Based on Compressed Sensing and CNN-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the strong time-varying and non-linear interactions between power electronic devices and the power grid, challenges arising from wide-band oscillation risks have been increasing under the backdrop of the “dual-high” power system development, making the precise location of oscillation disturbance sources difficult. This article introduces a method for the precise location of wide-area system oscillation disturbance sources, which is based on compressed sensing and a fusion of the CNN-LSTM algorithm. Firstly, we discussed the role and application conditions of compressed sensing and generated a measurement matrix synchronized with the oscillation signal, achieving high-rate compression of the oscillation signal. Subsequently, this paper constructed a deep learning model using CNN-LSTM, taking sparse sampling signals from various substations as inputs to achieve wide-band oscillation location. Finally, we applied this method to a disturbance source location task in an IEEE-39 bus system that includes a wind farm. The results indicate that this approach can effectively bypass the constraints of the Nyquist sampling theorem and achieve highly accurate disturbance source location under low computational requirements.

articleTitle: Ampacity Analysis of Power Cables Based on Polypropylene Insulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Polypropylene (PP) shows great potential to replace cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) as the next generation of insulation materials for power cable. To understand the operation characteristics, this paper studied the temperature distribution and ampacities of PP-based power cable. The differences in temperature distribution between the XLPE and PP cables was compared by solving a magnetic-thermal-flow field coupling model for a 110kV power cable. And the ampacities of the two cables were studied with different laid methods in the soil, pipeline and trench. The results show that XLPE has a better heat dissipation due to the greater thermal conductivity, whereas the PP cable has a higher ampacity and stronger short-time overload current withstand due to the higher temperature tolerance. If thermal conductivity increase, the ampacity of PP cable would be further improved. However, the thermal conductivity of PP has a saturation effect on the increase in cable ampacities. Under soil, pipeline and trench laying conditions, the ampacity of PP cables is 8.5%, 9.5% and 6.3% higher than that of XLPE cables, respectively. The application of PP as cable insulation can significantly increase the transmission capacity of cables without structural changes.

articleTitle: Research on Medium-and Long-Term Operation Strategy in the Province Considering the Uncertainty of Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In view of the acceleration of the marketization of renewable energy, combined with the current situation of the construction of China's power market, this paper studies the provincial medium-and long-term trading mechanism to promote the consumption of renewable energy and its connection with the spot market. Based on quantile regression method, a cooperative decomposition model of short-term contract electricity considering the utilization of high-quality renewable energy is proposed. Furthermore, to ensure the physical execution of short-term contract electricity, a day-ahead market clearing strategy based on robust optimization is established to realize the orderly connection between medium-and long-term transactions and the spot market. Finally, a numerical example is given to verify the effectiveness and practicability of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Simulation and Optimization Analysis of Integrated Energy System Considering Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To improve the economic performance of system operation and better coordinate the operation of various equipment in an integrated energy system, a day-ahead operation optimization for the integrated energy system considering load forecasting is proposed. Firstly, the CloudPSS IESLab platform is utilized to establish an integrated energy system model that encompasses photovoltaic, heating pump, and energy storage systems. The effectiveness of this model and the accuracy of the calculations are verified; Subsequently, utilizing the CloudPSS IESLab SDK along with statistical methods, machine learning, and neural network models, an integrated energy system load forecasting model is developed; Finally, the optimize the operation is implemented with the goal of minimizing the operating and maintenance costs of the integrated energy system based on predicted load scenario. The results show that the day-ahead operation optimization based on load forecasting method proposed in this article can significantly improve system economy performance, improve system efficiency, and achieve low-carbon operation.

articleTitle: Damping Level Enhancement Strategy for Large-Scale Renewables Penetrated Power System Based on Data-Driven Global Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The safe and stable operation of power system is threatened seriously by poor damping low-frequency oscillation in interconnected system. Aiming at the flexible operating conditions and insufficient damping in the large-scale renewables penetrated system, a data-driven global sensitivity calculation method is proposed in this paper, based on which, the correlation between the electromechanical interarea mode and the active power of the generator is quantitatively analyzed. Then, the optimal allocation scheme of the number of modulation units and the corresponding modulation amount is given. Finally, an active power modulation strategy of generator based on the proposed global sensitivity is constructed to improve the damping of interarea mode. The simulation results of IEEE 16-generator 5-area system show that the proposed global sensitivity calculation method can select the generator participated in modulation accurately, and the proposed damping modulation strategy can improve the system damping effectively.

articleTitle: Optimal Bidding Strategy of Electric Vehicle Aggregators in Energy, Frequency Regulation and Demand Response Market
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper proposes a comprehensive framework for Electric Vehicle Aggregators (EVAs) bidding in joint markets, namely energy, frequency regulation and Demand Response markets, across both day-ahead and real-time stages. The optimal bidding strategy aims at minimizing the total cost of EVA, while satisfying the charging demand of all connected electric vehicles (EVs), To address uncertainties associated with EV parameters and regulation signals, a two-stage stochastic optimization problem based on the aggregated EVs and regulation signal model is formulated. Additionally, a rolling-window method is employed to mitigate uncertainty during the real-time stage. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through extensive numerical tests involving 500 EVs, demonstrating its capability to yield lucrative profits while simultaneously satisfying EVs' charging demand.

articleTitle: Revenue Estimation for Orderly Charging of Electric Vehicles Based on Smart Meters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the rapid development of electric vehicles (EVs), uncoordinated charging of large numbers of EVs in residential areas leads to transformer overloading. Given a number of orderly charging approaches in existing literature, their business model and corresponding revenue estimation is still unclear, especially for residential areas. Therefore, a business model of smart meter-based ordered charging is proposed to alleviate the charging problems of users in residential areas and quantify the revenue of aggregators. First, a bidirectional” cloud-meter-pile-vehicle” communication scheme enabled by smart meters is established to facilitate data collection and implement controlled, organized charging. Then, A Gaussian mixture model (GMM) is employed to characterize users' historical behaviors, enabling the formulation of an orderly charging strategy designed to minimize charging costs for user groups. Finally, taking the actual data of a region in Hangzhou as an example, GMM is constructed to analyze charging start times, charging durations, and charging energy. This allows for revenue estimation of EV orderly charging within this business model and the determination of the investor's return period.

articleTitle: Bidding Strategy of Distributed Prosumers in Electricity Reserve Market Based on Information Gap Decision Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Distributed prosumers face market risks such as price fluctuations, load demand changes, and renewable energy generation output uncertainties when participating in electricity energy and ancillary service markets. In this paper, a bid decision model for distributed prosumers in the daily electricity and ancillary market is established using the Information Gap Decision Theory (IGDT). First, the agency architecture for distributed prosumers participating in these markets is analyzed. Next, a multi-type distributed resource regulation model is constructed, forming the basis of a decision model for the participation of distributed prosumers in the joint energy and ancillary market. Then, the various uncertainties faced by prosumers in their decision-making process are quantitively modeled using the information entropy theory, and an IGDT-based robust optimization model for deriving bidding strategies is developed. Finally, the proposed model is validated in the modified IEEE 33-node distribution system, and the bidding strategies generated by the proposed model effectively addresses the multiple uncertainties faced by prosumers, safeguarding their profits.

articleTitle: Research on Evaluation Method of Comprehensive Energy System Benefit Considering Electric Energy Substitution Effect
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: At present, the phenomenon of resource shortage and serious environmental pollution in China has received widespread attention, and solving the energy problem is urgent. The strategy of replacing electricity is an important measure to promote the energy consumption revolution. Its implementation helps to implement China's energy strategy as a whole, reduce the use of fossil fuels such as coal, improve the level of clean energy use, and reduce air pollution. This article comprehensively reviews and summarizes the practical experience, research status, and development trends of electricity substitution at home and abroad based on literature review. Based on this, a quantitative calculation model and comprehensive evaluation method for the evaluation indicators of comprehensive energy system benefits are proposed, taking into full consideration the positive effects of electricity substitution. Divide the construction benefits of the comprehensive energy system into three categories: social, technological, and economic benefits. Determine the quantification and calculation model of evaluation indicators. Based on the subjective evaluation method of the triangular fuzzy hierarchy process and the objective evaluation method of the entropy weight method, propose a combination weighting method that effectively integrates indicator weights based on the minimum deviation of weight vectors; Combine the expected combination weights obtained with the matter element extension model to solve the benefit evaluation level and rating value of the comprehensive energy system construction plan. Through case analysis, the scientificity and rationality of this evaluation method have been verified, proving that electricity substitution work has a positive effect on energy conservation and carbon reduction in the park.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Evaluation and Selection Application of Flexibility Transformation Technology for Thermal Power Units
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The flexibility transformation of thermal power units is one of the main measures to improve the flexibility of power system. It is very important to evaluate and select the appropriate flexibility transformation technology in the flexibility transformation of thermal power units. In view of the current situation that the evaluation industry of thermal power flexibility transformation technology lacks a complete evaluation system and the technical value is difficult to quantify, this paper collates the existing thermal power unit flexibility transformation technology, and establishes a value evaluation index system based on investment cost, investment recovery period, minimum output, technical maturity, technical applicability and other indicators. Based on the survey data, the comprehensive evaluation method of AHP-entropy weight method based on game theory is used to quantify the value of 14 representative flexible transformation technologies of thermal power units. It provides a reference for the technical selection and application of flexibility transformation in thermal power industry.

articleTitle: A Distribution Network Voltage Optimization Scheduling Method Based on the Virtual Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the large-scale integration of distributed energy, the distribution network faces overvoltage, undervoltage, and voltage fluctuation issues brought about by distributed energy. Flexible loads can participate in distribution network regulation through time shifting, but flexible loads have characteristics such as small individual capacity, dispersed location, and involvement of user privacy, which require centralized control. Virtual power plant (VPP) can be used to coordinate and control various distributed energy sources and flexible loads. Typically, VPP focus more on commercial profit and do not fully consider the technical constraints of the system. Technical virtual power plants (TVPP) can pay attention to the technical constraints of the system while considering commercial profit. However, when flexible loads participate in the scheduling of technical TVPP, user privacy cannot be protected. To address this, a flexible virtual battery model that aggregates multiple flexible loads is proposed. By equating flexible loads to virtual batteries, the regulation capacity of flexible loads can be quantified while protecting user privacy. This model is tested through the IEEE 33-bus test system. The results show that, on the premise of protecting user privacy, the technical virtual power plant can regulate the voltage quality of the distribution network through flexible virtual batteries, while considering the distribution network loss situation.

articleTitle: Loss Reduction and Voltage Regulation Strategy of Active Distribution Network with High Proportion Distributed Photovoltaic Resources
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With a large number of distributed photovoltaic resources and multiple types of loads entering the distribution network, the increase in network losses and voltage fluctuations are two important issues. In response to this issue, this paper proposes an active and reactive power collaborative optimization strategy for active distribution networks that considers loss reduction and voltage regulation. Firstly, an improved K-means clustering algorithm based on the maximum minimum distance criterion is used to effectively cluster the output scenarios of photovoltaic power generation, reducing the number of scenarios. Secondly, the impact of different data attributes of power generation equipment on the operation of the power system is analyzed to optimize the assessment of active power loss in the distribution network. Finally, considering the collaborative control of various controllable distributed resources, establish an active and reactive power collaborative optimization model, and cooperate with on load tap changer to reduce network losses while maintaining voltage levels. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is verified by an example on an improved IEEE-33 distribution network.

articleTitle: Dynamic State Estimation of Distribution Network Considering Distributed PV Access
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: After large-scale distributed PV access to the distribution network, there will be problems such as power flow reversal and voltage over-limit, which will bring more uncertainty to the operation mode and state perception of the active distribution network. It is urgent to establish an effective dynamic state estimation model of active distribution network with PV. However, in previous studies, the amplitude and phase angle of node voltage are taken as state variables, and there is no dynamic differential equation. In essence, it belongs to Forecasting-Aided State Estimation. In this paper, the dynamic variables under transient conditions are studied. Considering the dynamic process of distributed grid-connected PV, a general control model of photovoltaic grid-connected is established, and the dynamic process description based on differential equations is obtained. A dynamic state estimation model of active distribution network with PV is proposed, and the model is solved by Kalman Filter algorithm. Finally, an improved IEEE33 node system model with PV is built by PSCAD, which verifies the effectiveness of the state estimation model of active distribution network with PV.

articleTitle: A Section Location Method for High Resistance Fault in Resonant Grounding System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: It is difficult to locate the high resistance fault section in resonant grounding system, and the traditional protection is not sensitive or even ineffective, which brings a serious threat to the safety of distribution network. In order to solve the above problems, a section location method based on zero-sequence instantaneous power for high resistance fault in resonant grounding system is proposed. Firstly, the equivalent model of high resistance faults in distribution network is established. Based on this, the analytical expressions of zero-sequence voltage and zero-sequence current of faults are solved, and the relationship of zero-sequence instantaneous power waveform between faulty section and healthy section is deduced. Secondly, the similarity is visually measured by Spearman correlation coefficient to realize high-resistance fault section location. Finally, a simulation model is built in PSCAD to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method and its ability to resist transition resistances and noise. Simulation results show that the proposed method has a good application prospect.

articleTitle: Response-Based Synchronization Stability Analysis of Multi-Converter Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing integration of renewable energy into the power grid, the application of converters in the electrical systems has grown significantly. Due to the nonlinearity, the complexity and the difficult availability of the system models, traditional methods of synchronization stability analysis have revealed limitations and challenges when confronted with modern power systems. Additionally, the prevalence of grid-following converters in the grid leads to a shortage of voltage sources within the system, significantly increasing the risk of grid instability. This paper addresses the issue of synchronization stability analysis of multi-converter power systems, and proposes a response-based method to assess the synchronization stability level of the entire system. Through an analysis of the synchronization stability mechanism of grid-forming converters, a relationship is established between electromotive force, power angle, and node voltages. A quantitative stability evaluation of the system is achieved using the sBTTC index. Case studies show that the proposed response-based method is effective to analyze the synchronization stability of multi-converter power systems, with great practical viability in engineering applications.

articleTitle: Flexibility Mining and Improvement for Urban Electricity-Gas-Heat-Storage Integrated Energy Systems: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In recent years, the proportion of renewable energy connected to the grid has been steadily increasing. However, the randomness and volatility characteristics of renewable energy pose challenges to the flexibility of the energy system. Urban integrated energy systems, which combine electricity, gas, and heat, could enhance the flexibility of the energy system by coordinating energy storage with various energy systems. This paper focuses on the flexibility of urban electricity-gas-heat-storage integrated energy systems. Firstly, the paper discusses the difference between park-level integrated energy systems and urban-level integrated energy systems. Secondly, based on the existing research, the paper conducts an integrated modeling analysis of urban integrated energy systems. Finally, the paper explores the potential for flexibility in urban electricity-gas-heat-storage integrated energy systems.

articleTitle: Research on Power-Grid-Load-Storage Integration Based on Electricity-Carbon-Gas Cycle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the rapid development of urban economy and the construction of new towns, the problem of solid waste such as a large number of domestic garbage, sludge and agricultural and forestry waste has become increasingly prominent. In this context, it is particularly urgent to design an integrated scheme of source, grid, load and storage including electricity-carbon-gas cycle. In this paper, a collaborative utilization framework of waste-to-energy system, carbon capture equipment and power-to-gas technology is constructed to form an electricity-carbon-gas cycle. Among them, carbon capture equipment captures carbon dioxide produced by waste power generation, which is used for power-to-gas technology to convert into natural gas, and the power consumption of power-to-gas equipment and flue gas treatment is jointly transferred through storage equipment to achieve peak shaving and valley filling of load and fluctuation of renewable energy output. A multi-strategy fusion honey badger algorithm is proposed to be applied to the research on source-network-load-storage integration, which effectively improves the solution efficiency and the stability of the results. The simulation results show that the scheme has significant advantages in economy, carbon emission and energy efficiency, which provides guidance for the utilization of biomass waste resources and electricity-carbon-gas cycle in the region, and promotes the improvement of regional carbon emission reduction and energy efficiency.

articleTitle: A Unified Clearing Mechanism in the Dual Track Electricity Market Environment in China
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: After the market settlement, it is found that the historical billing data needs to be retroactively refunds due to over payment or additional payments due to underpayment for the data that has been settled historically because of measurement data correction, settlement price adjustment and billing calculation errors. However, at present, settlement rules for each province in China are different. The high degree of coupling among settlement data and the increasing volume of clearing data make it difficult to ensure timeliness, accuracy, and compliance with the approach of case-by-case funds handling. Therefore, this paper constructs a unified clearing mechanism that is adapted to the development of different provinces. It provides a theoretical basis for the design of the clearing mechanism in the future provincial electricity market and conducts case analysis using the improved IEEE-30 system to validate the feasibility of the model.

articleTitle: Power Grid Flexible Partition and Regional Flexibility Assessment Based on Complex Network Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The great uncertainty caused by the high proportion of new energy connected to the grid leads to increased randomness in the power grid and the problem of supply and demand balance. To introduce appropriate grid flexibility resources and accurately measure the degree of power grid flexibility at multiple grid levels, this paper proposes flexible zoning of power grids and flexibility assessment of regional power grids based on complex network theory, focusing on the spatial nature of flexible resources. First, based on the traditional zoning method for screening key transmission sections, the degree of node flexibility is considered to conduct flexible zoning of the power grid. Based on the zoning, starting from the flexibility of transmission channels and nodes, the flexibility of the zones is further evaluated. The method proposed in this article can effectively evaluate the impact of load and new energy output fluctuations on transmission capacity and identify areas of insufficient flexibility in regional power grids, demonstrated in test results on a modified IEEE 39-node system.

Author Keywords: flexible evaluation of regional power Grid

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration of Shared PV-Storage Integrated Fast Charging Station in Old Residential Communities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The electric vehicle (EV) industry has experienced explosive growth in recent years. Although the extensive deployment of charging infrastructure is common to mitigate the range anxiety of EV owners, this is not a wise solution for old residential communities due to the limited power capacity and parking space. In this paper, the shared PV-Storage integrated fast charging station is introduced to address the difficult-to-charge issue in old residential communities. This paper proposes a novel optimal configuration method to minimize charging station space and charging pile investment, while optimizing the capacity of photovoltaic (PV) and energy storage. Through the field assessment for a residential area in Shenzhen, the data such as power load and light intensity were obtained and used to establish a configuration mode. The final case study shows that the optimal number of parking spaces is 6, the PV capacity is 73.9721kW, and the equipped energy storage capacity is 473.0349kWh (146.7624kW).

articleTitle: Energy Storage Siting and Capacity Planning Considering Voltage Flexibility Under Extreme Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The volatility and non-dispatchability of renewable energy sources raise a series of challenges in the context of new energy boom. To cope with these problems, this study proposes a novel energy storage system siting and capacity planning method based on extreme scenarios. The method takes voltage flexibility into full consideration, and employs the K-means algorithm to identify extreme scenarios by analyzing the correlation between temperature and weather and load. Then, load scenarios under extreme meteorological conditions are generated using a generative adversarial network, and a small probability high load scenario generation model is constructed. On the basis of voltage stability and flexibility as indicators, nodes with lower stability and weaker flexibility were prioritized for the layout of energy storage systems. Subsequently, the capacity allocation of the energy storage system is optimized by an improved particle swarm algorithm to reduce the operation cost. Finally, the effectiveness and feasibility of the method in energy storage siting and capacity planning are verified by simulation results of the improved IEEE-33 node distribution system.

articleTitle: Strategic Feature Augmentation in TabNet for Unified Regional Wind Power Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting plays a pivotal role in the effective integration of renewable energy into power systems. This paper proposes a unified TabNet model tailored to predict across multiple wind farms within a region, negating the need for individual wind farm-specific models, which can induce computational burdens and inconsistencies in prediction quality. Our innovation hinges on the integration of TabNet's sparse-max feature selector with our advanced feature augmentation approach. Specifically, we employ numerical weather predictions (NWP) and introduce a novel radix one-hot encoding for wind farm indexing, providing enhanced sparsity and capturing farm-specific traits. By extending NWP input from neighboring grid points, our model gains an augmented spatial and temporal perception field. The proposed GeoNWP-Index Hybrid model for WPF outperforms traditional techniques, reducing nRMSE and nMAE to 14.72% and 11.67%, respectively, from the benchmarks set by XGBoost at 16.46% and 13.55%. This approach under-scores deep learning's potential in revolutionizing regional WPF, pointing towards more cohesive renewable energy management.

articleTitle: Observability Analysis and State Estimation of Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the complexity of modern power systems continues to increase, there is a growing need for timely and accurate state monitoring of the distribution grid. Therefore, it is necessary to summarize the existing state estimation methods and explore more reliable ones. This article reviews research on the state estimation of the distribution grid, mainly covering system observability judgment methods, static state estimation methods, and dynamic state estimation methods. First, the article reviews the discernment criteria for system observability in the distribution grid and provides observability judgment methods based on topology and model-based approaches. Next, the paper provides an overview of methods for system static state estimation, introducing orthogonal transformation and the Givens method based on the weighted least squares (WLS) algorithm. It also introduces the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) used by many power system state estimators as the estimation standard. In addition, the importance of dynamic state estimation (DSE) is discussed, especially when large-scale renewable energy devices and sites are integrated into the generation side. DSE can help grid operators better cope with uncertainties and ensure the reliability of the grid. The article elaborates on methods based on kalman filtering, such as the extended kalman filter (EKF) and the uncertain kalman filter (UKF), which have been widely used in DSE. Finally, against the backdrop of the rise of deep learning technology, this article expands on some researchers' attempts to integrate data-driven algorithms into state estimation research.

articleTitle: A Decision-Making Model for Custodian Institutions to Participate in a Carbon Market Considering Risk Preferences and Investment Constraints
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Given the target of “carbon peaking and carbon neutrality” as well as the establishment and development of the national carbon market in China, the carbon emission allowances (CEA) custody business has developed rapidly. In this context, it is necessary to conduct research on the decision-making model of custodian institutions participating in the carbon market. In this paper, the business mode and process of carbon emission allowance custody are introduced first. Then, a decision-making model is presented for custodian institutions to participate in the carbon market with risk preferences and investment constraints taken into account, using conditional value at risk (CVaR) to quantify the income risk caused by market price uncertainty. Finally, based on actual data of the carbon market in Guangdong province, some case studies are analyzed and compared under different scenarios, and the flexibility and effectiveness of the developed model are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Assessment of Integrated Energy Systems Based on an Improved AHP-Gray Assessment Methodology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the context of the increasing depletion of traditional energy sources and environmental problems, it is imperative to establish a sound energy system and solve new energy consumption problems. This will facilitate energy transformation and promote the green and low-carbon development of the energy industry. To ensure that the integrated energy system can operate economically and efficiently, it is crucial to establish a complete and accurate evaluation system. Therefore, based on the perspective of integrated energy system, this paper focuses on the problems of imperfection and inaccuracy of the evaluation system, and constructs a relatively comprehensive evaluation system for integrated energy system, including relevant indicators such as technical benefits, energy use benefits, environmental benefits, economic benefits and social benefits. In addition, this paper proposes a scientific evaluation method based on the improved AHP-grey evaluation method, which provides a comprehensive evaluation system for the integrated energy system.

articleTitle: Graph Convolutional Network Based Power System Risk Assessment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In modern electric power systems, accurate and fast risk assessment is of paramount importance. Traditional methods, relying on iterative computations, have a substantial computational demand, hindering their efficiency in real-time evaluations. This paper introduces a novel risk assessment approach using Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), which leverages the graph structure of power system data, thereby enhancing the efficiency of risk assessment and further bolstering the power grid's risk analysis and early warning capabilities. This study utilized the IEEE RTS-79 system to generate representative samples, designed experiments to fine-tune model hyperparameters via grid search, and subsequently trained the model. A comparative analysis was then carried out among various traditional machine learning methods and deep learning models. The results indicate that GCNs exhibit exceptional generalization capabilities, meeting the demands for real-time risk assessment in modern power systems.

articleTitle: Distributed Hybrid Secondary Control of Virtual Synchronous Generators for Isolated AC Microgrids with Low Bandwidth Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the high penetration of renewable energy based distributed generators (DGs), AC microgrids (MGs) exhibit a low-inertia characteristic. Thus, a novel control algorithm called virtual synchronous generator (VSG) is widely integrated to meet the demands of stabilizing MGs operation as well as providing ancillary regulation performance. In this paper, a distributed hybrid secondary control of VSGs for isolated AC MGs with low bandwidth communication is proposed to achieve frequency restoration and fair power sharing. We first model the VSG by imitating the operation of synchronous generators. Considering the nonlinear character of VSGs, distributed hybrid secondary control with inertial-support is then established for flexible frequency restoration under load disturbances. Moreover, by introducing a self-triggered communication mechanism, active power is fairly shared among VSGs with rarely communications, and hence the communication and computation burden of local controllers is considerably reduced. Finally, a test MG is constructed to illustrate the efficacy of the proposed hybrid control method, aligning well with the Lyapunov stability analysis.

articleTitle: Industrial Adjustable Resource Analysis And Control Boundary Research With Large Capacity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Industrial users have large demand for electricity. And their adjustable potential is outstanding. Exploiting its adjustable potential is of great significance to improve the flexibility of the power system. In this paper, we focus on analysing the iron and steel enterprises and establish the relevant physical model, and use it as a basis to study their adjustable boundaries.

Author Keywords: iron and steel enterprises adjustable boundary

articleTitle: A Two-tier Wind-solar Output Modelling Method Considering Day-to-day Output Pattern Transition and Intraday Output Dependent Changes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Generation of correlated wind-solar output sequences can improve the reliability of time series production simulations for wind-solar-containing power systems and provide guidance for power system planning and operation. A method is proposed for modelling correlated wind-solar output sequences, taking into account the transition of output patterns from day to day and the changes in output within a day. Firstly, the indicators that characterize the wind-solar power output properties are selected, and the k-means clustering method is used to cluster the wind-solar joint power output patterns. Secondly, a univariate Markov chain model is established at the upper tier to reflect the transition process of the joint power output pattern of the wind-solar between adjacent days. Additionally, Copula-based Markov chain models are built at the lower tier to describe the dependent changes in the wind-solar output during intraday moments. Finally, Monte Carlo simulation is used to obtain a correlated wind-solar output sequence for a specified time period. Simulation verification shows that the proposed method has a smaller RMSE than the traditional MCMC method and Copula model in terms of statistical characteristics, and it can generate output sequences that are more in line with the actual relevance of wind-solar.

articleTitle: Optimization Strategy of Electricity Retailers' Sales Packages Considering Green Energy Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the context of the gradual establishment of a unified national electricity market system and the large-scale integration of renewable energy, electricity retailers need to comprehensively consider inter-provincial spot trading and inter-provincial green energy spot trading. Additionally, electricity retailers need to design rational electricity package strategies to promote the consumption of inter-provincial green energy by the demand side. This paper first utilizes cloud modeling to represent the uncertainty of user load demand and formulates electricity purchase decisions for the retailer in the spot market based on chance-constrained programming. Secondly, a mechanism for inter-provincial green energy consumption integration is designed, and an electricity package optimization strategy is developed that balances retailer profits and user electricity benefits. Finally, through numerical examples, the proposed dual-layer model is validated to achieve a win-win situation for both electricity retailers and users.

articleTitle: Flexibility Exploration in Intergrated Energy Systems: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The integration of renewable energy into the power system requires a high degree of system flexibility. This flexibility can be achieved not only through the utilization of flexible resources within the power system but also through the coupling of different components in an integrated energy system, including thermal, gas, and electricity. The integrated energy system, which encompasses multiple energy carriers and storage technologies, can contribute significantly to enhancing the overall flexibility of the system. This survey will summarize the sources and the constraints of flexibility in integrated energy systems, as well as the methods to enhance flexibility.

articleTitle: Fault Isolation Strategy Based on Diode Groups of All-DC Offshore Wind Power Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The All-DC collection and transmission technology for offshore wind power has currently become a research hotspot, due to no need of power frequency transformers with large capacity, avoiding charging power problems of AC cable capacitors and the ability to improve the stability of offshore wind turbines generator (WTG) and converter stations, etc. The equipment of the All-DC wind power transmission system has a large number of power electronic devices and exhibits low-inertia characteristics, thus the rapid development of DC faults will threaten the stable operation of the system. This paper proposes an All-DC wind power transmission topology and fault isolation strategy based on diode groups. The system fault characteristics of DC cable faults on the WTG branch are analyzed. Combined with the unidirectional conductivity of diodes, a topology of connecting diodes on the branch of the series-connected WTGs is proposed, which provides conditions to decouple the faulted and healthy areas structurally. A fault isolation strategy is proposed and verified through simulation analysis. A preliminary study on the engineering application shows obvious economic advantages, thus providing a research basis for the large-scale offshore All-DC wind power transmission scenarios.

articleTitle: Impact of Identical Aggregated LC Output Filters on High-Frequency Oscillation Stability in DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The construction of DC micro-grid is conducive to the nearby absorption of renewable energy. Meanwhile, the increase of power electronic devices in the micro-grid may lead to the occurrence of high-frequency oscillations and other phenomena, which requires the evaluation of the stability of small disturbances during planning. In the evaluation process, the number of micro-power source is approximately proportional to the dimension of the system state matrix, so a large number of micro-power source connections bring challenges to modal calculation. It is necessary to propose a method of order reduction to meet the requirements of small disturbance stability analysis of DC microgrid. In this paper, an aggregated order reduction model for high frequency oscillations is proposed, which reduces the workload of numerical calculation in the process of modal analysis of the microgrid, and is helpful to better evaluate the microgrid in the planning stage. In the last part, simulations are carried out to verify the method for different micropower access quantity and different microgrid topology. The simulation results show that the method proposed in this paper can effectively evaluate the high frequency oscillation risk of DC micro-grid and simplify the difficulty of calculation.

articleTitle: Risk Evaluation of Minimum Design Temperature of Gas Insulation Switchgear
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The risk of extreme low temperature below design temperature is notable challenge to power system. Appropriate design temperature is a crucial factor to guarantee reliability of power system under extreme cold climate. According to existing code, electric equipment should be designed to withstand multiple annual mean minimum temperatures. Since rubber sealing of combined Gas Insulated switchgear (GIS) could shrink notably in extreme cold climate, it could induce extensive SF6 leakage and cause widespread outage of GIS switchgear once the environmental temperature is notable lower than the design criterion. In this paper, observed temperatures in 9 meteorological stations of Shandong province from 1973 to 2016 are analyzed with Generalized Extreme Value (GEV). The risk of exceeding minimum design temperature is evaluated based on mean annual minimum temperatures according to existing code. Moreover, different likelihood of exceeding minimum design temperature of GIS equipment are calculated based on historical minimum temperature and minimum temperature in typical area for comparison. Numerical results suggest that the proposed method provides theoretical support for transmission and transformation equipment minimum design temperature value to optimization.

Author Keywords: likelihood of extreme cold climate below design temperature

articleTitle: Distributed Photovoltaic Operating Status Assessment Based on DBN Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that distributed photovoltaic power stations lack electrical measurement equipment and traditional status assessment methods rely on a large amount of measured data, a distributed photovoltaic operating status assessment method based on deep belief network (DBN) feature extraction is adopted. This method uses DBN to extract the data features of theoretical values and measured values, and then calculates the similarity between the two feature vectors through Hausdorff distance (HD). In addition, considering that the HD value range is not suitable to directly reflect the operating status of the photovoltaic power station, a Logistic function layer is added after calculating the HD value, and the HD value after the Logistic function is defined as SI (Status Indicator) to reflect the operating status score of the photovoltaic power station. Calculation examples show that the proposed method has an accuracy of 97.5% in state assessment, can effectively solve the problem of difficult electrical data measurement in distributed photovoltaic power stations, and can provide data support for the daily operation and maintenance of distributed photovoltaic power stations.

articleTitle: Real-Time Control of Optimal Voltage in Distribution Networks Based on Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the gradual penetration of photovoltaic in the distribution network, while reducing system losses and overall carbon emissions, it also leads to issues such as periodic voltage exceeding limits. Voltage safety is of great significance for the stable operation of the distribution network. Therefore, a voltage control strategy based on the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm is proposed. Firstly, the role of photovoltaic inverters in optimizing reactive power and voltage in distribution networks was studied; Secondly, with the objective function of minimizing active power loss in the distribution network and considering the reactive power compensation capability of the inverter, a distribution network voltage control strategy based on deep deterministic strategy gradient algorithm is proposed; Finally, the voltage control strategy effectiveness was verified using a modified IEEE33 node example. The simulation results showed that the strategy learned by the DDPG algorithm can dynamically regulate the reactive power of each photovoltaic inverter to achieve the goal of controlling voltage safety, and the system network loss is reduced by 13.5% compared to before regulation.

articleTitle: Short-Term Prediction of Wind Farm Cluster Power Based on Load Risk Scenarios and Improved Weighted Loss During Peak and Valley Load Periods
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
