publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing integration of a significant number of Inverter-Based Distributed Generators (IBDGs), the transient characteristics on the low-voltage distribution network side have undergone substantial changes, rendering traditional stage division standards less applicable. This paper proposes a novel stage division standard for the transient response in Active Distribution Networks (ADNs), serving as a crucial tool for a more profound analysis of the interactions between ADNs and the transmission network. The paper begins by developing an electromagnetic model using a real ADN then performs large disturbance simulations for ADNs at different penetration levels, and introduces a new segmentation criterion based on the external characteristics of ADNs under large disturbances. By formulating mathematical models for the components within the ADN during transient stages, this paper delves into a mechanistic analysis of the external characteristics of ADNs at each phase and identifies key factors influencing the external characteristics in various stages.

articleTitle: Research on Optimal Scheduling of Multiple Improved Energy Hubs Under Energy Sharing Mode
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Improved energy hub (IEH) can improve the efficiency of the system's multi-energy complementarity and maximize the use of various energy sources. When multiple IEHs operate together and optimize their own control parameters, they not only have to consider their own economy, but also the influence of the control parameters on other IEHs. To address the above challenges, an optimal scheduling method for multiple IEHs under the energy sharing mode is proposed. Firstly, a cooperative game-based energy sharing mode framework and an IEH model are proposed; secondly, the objective function and game model of the energy sharing mode are constructed, and an improved Shapley value allocation strategy based on the contribution degree is proposed and solved by an improved double-layer nested quantum genetic algorithm; lastly, a real- world example-based simulation shows that IEHs participating in the energy sharing mode reduces the operation cost, and the adopted improved Shapley value allocation strategy can maximize its benefits in an equilibrium sense.

articleTitle: The Optimal Ratio of GFM-Converters to GFL-Converters for Transient Voltage Regulation with Weak Grid Condition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: High proportion of renewable energy connected to the grid has facilitated integration of grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) converters in the power system. However, the large-scale integration of converters and renewable energy has greatly changed the operational characteristics of the traditional grid, especially transient voltage characteristics. The grid with proper ratio of GFM-converters to GFL-converters may have ideal transient voltage characteristics. This paper proposes a configuration method to determine the appropriate ratio between GFM and GFL converters based on the analysis of the stability of PLL to improve the stability of transient voltage.

articleTitle: DNN-Based Prediction Method of Optimal Load Shedding for Power System With High Penetration of Renewable Energy Under Typhoon Weather
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Extreme natural disasters such as typhoons have a serious impact on the power system, and the probability of power equipment failure will increase dramatically, bringing uncertainty that will affect the operation of the power system. And with the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources such as wind power in the power system, the uncertainty and volatility of the power system operation state have increased dramatically. In this paper, we consider optimal load shedding with N-1 faults in the power system as the research object, and in addition to considering branch openings, we also need to consider renewable energy sources and load fluctuations, and the proliferation of the number of scenarios brings about the problem of high computational cost and computational time. To address the above problems, a DNN-based prediction method of optimal load shedding for power system with high penetration of renewable energy under typhoon weather is proposed, which firstly constructs a wind farm scenario under the influence of typhoon, and then establishes a deep neural network-based optimal current model to effectively explore the nonlinear characteristics of nonlinear energy flow equations. Using the trained deep neural network model, the N -1 fault analysis results are obtained by input feature mapping, and the calculation results represented by load curtailment are obtained. Finally, the proposed method is analysed and validated by IEEE case 24 test system. Based on the validation, the proposed deep learning-based optimal curtailment load forecasting method for high percentage renewable energy grids under typhoon weather is able to calculate the power system state quickly and accurately.

articleTitle: Research on Evaluation Method of AC Filter Circuit Breaker Based on Fuzzy Hierarchy Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to improve the safe and stable operation ability of AC filter circuit breakers, an evaluation method for AC filter four-break circuit breakers based on fuzzy hierarchy method is proposed. Firstly, based on the analytic hierarchy method and gray theory, an index evaluation system based on breaking wear, time parameters and other factors is proposed. Secondly, a comprehensive evaluation model is established, and the comprehensive weights of each index are obtained by using the combined weighting method, which effectively avoids the problem that the single weight method is not objective and accurate. Then, the fuzzy evaluation algorithm is introduced into the comprehensive evaluation model of AC filter circuit breaker, and the comprehensive evaluation is realized. Finally, the evaluation results are compared with the maintenance results, which verifies the effectiveness of the evaluation method proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: 3D-CNN-Based Spatial Load Forecasting Method Considering the Spatial-Temporal Influences of Multi-Source Data on Loads among Adjacent Cells
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Accurate spatial load forecasting is an important aspect of distribution network planning and power equipment configuration. Current research in spatial load forecasting primarily relies on time series forecasting with insufficient consideration of the spatial influences among adjacent cells, which may not provide a comprehensive explanation for the development of spatial loads. Therefore, in this work, a spatial load forecasting method based on a three-dimensional convolutional neural network is proposed, taking into account the spatial-temporal influences of multi-source data on loads among adjacent cells. First, a three-dimensional data structure is proposed to establish a spatial-temporal dataset that incorporates the multi-source data into specific cells. Second, a spatial load forecasting method based on a three-dimensional convolutional neural network is proposed using the spatial-temporal dataset, which quantifies the nonlinear spatial-temporal influences of multi-source data on loads among adjacent cells in the target year. Finally, case studies on cells within an actual distribution network are performed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can quantify the spatial-temporal influences of multi-source data on loads among adjacent cells and provide relatively more accurate long-term spatial load forecasting results for these cells than trend extrapolation-based SLF methods.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Shared Energy Storage System based on TTU in Low Voltage Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Energy Storage System (ESS) plays a significant role in novel power system because of its capability to improve system the accommodation capacity of clean energy. The traditional approach of utilizing ESS is applying the grid-scale but individual one into a low voltage distribution network. Due to the inefficiency and high-cost of the individual implementation, shared ESS (SESS) is proposed which thought to be a more attractive approach to utilize ESS. In this paper, the design and control method of a four-terminal shared energy storage system is proposed and practically implemented to improve the utility of ESS and provide auxiliary service for low voltage distribution networks. Experiment results show that a shared is effective in improving both the accommodation capacity of photovoltaic power and the power quality.

articleTitle: A Scenario Generation Method for Wind, PV and Load Uncertainty Based on DFKM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As new energy sources such as wind and photovoltaic connected to the distribution network in large quantities, how to describe the uncertainty of wind, photovoltaic and load (WPL) variations and generate typical operating scenarios is becoming more and more important for the operation scheduling and planning of the distribution network. Aiming at the problems of traditional clustering methods, which are difficult to deal with high-dimensional data, the separation of feature extraction process and clustering process, and the lack of clustering performance, this paper proposes a scenario generation method based on deep fuzzy k-means (DFKM) for WPL uncertainty sources. First, based on one-dimensional convolutional auto-encoder, we extract the temporal coupling features of the WPL data, and then use the fuzzy k-means with adaptive loss function to perform clustering in the embedded low-dimensional feature space. In the model optimization process, the feature extraction process and the clustering process are combined to obtain the final clustering results and generate typical scenarios based on different types of centers. The example takes the historical data of a region in southeast China as the research object, then analyzes the clustering indexes to verify the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Control Method with Model Predictive Function of MMC-HVDC System under Unbalanced Grid Faults
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Modular multilevel converter (MMC) based high voltage direct current (HVDC) system is expected to continuously and stably deliver power with high quality during unbalanced grid faults. To improve fault ride-through capabilities, a comprehensive control method with model predictive function is proposed. Initially, the dynamic characteristics of MMC-HVDC system are analyzed in this paper. Sequence decoupled resonant controller is used for positive and negative sequence separation, as well as phase tracking of the unbalanced grid voltage. Subsequently, a finite set model predictive current control method is proposed, which designs a current reference generator, aiming at suppressing current distortion and power fluctuations. On this basis, the cost function for AC current and circulating current is given, and the reference current tracking is realized. Finally, an 11-level two-port MMC-HVDC system is built on MATLAB/Simulink platform, which verifies the effectiveness of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: Estimation of Optimal PV & ESS Installed Capacity in R&D Facility EMS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to achieve carbon neutrality, a policy to ensure that photovoltaic power generation becomes the main source of electricity in the Japanese power system has been established. Because of the constraints imposed by the spatio-temporal discrepancy between Photovoltaic (PV) power generation and electricity demand, the introduction of energy storage systems at the consumer side is also progressing. There have been suggestions put out regarding the implementation of an Energy Management System (EMS) that utilizes photovoltaic (PV) technology and energy storage systems. However, the effective functioning and administration of the local EMS have encountered challenges related to determining the appropriate capacity of PV generators, as well as long-term and short-term energy storage systems. This study involved the execution of a trial calculation and verification process to determine the most effective combination of photovoltaic (PV) systems and energy storage systems within a research and development (R&D) building energy management system (EMS). The objective was to formulate a more reasonable in-house Photovoltaic (PV) panel and energy storage systems (ESS) installed capacity, thereby enabling it to maintain system stability during operation. Based on the findings, it is recommended to offer clients who have not yet installed photovoltaic (PV) and energy storage systems with the most advantageous installation capacity and operational schedule.

articleTitle: Physics-Informed Appliance Signatures Generator for Energy Disaggregation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Energy disaggregation is a promising solution to access detailed information on energy consumption in a household, by itemizing its total energy consumption. However, in real-world applications, overfitting remains a challenging problem for data-driven disaggregation methods. First, the available real-world datasets are biased towards the most frequently used appliances. Second, both real and synthetic publicly-available datasets are limited in number of appliances, which may not be sufficient for a disaggregation algorithm to learn complex relations among different types of appliances and their states. To address the lack of appliance data, we propose two physics-informed data generators: one for high sampling rate signals (kHz) and another for low sampling rate signals (Hz). These generators rely on prior knowledge of the physics of appliance energy consumption, and are capable of simulating a virtually unlimited number of different appliances and their corresponding signatures for any time period. Both methods involve defining a mathematical model, selecting centroids corresponding to individual appliances, sampling model parameters around each centroid, and finally substituting the obtained parameters into the mathematical model. Additionally, by using Principal Component Analysis and Kullback-Leibler divergence, we demonstrate that our methods significantly outperform the previous approaches.

articleTitle: Application of Intelligent Optimized Adaptive Disturbance Rejection Control in Fuel Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The general efficiency of a proton exchange membrane fuel cell is correlated with the oxygen excessive ratio (OER). However, the regulation of OER is challenging to design because of systematic uncertainty and frequent fluctuations in load. For the purpose to track the optimal oxygen excessive ratio, this paper employs an active disturbance rejection controller. The particle swarm optimization finds the controller parameters based on the best tracking performance and the least amount of control adjustment. The simulation results show that the proposed control is superior to commonly PID controllers in terms of integral absolute error, overshoot, control variation, and adjustment trajectory.

articleTitle: Dynamic Performance of 6.5kV/400A SiC MOSFET Module and its Gate Driver
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Compared with traditional silicon devices, silicon carbide (SiC) device has outstanding advantages in high frequency, high voltage and high temperature applications. At present, most commercially available SiC devices are low voltage and low power SiC MOSFETs, the dynamic performance of high-voltage and high-current power modules is seldom reported. The dynamic performances of a newly developed SiC MOSFET module under different test environments are studied. The related gate drive for this high voltage SiC module is also discussed. From the aspects of driving resistance R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>, operating junction temperature Tj, load current Id, bus voltage V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ds</inf>, the dynamic and short-circuit characteristics of a 6.5kV/400A SiC MOSFET are fully evaluated. The experimental results will help to optimize the device design and engineering application for high-voltage, high-current SiC devices.

articleTitle: Intelligent Clustering and Trending Analysis of EV Charging Behavior in Active Distribution Power Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The infrastructure of electric vehicle (EV) charging stations plays an essential role in fulfilling the increasing penetration of EV in the modern power network due to the strong support from national policies. An effective EV charging network with coupling between urban and rural areas needs to be formed. Given the growing uncertainties caused by the EV charging behavior of various types of owners, it is crucial to fully understand the profiles of various EV charging behaviors and the potential growth of EV integration. This paper represents a novel framework that analyzes massive historical EV charging data through the electricity load collection system in power companies and automatically creates clusters differentiating various characteristics of low-voltage EV charging load for understanding the complex interaction between EV charging networks and the growing penetration of EVs using unsupervised machine learning and the Bass diffusion model. The effectiveness of the proposed methodologies is verified on actual EV data in Shaoxing Electric Power Supply Company in East China.

articleTitle: Low-Carbon Economic Dispatching of Electricity-Hydrogen-Gas Integrated Energy Systems Accounting for Hybrid Energy Storage and Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Under the background of “dual-carbon”, the hydrogen-containing integrated energy system with hydrogen as the energy carrier is an important support for the low-carbon transformation of China's energy industry. In order to ensure the supply of hydrogen energy in the hydrogen-containing integrated energy system and improve the economic efficiency. this paper builds a low-carbon economic dispatch model for the EHG-IES(EHG-IES), taking into account the balance of energy supply and demand, and the constraints on the operation of each unit, so as to fully tap the energy saving and emission reduction potentials of the system, and the potentials of consuming renewable energy. Taking a typical day's system operation as an example, the effectiveness of the method is verified through a comparative analysis of the system's optimized scheduling results for each source, operating costs, light energy utilization, and carbon emissions under four types of scenarios.

articleTitle: Optimization Control Strategy for Power Flow in Distribution Network Based on New Flexible Distribution Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the continuous integration of multiple new energy power sources and the variability of loads in the distribution network, the optimization and control challenges of distribution network flows have gradually emerged. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a new topology structure for flexible distribution transformers and elaborates on its working principle. Mathematical models for regulating converters, energy acquisition converters, and electromagnetic transformers in the device are constructed, and a comprehensive and refined mathematical model for flexible distribution transformers is derived. Based on this mathematical model, the working principle of power flow optimization control for flexible distribution transformers is theoretically analysed. A distribution network power flow optimization control strategy based on new flexible distribution transformer is proposed using the PI control principle, which enhances the flow control capability and ensures the reliable power supply and energy quality of important loads in the distribution network. Finally, a simulation test model for distribution network power flow optimization control is established using PSCAD/EMTDC. Through simulation testing and analysis, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is verified, and it exhibits good transient and steady-state response performance.

articleTitle: Research on Runoff Flow Prediction Based on Variational Mode Decomposition and PSO-SVM Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Runoff prediction is an important part of water level monitoring and warning, which is very important for hydropower generation and energy recycling. Traditional signal decomposition models are incompetent to effectively deal with the nonlinear and non-stationary characteristics of long time series runoff. In addition, machine learning methods of shallow learning need to be improved for runoff feature recognition. Therefore, variational modal decomposition (VMD) and support vector machine with particle swarm optimization (PSO-SVM) are effective solutions to complex runoff prediction and parameter optimization problems. Based on the runoff observed at Guoluo Station in the upper reaches of Yellow River, the characteristics of monthly and quarterly runoff are analyzed and forecasted. The experimental results show that the proposed scheme is significantly superior to other models in signal decomposition ability and prediction accuracy. It is expected that this work can provide practicability for short-term and medium-term river management and data utilization to improve the power supply capacity of various regions by rationally adjusting water levels.

articleTitle: Extraction of Demand Response Features of Industrial Typical Customers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Accurate extraction of demand response (DR) features of industrial typical customers is the premise to evaluate customers' DR potential. Existing DR features extraction methods ignore the differences in different time periods, which reduces the accuracy of the DR potential evaluation results. Given this background, an extraction method of DR features of industrial typical customers based on integrated empirical mode decomposition is proposed in this paper. Firstly, industrial typical customers are identified, and a method for decomposing the typical load sequence based on integrated empirical mode decomposition is proposed, which lay the foundation for extracting the DR features. Then, DR features of industrial typical customers are extracted based on the decomposition results. Finally, case studies on 263 invited DR customers show that the proposed method can effectively characterize industrial customers' DR features.

articleTitle: Cross-Zonal Long-Term ATC Calculation and Allocation Model Considering Generation Cost Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the continuous advancement of electricity market reform, the scale of cross-zonal transmission is increasingly expanding. It is imperative to enhance the utilization efficiency of transmission channels, reduce network congestion, and improve transaction efficiency in the construction of China's electricity market. Therefore, it is proposed to establish a cross-zonal long-term Available Transfer Capability (ATC) calculation and allocation model that takes into account the uncertainty of generation costs. This model employs a scenario-based modeling approach to generate representative scenarios for ranking generator unit prices. The probability of each scenario is obtained through the application of probability sampling. The physical calculation results of cross-zonal long-term ATC are then utilized as network constraints in the market clearing model, thereby deriving the market allocation results of cross-zonal long-term ATC. This approach facilitates the realization of resource optimization and allocation across a larger scope, ultimately maximizing social welfare. The underlying principles and validity of this model are briefly illustrated using a simple three-node system example.

articleTitle: An Extreme Scenario Reduction Algorithm for Multi-time Scale Net-Load
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the uncertainty of renewable energy power, the power system needs to apply various types of flexible resources to balance supply and demand on multiple time scales. For multi-timescale planning and scheduling problems, the construction of typical scenarios of source-load is inseparable. Extreme scenarios are particularly important for power systems. For this reason, an extreme scenario reduction algorithm based on multi-time scale net-load is proposed in this paper. The study proposes a multi-time scale decoupling method based on annual net-load, decomposing the time series into monthly, weekly, and daily scales, with the time scales representing different net-load features. A scenario reduction algorithm is proposed that can select typical scenarios while retaining extreme scenarios and assign corresponding probability values to the extreme scenarios. The algorithm example is analyzed using data from Zhejiang Province, China, for 2019 to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Economic Evaluation of Energy Storage Projects Based on DEA Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: There are many kinds of energy storage technologies with different characteristics. How to integrate the economic value and technical characteristics of different energy storage technologies, and perform multifunctional combination of energy storage projects in different application scenarios such as generation side, grid side and user side, so as to maximize the advantages of hybrid energy storage systems, is an urgent problem to be solved. In order to realize the comprehensive technical and economic evaluation of energy storage projects based on the combined benefits of multi-scenario functions, this paper firstly establishes the technical applicability index system, and uses the combination-empowerment-TOPSIS method to evaluate the applicability and comprehensive applicability of various scenarios for various types of energy storage technologies. Then, combined with the cost and benefit of energy storage technology, the evaluation index system of energy storage project benefit based on function combination is established, and the DEA evaluation model of operational benefit in typical scenarios is established. Finally, several kinds of energy storage and their combinations with high applicability scores were selected as the initial energy storage schemes to evaluate the benefits of different energy storage schemes and realize the comprehensive comparison of different energy storage schemes. Among them, the hybrid energy storage scheme of supercapacitor energy storage and lithium-ion battery has the highest comprehensive efficiency evaluation value, reaching 0.990, and has the best benefits.

articleTitle: Economy Analysis of Demand Response Combined with Different Energy Storage Configuration Modes in Data Centers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As an indispensable infrastructure in the foreseeable future, data centers have developed rapidly. The number and scale of data centers continue to grow with rapidly increased power consumption, becoming one of the elemental loads of the future power grid. To reduce energy consumption and improve profits of current data centers, this research focuses on the feasibility of configuring energy storage in data centers. By summarizing expenditure and earnings of configuring energy storage in the data center, a comprehensive optimization configuration model for electric and cold energy storage is constructed. While meeting the basic energy needs of both electric and cold energy, the configuration capacity and power of both cold and electrical energy storage are optimized to minimize the total cost of equal annual value within the system's life cycle. The economy of different energy storage combinations is compared and the optimal data center energy storage configuration mode is obtained.

articleTitle: Research on the Probability Prediction Method of Electricity Price Response Load based on CNNLSTM and Quantile Regression Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This article explores the importance of power load forecasting in the power industry, especially the uncertainty when considering dynamic electricity pricing factors. Traditional methods cannot handle the impact of electricity prices on load, so deep learning techniques, especially convolutional neural networks (CNN) and short-term memory networks (LSTM), have been introduced. These two networks, combined with quantile regression, are used for probability density load forecasting, providing a complete probability distribution of load demand and supporting the smart grid. This article provides a detailed introduction to the principles of CNN and LSTM networks, and explains the concept of quantile regression. The study validated the effectiveness of this method using an Australian dataset. Through this method, real-time electricity price factors can be better considered, the accuracy of power load forecasting can be improved, and strong support can be provided for the planning and operation of the power system.

Author Keywords: Probability prediction of electricity price response

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant Control Strategy for Three-Level ANPC Inverter Based on Finite-Time Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: An improved fault-tolerant control strategy is proposed for Active neutral point clamped (ANPC) multilevel inverter switches open-circuit faults. Unlike traditional fault-tolerant control methods, this method reconstructs switching sequence under different switches faults with high power quality and quickly balances the neutral point (NP) voltage using a finite-time controller (FTC). The finite-time NP potential controller is constructed to control the NP voltage by adjustment of the amplitude of the reference voltage in real time. Switching sequence is reconstructed by replacing redundant vector without increasing the number of switches and level-cross jump. Based on the finite time theory, the Lyapunov function is constructed and the finite time stability is proved, and it is concluded that the tracking error will converge to zero during a finite time. Compared with traditional PI control, the proposed control strategy can balance the NP much faster to achieve better performance, and there is no need to add any extra switches or hardware cost. Therefore, this scheme improves the reliability and robustness of the ANPC inverter. Simulation results confirm the feasibility and correctness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Observability Assessment and Optimal Placement of Measurement Terminals in Distribution Networks with Graph Theory and Intelligent Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As an essential part of power grids, it is crucial to measure and master the operation state of distribution networks in real time. This paper proposes an approach for observability assessment and optimal placement of measurement terminals in distribution networks. Based on existing measurement terminals, the approach searches observable islands by graph theory and then calculates an observability assessment indicator. When the system state is unobservable, an OPMT scheme is provided by intelligent optimization algorithms. By deploying a minimum number of measurement terminals, the approach ensures that the status of all nodes in the distribution network is observable, thereby reducing investment costs of measurement terminals and improving the situational awareness of distribution networks. The proposed approach is verified by case studies with the IEEE 123-node system and a real-world distribution network.

articleTitle: Coordinated Flexible Energy Operation Strategy for a CCHP System Under Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The combined cooling, heating, and power (CCHP) system enhance energy utilization efficiency by integrating different energy utilization methods. They offer reliable energy supply, reduce energy losses, and have environmentally friendly benefits. However, the challenge lies in managing the imbalance between energy generation and the diverse load demand within the CCHP system. In order to address this issue, a collaborative interaction strategy, termed “Source-Load,” has been introduced. Additionally, a two-stage robust optimization approach has been adopted to efficiently coordinate multiple energy flows within the CCHP system, accounting for uncertainties. Through simulation analysis, the proposed model and collaborative interaction strategy have been validated as effectively addressing this challenge.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization Scheduling Strategy for Virtual Power Plants Considering Green Certificate Trading and Carbon Trading
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the construction of a new power system and the implementation of carbon neutrality goals, the green and low-carbon operation of virtual power plants has become one of the important research directions. However, the economic efficiency of their optimized dispatch is affected by the constraints of the multi-market of green certificate - electricity - carbon and the uncertainties of wind power, photovoltaics, and electricity prices. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-objective optimization dispatch research method for virtual power plants considering green certificate trading and carbon trading. Through a comparative analysis of two cases, the specific benefits of virtual power plants participating in market trading are examined. The results verify that the proposed method can effectively consider the net benefits of various market transactions and provide references for virtual power plants participating in the green certificate - electricity - carbon market.

articleTitle: Analysis of Influencing Factors of Carbon Emission Based on LMDI Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To achieve carbon emission peak and neutrality, analyzing how factors influenced carbon emission has great significance. In order to analyze influencing factors of carbon emission, we should not only decompose carbon emission into several factors individually, but calculate effects of each factor. This paper firstly used LMDI model to analyze the relationship among carbon emission and some key factors, including per capita GDP, energy consumption structure, etc.. Then chose Fujian Province to calculate how these factors influence carbon emission in decade. Finally found five factors which has effects on carbon emission, and pointed out how to control these factors in order to decrease carbon emission in the future.

articleTitle: Research on Electricity Consumption of Industrial and Commercial Users Based on Electricity Price Adjustment Policy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The study focuses on analyzing the impact of electricity price policy adjustments on the electricity consumption of industrial and commercial users in Zhejiang Province, based on survey data from 2021. The paper examines the price elasticity of electricity consumption for industrial and commercial users under different electricity price fluctuations scenarios using OLS (Ordinary Least Squares), ordered logit, and ordered probit methods. The results show that the electricity consumption of most industrial and commercial users in various industries is inelastic. The main factors influencing the electricity price elasticity of industrial users are voltage grade, electricity consumption scale, electricity cost, and electricity price grade.

articleTitle: Li-ion Battery SOH Estimation Based on BO-SVR Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The State of Health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries is a crucial aspect of battery management system, playing a significant role in ensuring the reliable operation of the battery. To improve the accuracy of SOH estimation for lithium-ion batteries, a SOH estimation method based on Bayesian Optimization-Support Vector Regression (BO-SVR) is proposed. Firstly, the voltage information during the relaxation phase of each cycle process is transformed into five health indicators to characterize the capacity degradation. Pearson coefficient analysis is then utilized to assess the correlation between these health indicators and battery capacity under various cycling conditions, filtering out the health indicators highly correlated with battery capacity degradation as SOH features. Subsequently, Bayesian optimization is introduced to optimize the hyperparameters of SVR model. Finally, the Bayesian Optimization-eXtreme Gradient Boosting (BO-XGBoost) model is served as a comparison model to validate the accuracy of the proposed model using a public dataset.

articleTitle: Wind-Solar Coordinated Optimization of Port Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To fulfill the “dual-carbon” strategy, distributed power generation utilizing natural clean resources such as wind and light has become a major trend. As one of the scenarios with large loads, ports urgently need to reorganize the power layout to achieve the transformation of energy structure. Therefore, this paper establishes a two-layer model for distributed power capacity allocation in port microgrids. The upper-level long-term planning model takes into account the annual investment and operation costs of the system, total abandoned wind and light rate, and power quality factors at distributed energy grid-connected points for optimal allocation; the lower-level short-term operation model optimizes scheduling with the goal of minimizing typical intra-day operating costs. The IEEE-33 system is used to validate the proposed power capacity allocation method, and the power quality levels of the power capacity allocation results are evaluated. The results show that the access of distributed power supply can greatly reduce the total cost, and the inclusion of power quality factor can guide the configuration results so that the power quality of the microgrid can be improved. The effectiveness of the distributed power configuration model for port microgrid proposed in this paper is proved.

articleTitle: A New Planning Model of Total Supply Capability of Distribution Network Based on Equivalent Bus
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the existing model of total supply capability, the low-voltage side buses are totally ignored. The connection was described as the feeder link from transformer to transformer. It leads to two incorrect considerations in calculation based on this model, which obviously produce errors. In this paper, a method applying equivalent bus is proposed to reformulate the model of total supply capability. Firstly, the supply transfer process after a transformer failure in actual operation was analyzed to clarify the consideration of this work, and proposed the equivalent bus; Secondly, through examples and inferences, the stable connection between equivalent bus and transformer was revealed. Thirdly, a new model of total supply capability was proposed based on the stable connection of equivalent bus, which considered the constraint of the low-voltage buses. Finally, the new model was tested in a simple distribution system with three substations, and a solution of building up the connection between equivalent bus and transformer was introduced. As the results, the calculation based on this model proposed the supply capabilities of transformers and substations, and the load distributions of buses, equivalent buses and feeders, which conclude a total error of 0.34% of the total supply capability.

articleTitle: Research on AHP-EW Based Comprehensive Capacity Evaluation of Electricity Selling Companies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The reform of the electric power system makes a large number of power selling companies enter the electric power market, and the increase of the number of power selling entities also increases the market competition. Therefore, only by improving their comprehensive capacity can power selling companies develop in the changing electric power market in the long run. Therefore, this paper first constructs the comprehensive capacity evaluation index system of power selling companies, then uses the combination weighting method combining the analytic hierarchy process and entropy weight method to calculate the weight of the evaluation index, and finally uses the data of ten power selling companies for example analysis, combines expert scoring and index weight to calculate the comprehensive score of power selling companies and puts forward suggestions for the long-term development of power selling companies.

articleTitle: Demand response-based operation optimization of a typical industrial and agricultural IES
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Irrigation, metallurgy and other industrial with agricultural users are characterized by large loads and high regularity of electricity consumption. Participation in demand response can play a huge role in building a new power system. At the same time, on the basis of the regulating capacity of the multi-energy flow integrated energy system, the adjustable capacity of demand-side resources can be further improved. To this end, first, various equipment loads are modeled, and a calculation model is proposed that takes into account the respective operating characteristics of various equipment and their response characteristics to the grid.Secondly, an integrated energy system for agriculture and industry that includes irrigation, metallurgy, and multiple types of energy storage/loads will be studied. A multi-energy system economic dispatch model considering demand-side response is constructed while considering time-sharing tariffs to find the optimal strategy for the system to participate in demand response. Finally, an arithmetic example is analyzed based on the operational data of an actual park. The results show that the proposed strategy can participate in the demand response while meeting the system energy requirements, and the results of the case analysis verify the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed model and strategy.

articleTitle: Optimization Model of Unit Commitment Considering Nonconvex Cost Characteristics of Coal-Fired Unit Deep Peak Shaving
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the nonconvex cost characteristics of coal-fired unit deep peak shaving, this paper first analyzes the non-convexity of the total operating cost of coal-fired power units. Secondly, it establishes an optimization model for unit scheduling that takes into account the non-convexity of deep peak shaving costs of coal-fired power units, proposes a linearization method for nonconvex cost curves, and transforms the problem into a mixed integer linear programming problem. Finally, based on provincial power grid data, the effectiveness of the model is verified through simulation.

articleTitle: Real-Time Wholesale Electricity Pricing for Power Systems with Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a prediction-free online algorithm to determine real-time electricity prices for a power system with energy storage. Starting from an offline optimization model that minimizes the overall operation cost of the power system, we apply the Lyapunov optimization technique to turn the model into its online counterpart. Two propositions regarding the feasibility and optimality of the proposed online algorithm are proven theoretically. Simulation results on the IEEE 39-bus system demonstrate the effectiveness of the model in achieving cost minimization and efficient utilization of resources.

articleTitle: Research on Load-Transfer Capacity Analysis and Network Reconstruction Method for Large City Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The structure of multi-section and multi-contact is widely used in the large city distribution networks. At present, research on load transfer and network reconstruction in distribution networks rarely considers multi-section and multi-contact structures, which cannot be applied to large city distribution networks. Therefore, this paper proposes a load transfer capacity analysis and network reconstruction method suitable for large city distribution networks. A model based on ordered tree topology is established considering multi-section and multi-contact construction. Adopting dynamic topology analysis method, an accurate calculation method for the load-transfer areas of multi-contact lines in the N-1 case is proposed. A linear programming model for network reconfiguration optimization is established to realize the balanced distribution of load on tie-lines in multi-contact distribution networks. The actual case analysis results prove the effectiveness and practical value of the method.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Industrial Load Adjustable Capability Considering Technological Processes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Industrial users with large electricity consumption and strong load regularity are important participants in demand response programs. Considering the impact of production processes on the actual adjustment ability of electrical equipment, a method for analyzing the adjustable capability of industrial load based on interpretative structural modeling is proposed. The multilevel hierarchical directed graph of electrical equipment involved in the production processes is established to sort out their correlation relationships, based on which the total adjustable load capability of the industrial user can be evaluated from bottom to top. Compared to user-level evaluation methods driven by load data, the proposed method is equipment-level and can better guide industrial users to choose suitable electrical equipment for load reduction, rather than simply shutting down production lines.

articleTitle: A Chance-Constrained AGC Power Sharing Scheme Considering the SOC of BESSs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESSs) are widely recognized as a quality power source for participation in Automatic Generation Control (AGC) with the rapid penetration of the renewables in grids. Typically, the optimal power-sharing scheme for BESSs is concerned with maximizing system stability or minimizing total cost. Therefore, this paper proposes a chance-constrained AGC power-sharing scheme to balance the system's stability and cost. Specifically, the SOC punishment factor (S-PF) is introduced in its cost function. The numerical simulation results demonstrate that, with the proposed scheme, the BESSs have low operating costs and are with strong stability.

articleTitle: Study and Verification of Covert Channels for Process Layer Network in Smart Substations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The covert channel is a dangerous cyber-attack threat to industry control networks; however, it is a lack of specific research for the network environment of smart substations. Existing studies merely explore the theoretical existence of covert channels in substation networks without building and verifying. In this paper, the process layer network environment of substations has been analyzed and potential information hiding schemes are proposed for covert channels. Furthermore, a laboratory simulation environment is developed to verify the efficacy of transmitting covert information. Results demonstrate that these covert channels can successfully transmit data while remaining undetectable by existing network detection equipment.

articleTitle: Deduction Simulation of Industrial Flexible Load Based on CEEMDAN-VMD-GRU
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: randomness and fluctuation of short-term power load are strong, and the traditional load forecasting method is difficult to grasp the law of short-term load change. In order to improve the accuracy of short-term power load forecasting, a method of short-term power load forecasting for industrial flexible loads is proposed, which Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise) (CEEMDAN), Varational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Gate Recurrent Unit) (GRU). The original load sequence was extracted from the data set and decomposed into multiple intrinsic mode functions (IMF) by using CEEMDAN. Then, the components with large fluctuations were decomposed twice by VMD to effectively reduce their instability. The GRU network was used to analyze the temporal characteristics of each component, and multiple prediction results were obtained. The final load prediction results are obtained by superimposing the forecast results in reverse normalization. The proposed method is compared with the reference model and other literature methods through practical examples, and the results show that the proposed method can accurately grasp the law of load change, and the accuracy of the daily load prediction problem is 96.60%.

articleTitle: Hardware-in-the-Loop and Field Demonstration Towards Voltage Regulation in Distribution System Considering Adjustable Inverter Air Conditioners
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The voltage quality of distribution systems is facing challenges due to the increasing intermittency and uncertainty of renewable energy generation. In contrast to the traditional regulation method, the demand response through regulating demand-side resources' power consumption is gaining greater attention. Inverter air conditioners (IACs) have a high percentage in the demand-side resources and have huge regulation potential for distribution system voltage regulation services. However, considering the large scale and complexity of the distribution system, most previous studies on IACs' voltage regulation are verified only by simulation tools, e.g., Simulink and Pandapower. This study demonstrates a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) platform for voltage regulation by realistic IACs with a real time digital simulator. The voltage sensitivity matrix evaluates the number of IACs participating in the voltage regulation. A modified IEEE 33-node distribution system with fluctuating photovoltaic generation is used to validate the proposed method. The experiment results show that the proposed method effectively maintains voltage stability in the distribution system.

articleTitle: Study on Interface Performance of Fiber Optic Hard Composite Insulator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Fiber optic composite insulator has the function of online monitoring of insulator operation status and real-time communication. At present, interface problems are common in fiber optic composite insulator. Flashover and internal insulation accidents occur during operation, and the operating life is much lower than that of ordinary composite insulator. In this paper, a new design of optical fiber composite insulator is proposed. The cycloaliphatic epoxy resin with good interface performance is used as the coating layer of optical fiber and the housing material of insulator, which reduces the number of interfaces between core- fiber-housing to improve the interface performance of optical fiber insulator. The samples were subjected to a long-term boiling aging test to measure the interface performance gap between the fiber optic hard composite insulator, the silicone rubber fiber optic composite insulator and the ordinary composite insulator by leakage current. Comparing the leakage current measurements, the interface performance of fiber optic hard composite insulator is better than that of ordinary fiber optic composite insulator in the same boiling aging time. The increase of the number of implanted optical fibers has no significant effect on the interface performance. This study shows that by using cycloaliphatic epoxy resin as the coating layer of optical fiber and the housing material of insulator can effectively improve the interface performance, which lays a foundation for long-term operation monitoring in the future.

articleTitle: A Low-Carbon Economic Operation Method of Green Virtual Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the proliferation of renewable energies, the consumption of renewable power has been a hot potato with considerations of the uncertainty and randomness. This paper proposes a green virtual power plant model to promote the consumption of renewable power and build a low-carbon society. A low-carbon economic operation model is proposed for the green virtual power plant model from the perspective of social welfare. Then, a distributed interactive algorithm based on the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers theory is proposed to solve the operation model and protect the privacy of participants. The effectiveness of the low-carbon economic operation model is tested on a green virtual power plant consisted of one wind power producer and four power consumers. Simulation results show that the proposed method can promote the consumptions of renewable power and reduce the total operation cost significantly.

articleTitle: Review on Modeling of Impact of Extreme Weather on Source-Grid-Load-Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Source-Grid-Load-Storage (SGLS) is an important part of a power system, and each part affects the safe operation of the power system. In extreme weather conditions, the SGLS link in the power system will be affected. This article starts from the four aspects of “source-grid-load-storage”, first analyzing the impact of normal weather and extreme weather on power system operation, then modeling the “source-grid-load-storage” based on several typical extreme weather scenarios, and then presenting several technical solutions to cope with extreme weather. Finally, the related issues of “source-grid-load-storage” and the future development direction are summarized.

articleTitle: The Economic and Environmental Benefits of Second-Life Batteries Applied in the Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Second-life batteries (SLBs) have attracted increasing attention due to their high remaining capacity and great potential market. Once not handled properly, SLBs will harm the environment and lead to resource waste. However, SLBs also have advantages such as low price and free carbon emission during production. Therefore, it is highly significant to build up effective pricing mechanisms and a clear assessment of economic and environmental benefits for SLBs. To evaluate the benefits of using SLBs, this paper introduces a pricing model for SLBs and integrates them into the power system planning model. The research investigates the impact of SLBs on carbon emission reduction and cost advantages. Ultimately, the study provides compelling evidence that leveraging SLBs can effectively lower power supply costs while making substantial contributions to achieving carbon neutrality.

articleTitle: Distribution System Recovery Method Based on Virtual Synchronous Generator Technology of Distributed New Energy Generator After Natural Disasters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To improve the frequency response of the distribution system after extreme natural disasters, a distribution system recovery method based on virtual synchronous generator (VSG) technology is proposed to solve the problem of frequency stability caused by large-scale distributed new energy generators access in the distribution system after extreme disasters. Firstly, a mathematical model is established to control the interface inverter of distributed new energy generators using VSG. Secondly, based on the rotor motion equation and the mechanical power response model of the generator, the expressions of the initial frequency change rate and the lowest frequency of the system are derived, which are used as the frequency constraints in the post-disaster recovery process of the distribution system, and the linearization method of nonlinear constraints is given. Then, in order to maximize the load-weighted recovery, taking into account operational constraints, frequency constraints, and topology constraints, and the post disaster load recovery problem of the multi-time distribution system is modeled as a mixed integer linear programming (MILP) model, and solved using a commercial solver. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed recovery method are verified by the improved IEEE 13 node and IEEE 37 node distribution system standard examples.

articleTitle: Critical Line Identification Method Considering Horizontal and Vertical Two-Way Volatility Adapted to Medium and Long-Term Transactions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: There are more and more trading entities in the electricity market, and the network is becoming more and more complex, which reduces the efficiency of transaction calculation. For medium and long-term transactions, critical lines play an absolute role in transactions. In order to deal with the problem of accurate and reasonable identification of key transmission lines, a dynamic comprehensive evaluation method of key transmission lines in power grid considering medium and long-term transaction and uncertainty of new energy is proposed. Firstly, from the two aspects of transaction and operation, the key line identification index considering medium and long-term transaction is proposed to measure the importance and blocking degree of transmission lines in power grid topology. Then, the key line index considering the horizontal and vertical two-way volatility is proposed to measure the degree of high uncertainty. Finally, the identification of critical lines based on RSR is proposed to fully measure the importance of lines in the power grid. The simulation results of IEEE39 node system show that the method is effective and reasonable.

articleTitle: A Composite-Window-Based Load Event Detection Method in Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Load event detection is the fundamental step in event-based Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM). Accurate detection of the complete transient process of events can effectively improve the subsequent event-based appliance state identification and load disaggregation. However, it is challenging for the existing methods to cope with the significant variances in the duration of events of different types. Moreover, load fluctuation and noise can also affect the detection accuracy. From this point, this paper proposes a load event detection method based on the composite-window strategy. The proposed method first utilizes the central sub-window to detect the edge of load events and tunes the window length by moving the other two sub-windows to cope with the various durations of events. Subsequently, the proposed method detects the start and end points of the events based on the principle of change point detection. Finally, the fluctuating events are identified and filtered out based on their waveform characteristics. Experiments conducted on the private and public BLUED datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the two benchmarks in general.

articleTitle: Soft Open Point Planning Method for Active Distribution Network Based on Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the continuous increase of the penetration rate of distributed generation (DG) in the distribution network, higher requirements have been put forward for the dependable and cost-effective operation of the distribution network. In order to address the impact caused by the intermittent output of a large number of DGs on the distribution network, this article proposes a planning method for soft open point (SOP) using generative adversarial network (GAN). First, to accurately simulate the operating characteristics of DG, a GAN is employed for sce-nario generation. Then, operational constraints for distribution networks with SOP are proposed, with the objective function being the minimization of annual total cost. By relaxing and linearizing the original non-convex and non-linear constraints, a second-order cone programming model is derived, and the objective function is solved under the constraints. Finally, the proposed scenario generation algorithm and planning model are analyzed and veriffed on the IEEE 33- node test system.

articleTitle: Active Bypass Control for Fault Tolerant Operation of Cascaded Three-Level Neutral-Point-Clamped Converters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The fault tolerant operation of the cascaded three-level neutral-point-clamped converter (C3L-NPC) is investigated in the paper. In the presence of fault conditions of submodules (SMs), the dc side of the fault SM is bypassed to ensure the continuous operation of system. The bypass operation is achieved by controlling the IGBT device on an additional circuit to smoothly discharge the dc capacitor. This scheme makes the bypass operation controllable, thereby effectively suppressing the discharge current of the dc capacitor. To achieve this, a buck-boost bypass circuit is added in the dc side, so the discharge current can be controlled through a current controller. The effectiveness of the presented method has been verified through simulation in PLECS. Results show that the fault SMs can be smoothly and safely bypassed by the IGBTs without exceeding the maximum current and junction temperature.

articleTitle: MDRAE: An Attention Mechanism-Based Autoencoder for Missing Data Recovery in Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Smart grids have rapidly developed in recent years, and a large amount of data has been collected and become the basis for decision-making of power grid operation. To ensure the safe and stable operation of the power grid, how to improve the data quality of the collected data has become an important research topic. Therefore, an attention mechanism-based autoencoder is proposed in this paper for missing data recovery to improve data quality in smart grids. The proposed method named missing data recovery autoencoder (MDRAE) contains two parts of an encoder and a decoder, and the attention mechanism is integrated into the encoder part to better extract the key information of the data. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by conducting experiments on two datasets including industrial load data and residential load data. The experimental results show that the model performance of the proposed method is better than that of the two benchmarks, and the proposed method can recover the missing data accurately.

articleTitle: Harnessing ERA5 Reanalysis Data for Improved Long-Term Rainfall Forecasting in Southern Iran
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Accurate long-term precipitation forecasts are important for water resource management and disaster prevention. Traditional precipitation forecasting is mainly a statistical analysis method. In recent years, methods based on machine learning have been widely used. However, it is an ongoing challenge to improve the accuracy of precipitation prediction. Therefore, this study proposes a long-term precipitation forecasting method based on decision trees intending to improve the accuracy of precipitation prediction. This study designed algorithm comparison experiments and evaluated various machine learning models for precipitation forecasting in Fars province located in the south of Iran, respectively. In this study, the ERA5 reanalysis dataset is used to make predictions of precipitation status. The results show that the prediction accuracy of XGBoost can reach 72% and the root mean square error is only 0.023K, which greatly improves the accuracy of monthly precipitation prediction in Fars province and also provides a new research idea for the development of machine learning in the field of precipitation prediction.

articleTitle: Cooling Load Prediction for Data Center Based on Re-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: For the load prediction for the data center, the traditional methods cover the thermal modeling process and data-driven models. The thermal modeling process takes a long time to generate prediction results. However, some historical data of the data center is not available due to the data encryption for the sake of data security, making the traditional data-driven models challenging. This paper proposed the Re-LSTM model based on the LSTM block and shortcut connection with the selected features as prior knowledge for the untrained model. The proposed model could handle the insufficient operation data and decrease the training cost to improve construction efficiency. As for the training results of different models, the proposed Re-LSTM demonstrated a significantly remarkable improvement compared with the data-driven model. The training time of Re-LSTM is around three times less than other models. By means of the Re-LSTM, the cooling load could be predicted accurately and efficiently, and it is practical to predict the cooling load when the operation data is not accessible.

articleTitle: Dynamic Equivalence Algorithm for AC-DC Hybrid System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the large-scale integration of new energy and the sustained growth of the number of high-voltage DC lines, the operational characteristics of power grid in China have undergone profound changes, and the security and stability of the power grid is facing enormous challenges. Studying the stability of large-scale AC-DC hybrid power grid is of great significance for the development of power grid in China. However, the large-scale AC-DC hybrid power grid has many dynamic components and complex topology structure, which is limited by hardware resources and difficult to accurately model each component. Therefore, it is necessary to combine dynamic equivalence algorithm to reduce the system scale while ensuring simulation accuracy. A dynamic equivalence algorithm for AC-DC hybrid power grid is proposed in this paper, which preserves the main network and simplifies the low-voltage power supply areas. The algorithm can ensure that the bus voltage, power flow distribution, short-circuit current, etc. of the main network are basically consistent before and after equivalence, with low computational complexity and fast calculation speed. The effectiveness of the algorithm is verified through simulation verification and comparative analysis of the power grid of a certain city in China before and after equivalence.

articleTitle: Integrated Energy System Dynamic Simulation Toolbox Based on Refined Modeling Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Integrated energy system (IES) is an efficient energy utilization system that organically combines different forms of energy, which can realize the comprehensive utilization of energy, improve the efficiency of the energy system, reduce energy consumption. It is one of the important ways for energy transformation and upgrading. Dynamic modeling of IES realize its state analysis, day-ahead scheduling, and operation control. Based on the MATLAB/Simulink platform, this paper focuses on the research of integrated energy dynamic refined modeling, builds a dynamic model library containing gas and heat network pipeline models, combined heat and power generation (CHP) model, and a toolbox to realize the dynamic simulation of gas and heat coupling network. Finally, this paper sets up examples for simulation analysis to verify the feasibility and adaptability of the dynamic model library of the toolbox. It provides the model basis and implementation method for the subsequent dynamic refined modeling and IES dispatch optimization. The results prove that the toolbox is highly expandable, widely adaptable, and simple in simulation operation.

articleTitle: WGAN-GP Based Data Reconstruction for Operational Faults of Power Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Accurate and rapid fault diagnosis is crucial for the safe and stable operation of distribution networks. Although artificial intelligence gains popularity in fault diagnosis for distribution networks, the imbalance in the proportion of fault data and normal operational data hampers accurate diagnosis. To address this problem, a fault data enhancement model for distribution networks using the Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP) is proposed. WGAN-GP uses the Wasserstein distance as the training target and introduces a gradient penalty mechanism to make the training process more controllable and efficient. Compared to the GAN-based method, WGAN-GP reduces the average relative error for nine dimensions in the standard deviation from 18.30% to 5.30% and in the mean from 4.03% to 0.48%, Compared with the probabilistic statistical based method, WGAN-GP greatly reduces the Wasserstein distance between real and generated data. Experimental results reveal that WGAN-GP can generate higher-quality data and solve the problem of data imbalance in power fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: A Forecasting-aided State Estimator Based on Enhanced Autoformer-UPF for Active Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In response to the issue of incomplete measurement configurations in active distribution networks, which leads to limited accuracy in traditional state estimation and subsequently results in decreased estimation precision, this paper introduces a Forecasting-aided state estimator for active distribution networks based on an enhanced Autoformer-UPF framework. The proposed Forecasting-aided State Estimator employs a predictive model based on Autoformer, and utilizes the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) for hyperparameter optimization to enhance estimation accuracy. Leveraging its multi-head self-attention mechanism, this model significantly improves prediction accuracy for long time series data, consequently enhancing the precision of state estimation. Simulation results on the IEEE 39-bus standard system demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method under both normal operating conditions and scenarios with presence of bad data.

articleTitle: A Lithium Battery SOC Estimation Method Based on AEKF-Composite Neural Network Hybrid Driven Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Lithium-ion battery State of Charge signifies the battery's remaining usable capacity and significantly impacts the stability and efficiency of new energy systems. Accurate State of charge (SOC) estimation is critical as renewable energy integration into the grid increases. This study explores a method for precise SOC estimation in lithium-ion batteries. We utilize the adaptive extended Kalman filter algorithm (AEKF), a model-based approach that adjusts noise covariance matrices based on measurement residuals, enhancing both accuracy and robustness in SOC estimation. Compared to the conventional extended Kalman filter, which assumes constant noise covariance matrices, the adaptive version demonstrates superior SOC estimation performance. Additionally, we introduce a self-correcting composite neural network prediction module, a data-driven technique that improves SOC estimation accuracy and robustness. It leverages historical data and model-based estimations to train a neural network capable of correcting estimation errors. Our proposed method combines the strengths of both model-based and data-driven approaches, and experimental results confirm its effectiveness and superiority.

articleTitle: Model Driven Based PMU Data Calibration Method Considering Time-Varying Characteristics of Line Parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The paper proposes a model driven PMU phase data calibration method to address the issue of PMU phase data errors caused by UTC time tag. Firstly, at a short-term scale, it is considered that the line parameters are fixed. The distribution parameter model of the transmission line was simplified using correction coefficients, and the simulation results showed that the accuracy met the requirements. Based on this, a π type equivalent model was established. By utilizing the mutual calculation of PMU data at both ends within the same time period, the available PMU data segments are determined. Combined with the equivalent model of the transmission line, PMU phase data calibration is achieved; Secondly, at a long-term scale, it is considered that the line parameters are unknown. Constrained by the basic relationship between voltage and current in the transmission line model, multiple sets of PMU data at different time periods are used to obtain the calculated values of resistance parameters. Through the variation trend of resistance in the parameter conversion formula, the available PMU data segments are determined then the line parameters within the current time period are obtained and brought into the transmission line model, to achieve the calibration of PMU phase data.

articleTitle: Calculation Model of Firm Generation Capacity for Wind-Solar-Hydro Complementary Generation System with Hybrid Pumped Storage Stations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Firm generation capacity (FGC) is a vital metric to assess the stability of power generation for renewable energy like wind, solar, and hydropower. Considering the uncertainty of generation resources, a first-order seasonal model based on Copula function is employed to stochastically simulate the output of wind, solar power, and natural inflow of hydropower. An FGC calculation model for the wind-solar-hydro complementary generation system with hybrid pumped storage stations (HPSS) is constructed subsequently. Case studies indicate that hybrid pumped storage units effectively enables seasonal energy regulation through reservoirs, thus enhancing the stability of power generation in the system. Furthermore, the installed capacity of HPSS impacts FGC of the system effectively, both FGC and the accommodation capacity for wind and solar power exhibit a nearly linear growth trend with the expansion of the installation.

articleTitle: Study on Complex-LSTM Photovoltaic Output Prediction Model Considering Reactive Power Distribution
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Accurate photovoltaic power generation prediction is key to daily grid dispatch management and secure, stable operation. The reactive power control method of photovoltaic power stations is related to the system operation status, which indirectly affects the relationship between reactive and active power outputs. Therefore, reactive information can be used to further improve the accuracy of photovoltaic active power output prediction. This paper proposes a distributed photovoltaic active-reactive power collaborative prediction method based on Complex Long Short-Term Memory networks (C-LSTM). First, the active power and reactive power are combined into a complex number, which then serves as an input to the C-LSTM. N ext, a photovoltaic power output prediction model based on complex convolution layers and Long Short-Term Memory networks is established, demonstrating stronger temporal feature extraction capabilities. Finally, a variety of methods are used to process and predict photovoltaic power using simulation verification.
