The results show that this method can improve the prediction accuracy of photovoltaic power output to a certain extent.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Robustness of a Transmission Line Network using Available Transfer Capacity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing size of power system networks, disturbances within the network are more frequent and severe. Therefore, modern power system networks are made more robust to withstand such disturbances and failures. Generally, contingency analysis is performed and various metrics are calculated to evaluate the robustness of a power system network in terms of its ability to handle the loss of critical components and maintain reliable operation. A robustness index quantifies the robustness of the system and provides valuable insights into how well a system can handle uncertainties, variations and disturbances. Therefore, calculation of such indices is critical for risk management, decision-making, optimization, and ensuring the reliability and safety of power system networks. For practicability and quick decision making, calculation of robustness index must be easy and computationally inexpensive. In this paper, we propose a simple and easily calculated robustness index, Available Transfer Capacity Robustness Index (ATCRI), on the basis of single line contingency analysis. A method to calculate the ATCRI is presented and used to quantify the robustness of a real system of transmission line network and provide the robustness information. The results are then compared with Active Power Flow Loss (APFL) index, which is a commonly used robustness index, for validation.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement of Hybrid Energy Storage for Mitigating Renewable Energy Generation Fluctuations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the ever-evolving landscape of the power system, the penetration of wind and solar renewable energy sources into the grid has steadily increased. However, the resulting intermittency of wind and solar power generation poses challenges to the stability of the power system. This paper presents a model for the Hydrogen Capacitor Hybrid Storage System (HC-HSS), comprising a Hydrogen Storage System (HSS) and a Super Capacitor System (SCS). Building upon a detailed modeling of material and energy flows within the HSS, a cost-effective method for mitigating wind and solar power fluctuations is proposed. Additionally, power allocation strategies are developed to accommodate the distinct characteristics of energy storage. The model is solved using a particle swarm optimization algorithm, and case studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the hybrid energy storage configuration and the proposed power allocation strategy.

articleTitle: Application Analysis of Energy Storage System in Wind Turbine Frequency Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In wind turbine applications, the energy storage system (ESS) functions as a stabilizing entity, addressing the discrepancies between wind power output and load demand. The ESS possesses significant advantages: its rapid responsiveness, bidirectional adjustment capabilities, and its operation unaffected by the wind turbine's operational state. This research examines the frequency modulation in wind turbines and assesses the ESS's involvement in this context. We conducted tests to gauge the ESS's efficiency in ensuring consistent power output from wind turbines and thwarting abrupt shifts in system frequency. The findings reveal that integrating the ESS into wind turbine operations effectively minimizes power fluctuations and offers reliable frequency modulation performance.

articleTitle: Li-ion Battery SOH Estimation Model Based on Finite Sampling in Relaxation Phase
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Accurately estimating the state of health of Li-ion battery is crucial for the safe operation of battery energy system. The effectiveness of features can be influenced by temperature variations and nonzero State of Charge. However, the relaxation phase after fully charged is relatively unaffected by the charging process. Therefore, this study proposed constructing relevant geometric features by extracting a finite number of voltage sampling points from the relaxation phase. Subsequently, the Pearson correlation analysis is performed on the derived geometric features, followed by the application of Principal Component Analysis to further reduce feature dimensionality, eliminating redundant information and decreasing the overall complexity of the model. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed features is validated using Kernel Ridge Regression and Support Vector Regression models for NCA and NCM batteries across diverse temperature cycling conditions. The results indicate that the proposed SOH estimation model maintains a high level of accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Operational Reliability Assessment Approach Considering Sample Imbalance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Operational reliability assessment is an important approach to evaluate the potential risk in the new power systems. However, the accumulated computation burden from calculating thousands of scenes in operational reliability assessment still challenges the advanced solving algorithm. To address this issue, data-driven approaches using neural networks are proposed. However, existing approaches suffer from imbalanced samples because the possibility of load shedding is extremely low. To this end, this paper proposes an intelligent operational reliability assessment approach considering sample imbalance. Specifically, the imbalanced load-shedding sample extension method is proposed based on the generative adversarial network to deal with the imbalance of the load-shedding samples in the training dataset. Besides, a novel loss function is constructed with a specific focus on the load-shedding buses. This learning strategy helps the neural networks capture the features of the imbalanced shedding loads in different buses. Finally, simulation results in the IEEE 39-bus and 118-bus systems demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve an obvious improvement in evaluation accuracy and facilitate online evaluation.

articleTitle: Game Strategies for the Thermal Power Plant and Building Clusters Considering Ground Level Concentrations of Atmospheric Pollutants
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The vast majority of thermal power plants burn coal to generate electricity and produce atmospheric pollutants. However, due to cost and other factors, the application of flue gas desulphurization, denitrification and dedusting technologies in thermal power plants is still being improved and promoted, so there is still a need to consider atmospheric pollutants generated by thermal power plants when studying the optimization of power systems. To this end, this paper proposes a Stackelberg game strategy for the thermal power plant and building clusters considering ground level concentrations of atmospheric pollutants. The Gaussian puff diffusion model is employed to describe the spatiotemporal distribution of atmospheric pollutants, which affects the cost of the thermal power plant and the game strategy. A joint electricity-heat optimization model is established for multi-type building clusters. The IbI Logic Algorithm (ILA) nested CPLEX solver is simulated in MATLAB, and the example results show that the optimization strategy proposed in the paper can ensure the quality of the ground environment while maximizing the benefits of each subject.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Power Flow Violation Adjustment Method Based on Adversarial Process
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Adjusting the power flow mode is vital for daily power system operation. However, with the increase in power system scale and uncertainty, it is tougher to ensure the N-l critics when adjusting the power flow mode. To this end, this paper proposes an intelligent power flow violation adjusting method based on adversarial process to meet N-l verification. While any branch power flow or voltage magnitude violation occurs in the N-1 verification, it can intelligently generate a new power flow mode to satisfy the N-l verification by changing node injection power, e.g., adjusting the generation of generators or renewable resources, shedding loads, and transfer loads. Firstly, the functional relationship between the power flow input and output under the N-l multiple topologies is constructed based on the fully connected neural network (FCN). Then, the power flow violation adjusting method is constructed based on the adversarial process of the power flow calculation neural networks. Finally, through simulations of the IEEE 30-bus system, it is verified that the proposed intelligent power flow violation adjusting method can quickly generate a power flow mode that meets N-l verification.

articleTitle: Investigation on Thermal Aging and Degradation of XLPE for High Voltage Cable Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper investigates the thermal aging and degradation of high voltage cable insulation materials. XLPE samples from a 4-year operated high voltage cable (old cable) and from a freshly produced high voltage cable (new cable) before and after thermal aging were prepared. The mechanical tensile test, DC conductivity test and AC breakdown test were performed to evaluate the mechanical and electrical properties of the samples. The test results show that the ultimate tensile strength and the elongation at break of the samples decrease significantly after thermal aging. Meanwhile, the DC conductivity of the samples increases, but the AC breakdown strength decreases, and the life time parameter of the XLPE decreases. It is found that the thermal aging can accelerate the XLPE degradation, which leads to the decrease of the mechanical properties of XLPE, and makes the molecular chain susceptible to break. Therefore, the AC breakdown strength and the overall insulation properties of the XLPE decrease.

articleTitle: Unit Commitment Based Optimal Aggregation and Control Method for Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the ever-increasing penetration of intermittent renewable energy generation in a power system, the emerging energy storage system (ESS) plays an increasingly important role in promoting the accommodation capability of fluctuating renewable energy generation, improving load profile, as well as enhancing operational security and economics. Given this background, an unit commitment based multi-objective optimization problem is first formulated for optimal aggregation and control of multiple types of ESSs, with power system operation economics and the utilization efficiency of ESSs as optimization objectives, and with operation security constraints respected. The multi-objective optimization problem is next transformed into a single-objective optimization problem by weighting different objectives. The built optimization model is non-convex and is then convexified for facilitating the solving procedure. Finally, a modified IEEE 33-bus distribution system is employed to demonstrate the proposed optimal aggregation and control method, and the Pareto front and the compromised optimal solution of the multi-objective optimization problem are obtained.

articleTitle: Integrated LVRT Technology Based on Stator-side Series Impedance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The low voltage ride-through (LVRT) technology of series impedance on the stator side of the doubly-fed wind induction generator (DFIG) can ensure the low voltage ride-through performance of the DFIG, and at the same time provide reactive power to the grid during the fault period to support the voltage. Putting impedance on the stator side during the fault can reduce the transient impact of the unit and shorten the transient transition process of the unit, but when the voltage drop is small, the input impedance will aggravate the transient impact of the unit, increase the oscillation of the flux, and affect the active and reactive power output of the unit. Based on the above research, a comprehensive LVRT technology is proposed to use the inverter feedforward compensation control when the voltage drop degree does not reach the input threshold, and when the voltage drop degree is greater than the input threshold, the inverter control is used to control the inverter and the series impedance on the stator side. The simulation results show that the proposed method can ensure the low voltage ride-through performance of the fan in the event of a fault, and at the same time, when the voltage drop degree is greater than the threshold, it can cooperate with the series impedance on the stator side to improve the fault operation ability of the unit.

articleTitle: A Method for Identifying Abnormal Risk Points in Electricity Market Prices Based on Time Series Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In view of the abnormal point situation of electricity price in the electricity market, this paper proposes an identification method of abnormal point of electricity price based on the residual component after time series decomposition combined with a variety of time series data anomaly identification methods. First, the grid electricity price data is decomposed into time series. Based on the residual components obtained from the decomposition, the Box plot method, Histogram-Based Method, Z-score method, Robust Z-score method and other methods are further used for anomaly detection and identification of abnormal data points. Afterwards, through comparative analysis of the identification results, it was found that the electricity market price abnormal risk point identification method based on time series decomposition combined with the Robust Z-score method has the best effect, far better than the traditional point-by-point identification method.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Ordered Charging Strategy for Electric Vehicle Guided by NSGA-II Algorithm Based on Real-Time State of Traffic Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) exhibit highly unpredictable travel patterns. It is imperative to guide EVs in an orderly fashion to enhance the charging experience, improve charging station efficiency, and maintain power quality in the distribution network (DN). This study introduces a multi-objective orderly charging guidance strategy based on the “Vehicle- Traffic-Station-Network” (VTSN) information interaction model. The strategy aims to achieve optimal EV charging experiences, ensure balanced utilization of charging station network resources, and minimize voltage deviation in the DN. It employs the NSGA-II algorithm to identify the optimal charging path. Through this approach, EVs can engage in systematic charging. Simulation results confirm the efficacy of the proposed method in this research.

articleTitle: Research on the Effect of Renewable Energy Reactive Output on the Voltage Support of the Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Under the promotion of the national dual carbon strategy, the grid connection technology of renewable energy generation has gradually become a research hotspot. Renewable energy power generation has intermittency and uncertainty, and connecting to the system can easily cause bus voltage fluctuations, posing new challenges to system reactive power and voltage stability. This article theoretically derives the mechanism of the reactive power output from the renewable energy machine on the voltage stability support of the grid connection points, proposes a voltage reactive power sensitivity analysis model, and further verifies the impact of the renewable energy reactive power output on the voltage stability of each grid connection point in the system and the accuracy of the model through simulation analysis of renewable energy access system examples.

articleTitle: Survey of Electric Vehicles and Charging Equipment for Fault Warning with Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the vigorous development of new energy technologies worldwide, electric vehicles and their supporting charging facilities are becoming increasingly popular. However, the spontaneous combustion accidents of electric vehicles and charging safety have attracted much attention from researchers. From the perspective of charging safety factors, this article summarizes the methods based on recent deep learning algorithms applied in charging fault early warning of electric vehicles and charging equipment. First, this article introduces the fault diagnosis process for electric vehicles and charging equipment based on deep learning algorithms. Then, we classify existing charging safety warning methods based on deep learning algorithms and compare them according to their characteristics and limits. Finally, this article looks forward to the opportunities and challenges in the follow-up research on fault warning of electric vehicles and charging equipment.

articleTitle: Collaborative Post-Disaster Fault Recovery Strategy of Main-Distribution Networks for Resilience Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Extreme disasters can cause various degrees of damages to transmission and distribution networks, disrupting the regular operation of the power system. In the event of a fault, implementing a well-planned fault recovery strategy is essential for expeditiously restoring power supply and mitigating power outage losses. With the emergence of active distribution networks and the development of smart distribution systems, internal flexible resources can restore power supply and coordinate with the transmission network for post-disaster recovery. In view of the situation where disasters cause damage to the transmission and distribution network at the same time, by simultaneously considering the fault conditions in the transmission and distribution network, a transmission and distribution coordinated post-disaster fault recovery model is established. It coordinates various resources in the transmission and distribution network, and aims at minimizing operating costs during the recovery process. It also takes into account the generating units in transmission network, fault repair sequence and controllable load response, controllable distributed power output and topological structure changes in distribution network. Finally the Analysis Target Cascading (ATC) method is adopted to solve the proposed model. Example analysis shows that the proposed model can effectively reduce outage costs and enhance the resilience of power systems.

articleTitle: A Method for Cyber Attack Threat Assessment of Electric Power Supervision and Control System Considering Its Vulnerability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Nowadays frequent cases of cyber attacks on industrial control systems, including the supervision and control of power system, have occurred around the world. Large amount of work, related with cyber security protection of power system, has been carried out, in accordance with the principle of security partition, dedicated network, network isolation and authentication. However, consideration of the system vulnerability is often lacked in threat assessment methods commonly used. This paper proposes a method to assess cyber attack threat of the supervision and control system of power system, considering its vulnerability. To be specific, typical scenarios of cyber attack are built and the corresponding threat means are identified firstly. Then, the related security protection areas are sorted out, from which the vulnerability assessment values of the system can be got. And then the threat-vulnerability correlation values are determined in consideration of the vulnerability. Based on threat-vulnerability correlation values, the threat assessment of attack scenarios is obtained. Finally, in view of overall scenarios, quantitative evaluation of cyber attack threat in substations, power plants, etc, is realized. A typical substation is analyzed as test case, to verify the effectiveness of this method.

Author Keywords: electric power supervision and control system

articleTitle: Enhancing the Efficiency of Relay Coils in Three-Coil Wireless Power Transmission Systems through Design and Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Wireless Power Transmission (WPT) systems, which eliminate the need for physical connections and enhance the convenience of power transmission, have garnered increasing attention in recent years. However, while the addition of a relay coil significantly enhances the power transmission capacity of WPT systems, it also leads to increased electromagnetic radiation. Hence, it is essential to explore the design optimization of the relay coil. In this paper, we analyze the impact of different compensation methods on the transmitting current and select the series compensation topology that results in the lowest transmitting current. Next, utilizing the inner diameter, turns, turn spacing, and position of the relay coil as variables, we employ the SPEA-II multi-objective optimization algorithm to optimize the transmitting coil current, relay coil current, and transmission efficiency. Finally, with transmission efficiency and output power as optimization objectives, we obtain the optimal relay coil compensation capacitance model for the three-coil WPT system. This paper aims to design and optimize the relay coil parameters and compensation capacitance of the three-coil WPT system with the goal of meeting low electromagnetic interference requirements while achieving high transmission efficiency.

articleTitle: Distribution Network Planning Considering the Microgrids' Flexible Capability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, a two-stage expansion model for the distribution network is established for the purpose of minimizing the planning cost of the distribution, considering networked microgrids (MGs) as flexible regulation resources. In the first stage, the planning decision is made according to the measure of constructing lines, while in the second stage, the operating cost of the distribution network is evaluated by considering MG's flexible regulation capability. Based on the DistFlow model, the expansion model can be transformed into a second-order cone programming (SOCP) problem which can be easily solved by the YALMIP toolbox and GUROBI solver used in the study. Finally, a 20-bus distribution network test system is used to test the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Improved Differential Protection Method for the Transmission Line of Photovoltaic Station
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the inherent features of the thyristors and the control strategies of the converters, the fault transient features of the photovoltaic (PV) inverters are totally different from synchronous generators. This makes the conventional current differential protection not applicable for transmission lines connected to photovoltaic station. Therefore, fault transient analysis of the photovoltaic inverters and the performance of the differential protection are carried out. It showed that the conventional differential protection has a high risk of refusing action. To cope with this problem, a phase-correction differential protection method is proposed. And it revealed the effectiveness of the new proposed method.

articleTitle: Coupling Characteristics of Active and Reactive Power in Power System with Renewable Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: A universal functional method to express the coupling characteristics of active and reactive power is proposed in this paper using the coordinated dispatch model and polynomial fitting. The coordinated dispatch model of active and reactive power, as a more accurate operation model, is introduced to calculate the active and reactive power flow in multiple scenarios to show the global feature of the power system under the uncertainty of renewable generation. The polynomial fitting analyzes the active and reactive power flow data from coordinated dispatch and extracts a universal functional form to describe the coupling characteristics of active and reactive power in the power grid, which is applicable in any network with different structures and different resource configurations. This universal function is also validated in an IEEE-39 system.

articleTitle: A Method for Identifying Weak Links in Medium Voltage Distribution Networks Based on the Value at Risk of Customer Blackout
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the improvement of end-users' requirements for continuous power supply capability, the improvement of power supply reliability level of distribution networks has also become an important research topic. This paper proposes a method for identifying weak links in medium voltage distribution networks based on the value of user blackout risk. By simulating the failures of major components such as lines and switches in the medium voltage distribution network, the risk of blackout caused by the failures is analyzed, and then weak components such as sectional branch circuits and sectional contact switches are identified, which lays the foundation for the improvement of power supply reliability of the medium voltage distribution network. Finally, the effectiveness of the method is demonstrated by an example.

articleTitle: Distribution Network Fault Recovery Method Considering Demand-Side Response Participation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The traditional recovery methods of distribution networks may have inflexible scheduling and insufficient power output, limiting the recovery effect, which calls for dispatching other resources from non-grid entities to participate in fault recovery. However, the output of these resources may be affected by external factors, or the decision of resource owners due to their own subjective reasons, which brings uncertainty to the grid restoration. Aiming at improving restoration quality and reducing uncertainty in restoration, the grid is required to assess the credibility of power resources with dispatch potential. In this paper, uncertainty is divided into objective one and subjective one. For the latter, a calculation method of user's credit value is proposed based on the evaluation of historical behavior records and the establishment of user behavior data table. Gaussian mixture model (GMM) and chance constrained programming are introduced to model the uncertainty of different power output and to describe the response capability.

articleTitle: Force Calculation and Analysis on Salvaging of Faulted Submarine Cables Considering Submarine Topography and Soil Mulch
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Salvage of submarine cable is a very important step in their troubleshooting. It is necessary to ensure the safety of the salvage and avoid secondary damage to this submarine cable. A force model is established for the salvage process of submarine cable, and it is analyzed the effects of water depth, slope, uplift, and low-lying terrain on the curvature and force of the salvaged submarine cables. At the same time, it also analyzes the impact of cable surface cover cleaning on the salvage process. Calculations indicate that, during the cable salvage, the tension of the lifting point needs to be strictly controlled when lifting, as it is the largest force bearing point for regular cables. The paper provides a control range for the angle of the cable at the lifting point, which needs to be maintained at different lifting heights to control the angle of the lifting point and always remain within this range to avoid cable bending failure. It is obtained from the simulation that, the length of cable bending failure increases with the increase of routing slope, and as the routing slope increases, the water depth at the location where the submarine cable leaves the site decreases, resulting in a decrease in the maximum effective tension. Meanwhile, it can be concluded that when the speed ratio is large, the influence of seabed uplift height can be ignored, and when the cable salvage passes through low-lying areas, the extreme curvature values are distributed at the front end of the cable and at the turning points from the downhill section to the horizontal seabed. In addition, calculations have shown that during the salvage process, the state of the cover has a small impact on the tension of the submarine cable, but a significant impact on the curvature of the submarine cable. In the incomplete cleaning section of the cover, the minimum bending radius of the submarine cable may exceed the limit that the submarine cable can carry, causing damage to the submarine cable.

articleTitle: Characterization of Lorentz Force Distribution in Electromagnetic Repulsion Mechanism of Multiple Parallel Circuit Breakers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to meet the requirements of parallel circuit breaker opening rapidity and synchronization, a new structure of electromagnetic repulsion mechanism (EMRM) is proposed in this paper. A three-dimensional transient flexible body model of the mechanism was built in COMSOL. Simulation results show that the EMRM can reach the rated opening distance of 20mm in 4.86ms, and the maximum stress during the motion is 246MPa. There is vibration in the motion process due to the uneven distribution of Lorentz force, and the vibration is periodic. The maximum stress is related to the vibration characteristics. Through theoretical derivation and simulation analysis, an analytical formula describing the relationship between the Lorentz force distribution and structural parameters is proposed in this paper. Error between the formula results and the simulation results is less than 4.5%. The analytical formula can be applied to parameter design.

articleTitle: Small-signal Stability Analysis of Offshore Wind Farm Integrated Grid-forming VSC-HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: VSC-HVDC (voltage source converter based on high voltage direct current) technology has become the mainstream trend for offshore wind power grid integration. At present, VSC-HVDC is mainly based on grid-following type control. As the proportion of synchronous machines in the grid decreases and the strength of the grid decreases, the system with grid-following type control is prone to small disturbance instability. However, the grid-forming control can solve the small disturbance instability problems such as low inertia. VSG (Virtual Synchronous Generator) control is a common type of the grid-forming control that is utilized in the rectifier side of the HVDC transmission system in this paper. On this basis, a dynamic mathematical model of a wind farm connected to the grid through the VSC-HVDC system is established. After that, small-signal modeling of the whole system model is carried out, and the influence of VSG control parameters on system stability is analyzed by eigenvalue analysis method.

articleTitle: Shafting dynamic Analysis of the PMSG-based Wind-driven System Considering Virtual Inertia Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The majority of PMSG-based wind systems currently use grid-following control, which depends on a phase-locked loop (PLL) for grid connection. However, it leads to a lack of inertia support in the system. To tackle this issue, the implementation of virtual inertia control (VIC) is essential for improvement. However, it may introduce potential instability to the shaft system, which remains a relatively unexplored area. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of a grid-connected wind farm (WF) system based on PMSG. It confirms the necessity of using a full-order model for studying system stability through a comparison with a reduced-order model. Furthermore, the transfer function of electromagnetic torque and speed difference in the PMSG is derived, taking VIC into account. The detrimental effect of VIC on shaft system damping is illustrated using the damping torque method. Subsequently, a comprehensive modal analysis is performed to assess how VIC parameters affect the primary oscillation modes in three common control scenarios. Lastly, the theoretical analysis is validated through SIMULINK simulation verification.

articleTitle: Triple-Vector Model Predictive Control for High-Voltage Islanded Microgrids Based on Two-Step Accelerated Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, triple-vector model predictive control(MPC) based on adaptive virtual impedance is proposed for high-voltage islanded microgrids, and the limitations arising from control delay are alleviated by a two-step accelerated prediction method, which improves the control accuracy and reduces the amount of real-time computation at the same time. The suppression effects of circulating current and harmonic of different vector MPC are compared under two typical operating conditions, namely, load suddenly change and load fluctuations, to verify the superiority of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Optimal Dispatch of the Electricity-Heat Integrated Energy System Under Epistemic Uncertainty of Thermal-Inertia Based Flexible Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The flexibility of buildings' thermal loads has been widely recognized as the resource in the operation of the heat and electricity integrated energy system(HE- IES). Recently, the data-driven method has proven to be an effective means of measuring the flexibility in buildings' thermal loads. Nevertheless, measurement errors can hardly be avoided. This paper proposes an optimal dispatch model of the HE-IES that is compatible with the measurement errors of demand flexibility in buildings' thermal loads. First, the measurement errors are modeled as epistemic uncertainty related to the demand response and the multiple error sources are combined through the D-S evidence theory. Then, the representative scenarios are selected and reduced by the LHS and fuzzy clustering method. Last, the scenario-based stochastic scheduling model is developed to dispatch the HE- IES. The results demonstrate that considering the epistemic uncertainties of the thermal load demand response is essential for reducing the wind power curtailments and improving the flexibility of HE-IES.

Author Keywords: heat and electricity integrated energy system

articleTitle: A Flexible Model for Collaborative Charging Scheduling of Electric Vehicles and Hydrogen Vehicles in Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper presents a collaborative charging scheduling model for electrical vehicle (EV) and hydrogen vehicle (HV) in distribution network. First, the optimization constraints for EV-HV considering personal charging habits of each vehicle are established. Then, the optimization model is developed to minimize the total energy cost on load-side and the wind curtailment cost. It is modelled as a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming problem that solved by MATLAB/ Gurobi solver. Simulation results are given to validate the effectiveness of the proposed optimization model in flexible scheduling of EVs, HVs, and electrolyzer. The proposed strategy can minimize distribution network cost.

articleTitle: Scheduling Optimization Method for Charging Piles in Electric Vehicle Charging Stations Based on Mixed Integer Linear Programming
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: For electric vehicles (EV s) choosing the same target charging station, appropriate guidance for them to choose the appropriate charging pile for charging will help reduce the charging waiting time of EV users and increase the utilization rate of charging piles. In this context, a scheduling optimization method for charging piles in EV charging stations is based on Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP). Firstly, the arrival time and charging demand of EV s choosing the same target charging station during the same scheduling optimization period, time are collected; Secondly, a scheduling optimization method is constructed with the goal of minimizing the charging waiting time of EV users and maximizing the utilization rate of charging piles, in which the non-linear constraints are transformed into linear constraints by using the method of MILP; Finally, the validity and feasibility of the proposed scheduling optimization method are verified through practical examples to illustrate the basic features of the proposed method. The results of the analyses show that the proposed method can not only save the time cost of EV users waiting for charging, but also effectively take into account the utilization rate of charging piles.

articleTitle: Hybrid Storage Capacity Configuration Based on SG Filter and VMD
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Focusing on the photovoltaic (PV) power output fluctuation, a hybrid energy storage system (HESS) capacity configuration method is put forward based on SG filter and variational mode decomposition (VMD). The PV grid-connected power and HESS power are obtained by SG filter. The high and low frequency components in HESS are extracted by VMD and Hilbert transform, the power of flywheel energy storage (FES) and lithium iron phosphate (LRP) are obtained by reconstructing them. Finally, the HESS capacity configuration model is established based on life cycle cost(LCC), and different energy storage capacity allocation strategies are adopted. The effectiveness and economy of the proposed method are verified by actual data simulation.

articleTitle: Research on High-Frequency Spatiotemporal Electrical Carbon Intensity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The research on electricity carbon emission intensity has evolved towards greater precision, finer regional granularity, and increased timeliness. This paper introduced a theory of coupled analysis between power flow and carbon flow and pre-sented a method for calculating electricity carbon intensity across various time and space dimensions. Utilizing the constructed “Electricity Carbon One Graph” system, this research acquired spatiotemporal carbon intensity values for a provincial power grid in southwestern China. By comparing carbon emission amounts calculated with different carbon factors based on electricity generation and consumption, this study emphasized the necessity of researching and applying spatiotemporal grid carbon emission factors. It was evident that using spatiotemporal grid carbon emission factors has been the future trend in carbon emission accounting.

articleTitle: Multi-Energy Coupling Characteristic Analysis and Modeling Technology of Integrated Energy System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Integrated energy system is an important path for the development of energy revolution and will play an important role in the future energy system; it is of great significance to carry out the research on the multi-energy coupling characterization and modeling technology of integrated energy system. The paper summarizes the research results of research institutes and scholars in various countries around the world on the multi-energy coupling characterization and modeling technology of integrated energy system in recent years. On this basis, the current status of the research and the future research direction are analyzed.

articleTitle: Dynamic Equivalent Model of Active Distribution Network Using Hierarchical Double Deep Q Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The modeling of active distribution networks (ADNs) has become more and more difficult due to the increasing distributed generation from renewable energy sources and electric vehicle (EV) loads. To address the accuracy problem in simulating power flow in ADN, an equivalent ADN model, including equivalent wind turbine, asynchronous motor, EV loads, and daily loads with internal identification of EV loads, is proposed. Regarding parameter identification, a hierarchical double deep Q network (HDDQN) is presented by improving sample selection and behavioral value function evaluation in deep reinforcement learning through the dyadic network, prioritized empirical replay, and Huber loss function strategies. In HDDQN, the first layer establishes an equivalent model, the second layer determines the model weights, and the third layer determines the weights of EVs. The dynamics of the original ADN are tracked in layers with high accuracy. The simulation results show that the equivalent model obtained by the HDDQN is more accurate and applicable than those obtained by the traditional DDQN and DQN.

articleTitle: Optimal Integration of Wind+BESS and Solar+BESS Hybrid Microgrids Based on Cooperative Transactions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In response to explicit directives mandating the incorporation of battery energy storage systems (BESS) in new energy power generation, this paper introduces the integration of wind+BESS and solar+BESS hybrid microgrids based on cooperative transactions, forming multiple regulation and response strategies to encourage renewable energy consumption. With the peer-to-peer (P2P) trading technique, the proposed approach facilitates collaborative alliances between wind+BESS and solar+BESS hybrid microgrids during periods of power surplus or shortage. The objective of these alliances is to circumvent the sale of power at suboptimal prices and the purchase of power at inflated rates from the distribution system. A cooperative trading approach between hybrid microgrids is presented and the cooperative surplus is calculated based on the Shapley value method. With case studies, the efficacy of cooperative transactions in optimizing the integration of wind+BESS and solar+BESS hybrid microgrids is further validated. The analysis shows that cooperative transactions improve the overall benefits of wind+BESS and solar+BESS hybrid microgrid alliances, reduce the burden of distribution network, and foster the fair sharing of BESS costs among microgrids.

articleTitle: Investigation of Artificial Intelligence Vulnerability in Smart Grids: A Case from Solar Energy Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources, such as solar photovoltaic (PV), into the power grid has heightened the significance of accurate solar radiation forecasting for grid stability and energy management. Deep learning-based models have shown promise in improving the accuracy of solar radiation forecasts, but their vulnerability to adversarial attacks remains a largely unexplored area of research. This paper investigates the vulnerability of deep learning-based solar radiation forecasting models to imperceptible adversarial attacks, focusing on false data injection within a restricted input data region. Leveraging Bayesian optimization, we strategically craft subtle perturbations in the input data to target the local optimum with the largest error from the true value while ensuring the perturbations remain imperceptible. Our experiments validate the potency of these attacks, highlighting the critical need for improved model robustness and security in applications vital to energy infrastructure. We explore the transferability of these attacks across different models and rigorously evaluate their resilience under various environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Optimization of Renewable Energy Consumption Responsibility Weighting Apportionment Model Considering Equity Principle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Currently, the construction of the electricity spot market and the renewable energy consumption responsibility weighting system are going hand in hand. In order to ensure the smooth landing of the consumption weighting system, this study focuses on the background of the current power market construction, in-depth analysis of the system to implement the specific process of renewable energy consumption responsibility weighting; secondly, this paper studies the coupling relationship between the power market and the renewable energy consumption market, and at the same time, joins the consideration of the green certificate and the green power trading, establishes the renewable energy consumption responsibility weighting model considering the principle of fairness of allocation considering the principle of fairness of renewable energy consumption responsibility weighting model optimization considering the principle of fairness of renewable energy consumption responsibility weighting. Renewable energy consumption responsibility weighting power trading strategy; Finally, through empirical analysis, we confirm the effectiveness of the model established in this paper on the evaluation of trading decision-making, to provide support for the relevant power generation enterprises to make auxiliary decisions.

articleTitle: Probability Assessment of Open-Loop Mode Resonance in Grid-Connected Wind Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Since wind power generation has characteristics such as randomness, the power system stability also exhibits certain probabilistic characteristics due to the integration of wind power into the grid. Therefore, it is also extremely important to study the probabilistic assessment of closed-loop system stability that considering the randomness of wind generator output. This paper first establishes a closed-loop interconnection model with the wind turbine represented by the permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) as the “feedback subsystem” and the remainder of the power system as the “feedforward sub-system”; analyzes the open-loop and closed-loop interactions between the two subsystems. At the same time, open-loop mode resonance is introduced to derive the criteria for system oscillation instability in closed-loop conditions. Then, the regional wind generator distribution characteristics and wind turbine output characteristics are numerically analyzed with the help of Weibull distribution and the wind speed power curve of the wind turbine. Characterize and obtain the probabilistic model of wind power output power; through the above relationship, the probability of subsynchronous resonance (SSR) in the power system caused by grid-connected wind power is finally evaluated, and the reliability and applicability of the evaluation results are verified with the help of cases and time domain simulations. Finally, based on the evaluation results, reasonable plans and suggestions are put forward for power system oscillation prediction and wind farm turbine operation.

articleTitle: Analysis and Comparison of Sub/Super-Synchronous Oscillation Source Location Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Accurate location of the source of sub/super-synchronous oscillation (SSO) based on online measurements is critical to effective emergency control when SSO occurs. The impedance method and the transient energy flow (TEF) method are two common methods for SSO source location in the literature. The paper first analyzes the theoretical foundation of the two methods based on the passivity theory, and elucidates the rationality of both methods. Then, the differences between the two methods in damping evaluation are studied. The impedance method takes the sum of super-synchronous power and sub-synchronous power as the rate of energy dissipation, while in the TEF method the the rate of energy dissipation is proportional to the difference between the two. Finally, the efficacy of the two methods for forced oscillation source location is tested through the utilization of eletromagnetic transient simulations. The results demonstrate that the TEF method achieves relatively high accuracy, while both methods still require further improvement.

articleTitle: A Two-Stage Robust Optimization Method for Microgrids Considering Wind Power and Photovoltaic Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Microgrids play an important role in managing the increasingly developed renewable energy sources. As the primary renewable energy sources, the outputs of wind power and photovoltaics show a lot of uncertainties influenced by meteorological factors. These uncertainties can have adverse effects on the economic efficiency of microgrid operations. We have established a two-stage robust optimization model tailored for microgrids considering wind power and photovoltaics to address this issue. In this model, a box uncertainty set of wind power and PVs that can be quantitatively adjusted is proposed. The two-stage model is a Mixed-Integer Programming (MIP) model, which belongs to an NP-hard problem. Therefore, we choose the Columns and Constraints Generation Algorithm (C&CG) to solve the model. Finally, the practical validity of our model is demonstrated through the results obtained from its application to the modified IEEE-39 bus system.

articleTitle: Distributed Settlement Mechanism Design for Carbon Market Based on Blockchain-Enabled Edge Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The trend towards decarbonizing the power industry is accelerating due to the environmental crisis. The development of carbon markets as one of the solutions for decarbonization has received more attention. The current annual carbon market widely adopts the method of calculating carbon emission according to the average carbon emission factor. The roughness of the average carbon emission factor and the long carbon market cycle lead to some problems in carbon market settlement in the carbon market at present. In this paper, we propose a blockchain-based scheme for real-time local settlement of carbon emissions. The system obtains accurate carbon emission information of generating units calculated from real-time power information through IoT devices. The digital carbon asset stored in the unit's account are written off in a short period through a blockchain smart contract. The above scheme eases the communication burden caused by accurate carbon emission records. With hardware devices, we verify the feasibility and operability of the scheme.

articleTitle: Research on Optimal Scheduling Method for Electric Vehicles Participating in Load Aggregators Based on Demand-Side Response
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the number of electric vehicles gradually increases, their overall charging load will increase accordingly, and the charging time coincides with the daily electricity intensive time, leading to the peak load being breached and the peak-valley gap increasing. Therefore, how to guide the orderly charging of electric vehicles becomes an urgent problem to be solved. This paper proposes to integrate electric vehicles (EV) with load aggregators for demand response. Firstly, by analysing EV travel data, establish a probability distribution model of EV travel and adopt Monte Carlo random sampling method to generate EV charging in a disorderly state. Secondly, combining with the short-term base load prediction model of EV load aggregators, dynamically adjust the tariff segmentation interval to optimise a price segment that better fits the basic load forecasting models. Finally, by setting multiple optimisation objectives, an adaptive genetic algorithm with elite operators is used to solve for the vehicle charging state. The simulation analysis shows that the proposed multi-period dynamic tariff strategy can reduce the difference between peak and valley loads and mitigate the overall charging cost by simulation analysis.

articleTitle: An Energy and Reserve Combined Dispatch Model for Wind-Thermal-Pumped Storage Complementary Generation System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The output of wind power has the characteristics of low predictability and instability, which brings challenges to the security operation of power system. The power system needs to configure higher reserve to solve this problem. Increased reserve levels and operational constraints may force the wind turbine to operate below its maximum available power. The paper shows that the pumped storage system can not only store energy, but also provide reserve, so as to reduce the abandoned wind in the power system. This paper presents a dispatch model for wind-thermal-pumped storage complementary generation system, in which the spinning reserve is provided by pumped storage to improve the wind power consumption level of power system. Based on the numerical simulation of the IEEE 39-bus test system, the improvement of wind power consumption level of power system by pumped storage system is simulated and analyzed.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Cluster Forecasting Based on Spatial Correlation-Informed Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the uncertainty and volatility of photovoltaic (PV) power generation systems, accurately forecasting the PV power output has become one of the key challenges for improving system efficiency. Unlike single-site PV forecasting, PV cluster forecasting not only enhances the precision and dependability of energy management but also contributes to power balance in the provincial power grid. While deep neural networks have emerged as the mainstream method for PV forecasting, they remain constrained to single-site forecasting. In this study, a short-term PV forecasting model is developed by combining two neural networks, utilizing numerical weather prediction (NWP) as the foundation, to accurately forecast PV output for each site. Additionally, a fully connected layer is employed to analyze the spatial correlation among sites within the PV cluster, thereby adjusting the forecasted values of each individual site and establishing a more precise power generation forecasting model. Comparative experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, demonstrating an error reduction of nearly 1% compared to single-site forecasting and showcasing improved performance in PV cluster power generation forecasting.

articleTitle: Probability Based Vulnerability Analysis of UHVDC Supported Filter Circuit Under Earthquakes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The direct current (DC) supported filter circuit is a critical electrical circuit in an ultra-high-voltage (UHV) substation, but its unique structural properties render it susceptible to damage during significant earthquakes. In order to investigate the seismic vulnerability of a supported filter circuit, numerical modelling was performed on an 800kV supported filter circuit. Modal analysis and seismic response time history computation on the circuit were performed using the numerical model. In addition, a seismic vulnerability analysis of the circuit was conducted. The results show that the first three order frequencies of the model were calculated as 1.354 Hz, 1.471 Hz and 1.621 Hz. Coupling has a beneficial effect on the seismic performance of pillar equipment and LV equipment capacitor C3 and reactor L3. However, the coupling amplifies the root stress responses of support insulators of capacitor C2 and reactor L2, and the stress response of transformer T1 in the LV region. The order of vulnerability of equipment in the circuit system is: the underlying insulator of the DC filter Cl> electronic transformer T2> pillar insulator PI1-4> disconnector Q1-3.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of Regional Integrated Energy System Based on Stackelberg Game
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Regional integrated energy system (RIES) is an effective way to address the challenges of low energy utilization efficiency and difficulties associated with renewable energy consumption. Firstly, the RIES including wind power, photovoltaic, gas turbines, waste heat boilers and gas boilers was modeled and analyzed. Considering the adjustable ability of load in RIES, a demand response model for the load was established. Secondly, with the park operator as the leader, and the energy suppliers and load aggregators as followers, an optimal operation model for RIES was established based on Stackelberg game. This model aimed to maximize the benefits of all parties by optimizing the pricing strategy, output plan, and user demand. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method was verified by a practical example.

articleTitle: An Improved Wind Power Forecasting Framework Based on Seasonal Feature Selection and Temporal Convolutional Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Large-scale wind power forecasting with high accuracy and reliability can proficiently decrease the unfavorable impacts of wind power uncertainty. However, the existing wind power forecasting performances are greatly influenced by intermittent changes of environmental and meteorological factors, which brings much challenge for wind power integration. To solve the above problem, based on a dynamic selection of seasonal features, an improved Seasonal Feature Selection Temporal Convolutional Network (SFS-TCN) model is proposed to forecast ultra-short-term wind power forecasting in this paper. Firstly, to simplify the model input and improve the forecasting efficiency, the correlations between multiple environmental variables and wind power under different seasonal characteristics are studied respectively. Secondly, a wind power forecasting framework based on temporal convolutional network is developed. The seasonal characteristic variables are selected as model input to forecast the wind power 10 minutes ahead. Finally, the forecasting accuracy of the proposed method is compared with the original TCN model by using the actual dataset of a case wind farm. The case study results show that compared to the original TCN model, the proposed improved SFS-TCN model has better forecasting performance, of which the forecasting errors decrease by 16.7% (MSE), 22.5% (MAE) and 11.5% (RMSE) respectively. At the same time, compared to benchmark models including multi-layer perceptron (MLP) and long short-term memory (LSTM), forecasting errors of the proposed model decrease by 28.6%, 16.7% (MSE); 39.2%, 36.7% (MAE) and 20.7%, 13.8% (RMSE) respectively.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation Method for Aging Detection of 10 kV Composite Insulator Based on Microwave Transmission Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Composite insulators are susceptible to aging of the umbrella skirt and sheath during operation, which can affect their insulation performance and mechanical strength. In this paper, a microwave aging detection method for composite insulators is proposed based on the principle of microwave transmission. The study focuses on 10 kV composite insulators, and a numerical simulation model for microwave aging detection of composite insulators is established. By using a pyramidal horn antenna instead of the traditional rectangular waveguide, the method enables overall aging detection of composite insulators without the need to move the antenna, simplifying the detection process and improving efficiency. The results show that the proposed method has low accuracy requirements for the lifting distance, making it less susceptible to accidental errors caused by fluctuations in the lifting distance. The horn antenna has a wide frequency band, with the low-frequency band being suitable for predicting the aging life of composite insulators, and the high-frequency band being suitable for rapid identification of severely aged composite insulators. The research findings are of great significance in the field of aging detection and assessment of composite insulators.

articleTitle: Application Research of Blockchain Technology in Virtual Power Plant Dispatching and Trading
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Virtual power plant collects all kinds of decentralized and callable power and load, and uses digital means to do unified scheduling and management through virtual power plant. Virtual power plants have a huge variety of resources. This paper proposes to use blockchain technology to support the scheduling and trading of virtual power plants. The introduction of blockchain technology into the scheduling and trading of virtual power plants can not only ensure the security of virtual power plant data information, but also reduce the credit cost of virtual power plant trading center, so that virtual power plants can obtain a greater degree of security, so as to solve the current difficulties and challenges faced by virtual power plants.

articleTitle: Coordinated Restoration of Generators and Load for the High Renewable Energy Penetrated Power System with Frequency Regulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The frequency dynamic of converter-based renewable energy generators is much different from the traditional inertia-based generators in the restoration process of the high renewable energy penetrated power system (HREPPS). Considering the frequency regulation capability (FRC) of renewable generators, this paper proposes an optimization method of coordinating generator restoration with load restoration in the network configuration stage of the HREPPS. Firstly, the unified transfer function structure is introduced to analyze the FRC of restored HREPPSs. Then a quantification model of the maximum pick-up load is proposed considering the frequency dynamic performance of restored HREPPSs. Secondly, the optimization model with FRC is proposed to coordinated restore all generators and more load in the shortest time. Finally, results on a modified IEEE 39-bus system are studied to verify the applicability of the proposed FRC model and coordinated restoration method for the HREPPS. This work can serve as an important guidance for operators to develop restoration strategies for the blackout HREPPS.

Author Keywords: high renewable energy penetrated power system

articleTitle: Power Fluctuations Smoothing Control Based on PCH Model of D-PMSG Wind Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To effectively mitigate power fluctuations in a wind power system, the self-capability of the Direct-drive Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (D-PMSG) is harnessed for power smoothing support through the Port-Controlled Hamiltonian (PCH) model. By combining rotor speed control and PCH passive control, the PMSG can quickly track the reference speed and DC-link voltage control can support power smoothly within the rated operating range of the wind turbine. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, a simulation was conducted by comparing it with traditional maximum power point tracking control.

articleTitle: Fast Access of Power IoT Devices Based on Deep Message Parsing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the development of the Internet of Things (IoT), a large number of Power Internet of Things are being integrated into power systems. The Internet of Things platform is used to monitor and manage the operation of these IoT devices. However, there are many types and numbers of Internet of Things devices, and many device access protocols are private, which are quite different from the standard protocols provided by the Internet of Things platform. Consequently, it is difficult to directly access these IoT devices on the Power Internet of Things platform. It is urgent to study the plug-and-play of Power IoT devices due to the huge cost of manual access. This paper proposes a fast access methodology for Power IoT devices based on deep message parsing, in which a new IoT device is automatically connected to the gateway by matching its static and dynamic feature vector with the existing one in the feature library. This realizes a fast integration of massive IoT devices through the device's automatic registration and data transmission using the smart gateway.

articleTitle: Hybrid Neural Network based Power Generation Prediction of Photovoltaic Farms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The large-scale penetration of intermittent photovoltaic power generation has brought direct challenges to the safe and reliable operation of the power systems. Accurate prediction of photovoltaic power generation can reduce the negative impact of generation fluctuations and support optimal power system planning and energy dispatch. This paper presented a hybrid neural network based photovoltaic power generation prediction solution. Firstly, the data preprocessing is carried out for prediction, e.g., wavelet denoising for power data and polynomial feature engineering for weather factors. Then, the long short-term memory network (LSTM) and convolutional neural network (CNN) models are adopted and the SE channel attention mechanism is integrated into the convolutional neural network. The proposed solution can achieve complementary advantages and presents the divergence-fusion structure CNN-SE-LSTM hybrid model. The proposed solution is assessed through simulation experiments and the numerical result confirms the effectiveness of the feature engineering and the superiority of the hybrid model in photovoltaic power prediction.

articleTitle: Research on a Novel Multi-port Hybrid Circuit Breaker
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: A novel hybrid circuit breaker topology is proposed to address the shortcomings of hybrid circuit breakers, which are costly and difficult to be applied to multi-port grids. This topology adopts the structure of multi-branch multiplexed transfer circuit's combined with LC commutation, which reduces the number of power electronic components in hybrid circuit breakers in multi-port grids and greatly reduces the cost of circuit breakers. With respect to the topology of this novel multi-branch multiplexed circuit breaker, its working principle is introduced, a simulation model is established, and the effects of different transfer branch structures on the opening performance of the circuit breaker are analyzed. The results show that the structure combining anti-parallel thyristor and LC commutator has better breaking performance and lower cost.

articleTitle: Research on Frequency Characteristics and Analysis Methods of New Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: For the last few years, as the country puts forward and promotes the “double carbon” strategy, the proportion of new energy power generation in the power grid has been increasing, a large number of traditional thermal power units have been replaced, the system inertia has been reduced, and the frequency regulation ability has been weakened. On the other hand, with the rapid development of UHV DC transmission projects, the scale of asynchronous interconnection of power grids is increasing, and the frequency characteristics of power grids after faults or disturbances are becoming more and more complex. In this paper, aiming at the problems of large amount of calculation and difficult modeling in the frequency analysis of new energy high-proportion power grids by traditional frequency analysis methods, the frequency characteristics of new energy high-proportion power grids are studied, and the method of using deep learning network to predict the frequency characteristics of new energy high-proportion power grids is explored. Finally, a case study is carried out in the East China Power Grid model, which verifies that the proposed method has high accuracy and adaptability.

articleTitle: Statistical Characteristics and Non-Gaussianity of Grid Frequency Based on Measured Data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The grid frequency is a crucial factor in ensuring the stable operation of the power system and, therefore, must be strictly maintained close to the nominal frequency. With the integration of renewable energy generation into the grid, the impact of more frequent power variations on power quality intensifies. In this context, studying the statistical properties of frequency holds significant guiding importance. In this paper, we gathered real-time grid operation data from SML devices deployed nationwide. We analyzed the mean, variance, and other operational indices for the 24-hour frequency data of each location on the same day. Furthermore, we calculated the autocorrelation of the frequency data and identified the implied trading interval of the electricity market. We also investigated the non-Gaussianity of the frequency probability distribution in China's power grid. Our findings indicate that primary frequency control, secondary frequency control, and load power all influence the formation of the bimodal distribution, a conclusion substantiated through simulation experiments. The results of this study can provide guidance for controlling and researching applications based on grid frequency.

articleTitle: An Integrated Sensitivity Calculation Method for Cross Voltage Levels of Unbalanced Medium- and Low-voltage Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Voltage-power sensitivity reflects the relationship between the voltage and load power at each node of the grid, and is one of the important indicators for voltage control in the distribution network. In order to effectively predict the variation of grid node voltages and develop corresponding voltage control strategies, this paper proposes an integrated sensitivity calculation method for cross voltage levels of unbalanced medium- and low-voltage distribution network (MV-LV distribution network). Firstly, the equivalent model of the transformer under Dynll wiring is analyzed. Secondly, the correlation between voltage, current, and power on the primary and secondary sides of the transformer is established and quantitatively analyzed. Thirdly, the integrated sensitivity calculation method of MV-LV distribution network is derived based on the correlation relations. This method allows for the calculation of inter-voltage and inter-phase sensitivities for MV-LV distribution network. Finally, the Dynll transformer is selected to carry out the case study to analyze the propagation mechanism of power quality and inter-phase power propagation mechanism in the MV-LV distribution network.

articleTitle: Communication Restoration and Fault Location in Distribution System by UAVs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The orderly and rapid restoration of the distribution system after disasters relies on the accuracy and reliability of fault identification, while disasters often damage communication links resulting in failure to report fault information in a timely manner. This paper proposes a two-stage communication restoration and fault location strategy, and adopts a method to construct a wireless emergency communication link between the remote fault indicator (RFI) and the distribution operating center to realize the communication restoration and real-time transmission of current information by using the unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) emergency communication in the first stage. Then, the fault location method according to the fault information of the RFIs is developed and takes into account the RFIs failures and malfunction in the second stage. The proposed method is verified the accuracy and validity by applying it to the IEEE 33-node distribution system.

articleTitle: Information Fusion Model Based Improved Multi-Scale Convolutional Neural Network for Fault Diagnosis in EV V2G Charging Pile
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the rapid proliferation of electric vehicles, the demand for charging infrastructure is surging. Consequently, it becomes imperative to address the issue of maintenance for charging pile faults. To harness the multi-scale characteristic present in fault signals more effectively, this paper proposed an information fusion diagnosis model based on an improved multi-scale convolutional neural network for the automated diagnosis of switch tubes open-circuit in charging piles. The approach conducts feature extraction at different scales on the fusion information from the original fault signals through a parallel branching structure. Furthermore, a channel attention mechanism is incorporated in the final layer of the network branch. This mechanism gives precedence to different channel features, dynamically assigning weights to the features obtained from distinct filters. This enhances fault-related features, suppresses ineffectual ones, and subsequently elevates the model's performance. Ultimately, the different scale features acquired from each network branch are merged and subjected to classification and recognition using a Softmax classifier. Simulation results underscore the effectiveness of the proposed method in diagnosing switch tube open-circuit faults in the charging pile.

articleTitle: A Novel Two-level Multi-dimensional Operating Evaluation System for Building Integrated Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Building integrated energy system (BIES) is an important type of multi-energy complementary energy supply system. Following the relevant guidelines for post-evaluation in the power industry, BIES also requires detailed evaluation during operation to ensure it operates in an economical, reliable, and energy-efficient manner. However, existing standards lack regulations on the operation evaluation of BIES, and most literature evaluates BIES based on design conditions and indicators, which cannot meet the need for accurate and timely evaluation of BIES operation under complex and variable operating conditions. Firstly, a two-level operation evaluation system that covers changes in different seasonal and operating state effects was proposed, which can accurately evaluate BIES operation under different conditions. Subsequently, a multidimensional evaluation system was demonstrated and a combination method for the inner and outer weights of the twolevel operation evaluation system was proposed. Finally, a certain BIES application was taken as the research object to calculate the inner and outer weights by analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and analytic network process (ANP), respectively. The final evaluation score was obtained by the combination method.

articleTitle: Analysis of Voltage Transformer Failure Mechanism and Prevention Measures Based on ATP-EMTP
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Targeting potential transformer (PT) analysis of faults and corresponding principles. This article first analyzes voltage transformer fault cases of different voltage levels and analyzes the fault characteristics of PT. Then it mainly focuses on the PT ferromagnetic resonance overvoltage and introduces the fault mechanism of PT. On this basis, an overvoltage model containing PT-type automated terminals was established and its influencing factors were analyzed. Finally, solutions and prevention measures for different types of PT faults were proposed, which will serve as a basis for future PT protection work has laid a certain foundation.

articleTitle: Research on Power Supply Strategy of DC Microgrid with Diesel Rectifier Generator and Hybrid Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Aiming at the shortcomings of power supply continuity and reliability of off-grid power systems such as remote areas, islands and offshore drilling platforms, this paper proposes a multi-energy complementary power supply strategy based on DC grid for parallel connection of diesel rectifier generator and hybrid energy storage system, so as to make the power distribution in the power supply system reasonable and DC bus voltage stable under different operating conditions. Build Matlab/Simulink simulation model to verify the power supply strategy.
